title: Agent-pool 5-min idle reaper orphans busy-but-quiet subagents (msSinceLastMsg eviction)
description:
ROOT CAUSE of the recurring 'orphaned subagent' bug, finally pinned. admin-shim/lib/agent-pool.ts:66: IDLE_EVICT_MS = (SHIM_POOL_IDLE_SEC ?? 300)*1000. The pool eviction loop (line ~808: now - w.lastUsedAt > IDLE_EVICT_MS) evicts any session idle 5 minutes, killing its CLI subprocess. Confirmed: every orphaned subagent exited 'code=0 signal=null' with msSinceLastMsg ~325-329s — right at the 300s ceiling. Two subagents dispatched together died 'at the same time' because the eviction sweep reaped them on the same pass.

FATAL FLAW: idle is measured by LAST MESSAGE TIME, but a subagent doing a long QUIET task (gradle build, APK assembly, deep reasoning, a slow foreground tool call) emits no wire messages for minutes — so the pool mistakes 'busy but quiet' for 'abandoned' and evicts it MID-WORK, orphaning everything not yet committed/PR'd. This is deterministic, not flaky. It's the same timeout family as the turn-timeout/requires_approval beads but a distinct mechanism (subprocess idle-evict, not turn stream timeout).

IMMEDIATE MITIGATION (applied): raise SHIM_POOL_IDLE_SEC (e.g. 1800).

REAL FIX: the pool must NOT evict a session that has an ACTIVE/RUNNING task or in-flight tool call. Track liveness by 'has in-flight work' (running run/turn, active background task, pending tool) — not just lastUsedAt/last message. Bump lastUsedAt on ANY activity including tool execution and background-task progress, or exempt sessions with a non-terminal run from eviction entirely. Only evict truly-idle (no active work AND no messages for the window) sessions.

ACCEPTANCE: a subagent running a >5min quiet task (e.g. a gradle build) is NOT evicted and its work completes/PRs. Verify with a deliberate long-quiet dispatch.

RELATED: lcp-00z7 (async tool execution decoupled from turn), requires_approval/lcp-gukg, background-agent lifecycle research, the orphan-and-rescue tax noted across the 73o2h/pbnxa/active-bar work.

title: CRITICAL: rig pushes unreviewed/broken code directly to origin/main — no PR, no CI gate
description:
## What happened (2026-06-02)
After enabling vibesync for self-dispatch, the rig ran three self-fix beads (lcp-kamu, lcp-mj0h, lcp-lxgm) autonomously. Instead of opening PRs (as the awbf.1 run did), the coder/PM agents COMMITTED DIRECTLY TO main AND PUSHED to origin/main with NO review and NO CI gate:
- df99749 (lcp-kamu) — pushed to origin/main, and it DOES NOT TYPECHECK: boot.ts(363/368) reads packDir/storageDir off a routing type that has no such fields; DoltHubProvisioningService(457) wrong arg count. It will crash/misbehave if deployed.
- 9615929 (lcp-mj0h) — pushed to origin/main, unreviewed.
- 857c397 (lcp-lxgm) — committed to a local branch (not pushed); its log-hygiene change appeared ineffective (mirror stack-trace spam continued).

Production survived ONLY because the running service hadn't restarted onto the bad code. A routine 'restart to deploy' would have taken down the rig with non-compiling main.

## Why this is P0
The rig can self-modify and push broken code straight to the mainline of its OWN orchestration service, bypassing the review gate that makes the dispatch loop safe. This is the single most dangerous rig behavior — it can break itself (and the deploy) with no human or CI checkpoint. The awbf.1 run opened a PR; these did not — so the behavior is INCONSISTENT and untrustworthy.

## Required fixes
1. The rig must ALWAYS open a PR on a feature branch — NEVER commit to main, NEVER push to main directly. Enforce in the coder/PM role instructions AND structurally (the role agent's git context should not have push-to-main capability; protect main branch on the remote).
2. A CI gate (typecheck + build + tests) must pass before any rig PR can merge. A coder PR that does not typecheck must be blocked.
3. The merge step must be a separate, gated action (human or a reviewer-agent that actually runs the build), not auto-push.
4. Branch protection on origin/main (require PR + passing checks) as a backstop.

## Immediate remediation (separate, doing now)
- origin/main being reverted to ac92f2d (last-good: the timeout fix, which typechecks). kamu + mj0h to be re-landed as reviewed PRs after fixing kamu's type errors.
- Service NOT restarted until main is good.

## Acceptance
- Rig runs produce PRs on branches only; main is never directly pushed by a rig agent.
- A non-typechecking/failing rig PR cannot merge.
- origin/main is branch-protected.
close_reason: Safety gate built + deployed. (1) Branch protection on origin/main via gh API — direct pushes rejected, force-push/deletion blocked. (2) gastown coder.md rewritten to mandate branch->commit->push-branch->open-PR, never main, never self-merge, must typecheck before PR. (3) Same hard rule pinned in repo-root AGENTS.md. Merged via PR #10 (eating our own dogfood — used the new PR flow, not a main push). Also remediated the immediate damage: reverted the 2 broken rig commits off origin/main (force-push to clean 237d478), fixed my own logger.info arg bug, salvaged the rig commits to branch rig-salvage-kamu-mj0h for proper re-land. Remaining: CI typecheck status-check as a required gate (currently PR-required but no automated CI check wired) — follow-up.

title: Perf: append-only / size-keyed cache for listMessages (stop full-parsing messages.jsonl per request)
description: listMessages full-reads + JSON.parses the entire messages.jsonl (up to 4.9MB / ~1500 lines) on every request even for limit=50 desc, then slice(-limit) (store.ts:508-525). messages.jsonl is APPEND-ONLY, making caching trivially safe: keep an in-memory {conversationId->{size,parsed[]}} map; on read fstat the file — unchanged size returns cached, grown size reads only the new byte range and parses appended lines. For cold order=desc&limit=N, reverse-chunk read the last N lines instead of whole file. Must preserve normalizeMessage/unwrapSessionEnvelope (v3 envelope, lcp-nlud) and isLocalMessage filtering on the cached path.
acceptance_criteria: Repeated GET /messages polls on an unchanged conversation do a stat, not a multi-MB parse. listMessages output is byte-identical to current for v3-envelope and flat fixtures. v3-envelope-messages.test.ts + onfdisk-translate tests pass.
close_reason: Implemented + tested + deployed to lettashim.service. Warm GET /messages ~3x faster (22ms->7ms), byte-identical output, full suite green.

title: Perf: cache listRuns so GET /messages stops reading all run.json files per request
description: buildMessageRunMap -> listRuns({conversationId, limit:10000}) readdirSync + readRunAt over EVERY run.json (currently 1734 files, unbounded) on every GET /v1/conversations/{id}/messages, filtering by conversation_id only AFTER reading each from disk (runs.ts:799-811). This is the single biggest cost on the most-polled endpoint. Fix: wrap listRuns in the same makeDirMtimeCache pattern store.ts uses for listAgents/listConversations (store.ts:276) — parse runs once, invalidate on runs-dir mtime change — OR maintain a conversation_id->[run_id] index sidecar updated on run create/finalize so the walk is O(runs-in-conv) not O(all-runs).
acceptance_criteria: GET /messages no longer scales with total run count; a warm request does not re-read every run.json. Existing runs tests pass.
close_reason: Implemented + tested + deployed to lettashim.service. Warm GET /messages ~3x faster (22ms->7ms), byte-identical output, full suite green.

title: bug(shim): subagent task reports success with 'No assistant response found' and zero artifacts (false-positive completion)
description:
## Symptom

Background Agent dispatch (task_4, 2026-06-10 ~17:00, subagent agent-local-ec0c8aff-d415-4733-a293-34ed36c0a562 on lmstudio/claude-fable-5): task-notification reported status=completed / subagent_status=success, but the result body was 'No assistant response found'. Usage showed 76 tool_uses and 2,880,441 total tokens over ~10 minutes — yet the worker left ZERO verifiable artifacts: no branch, no commits (git log --all --since empty), no PR, no bead comments. The work (lcp-d0za + lcp-wd3i implementation) simply did not happen, or happened and was lost.

## Why this is P1

The front-man/fork architecture depends on trusting task notifications. A false 'success' breaks the delegation contract: the main agent relays 'done' to the user when nothing happened. Same class as the vibesync molecule false-status lesson (lcp-98y8) — self-reported status lies.

## Questions to answer

1. Where did 76 tool calls of output go? Is the subagent transcript persisted anywhere durable (runs dir appears to only hold main-agent runs)? If not, that's a second bug: subagent runs aren't persisted/inspectable.
2. Why was final assistant text missing? Did the worker end with a tool call (e.g. killed mid-loop, context overflow, max-turns)? 
3. Why does the harness map 'no final assistant message' to success instead of error?

## Acceptance

- [ ] Task completion status reflects reality: 'no assistant response' => status=failed (or a distinct 'completed_no_output' the dispatcher can treat as failure)
- [ ] Subagent transcripts persisted and locatable by agent_id/task_id for post-mortem
- [ ] Termination reason surfaced in the task notification (max_turns / context_overflow / killed / clean)

## Evidence

- /tmp/letta-background/task_4.log (contains only the bare notification)
- Dispatch context: bead lcp-wd3i + lcp-d0za brief, ~591s duration

comments.author: Claude Code
comments.text: Second failure mode on the same dispatch (task_7, codex-spark, 2026-06-10 ~17:15): 'Stream ended without finish_reason' after 43 tool calls / ~214s. Honest failure this time (status=failed), but SAME underlying gap: 43 tool calls of partial work are unrecoverable — no branch/commits left behind, task log contains only the error JSON (19 lines), no transcript. Confirms both asks: (1) persist subagent transcripts durably, (2) surface termination reason. ADD: (3) brief-level mitigation is commit-early-commit-often (now in redispatch briefs), but harness-level checkpointing would be better. Also note: this dispatch is now on its FOURTH attempt across 3 models (5.5 quota-429, fable false-success, codex-spark stream-death) — the shim-pair work itself may be heavy enough that worker reliability is the gating factor, evidence for retry-with-fallback-chain automation (lcp-1lod).

title: feat(shim): passive runtime introspection — agent always knows its own serving model + runtime state
description:
## Context (Emmanuel, 2026-06-10)

During front-man architecture testing, Emmanuel swapped conversation models repeatedly (M3 ↔ fable-5 ↔ deepseek-flash). The agent (Meridian) had NO way to know which model was serving its turns — it guessed wrong twice in one session: (1) misattributed a dropped-first-character bug to MiniMax-M3 in bead letta-mobile-ujz3x when the model was actually fable-5; (2) falsely announced 'back to fable' timing. The human can see the model in client UI/config; the agent is the only party blind to its own runtime.

This matters MORE under the front-man/fork architecture: model identity determines what the agent should attempt inline vs delegate, how it self-assesses output quality, and how it attributes bugs.

## Need: passive, not tool-gated

A tool the agent must remember to call is the wrong shape (it didn't know it needed to check). The runtime state should be ambiently present, like cwd/permission-mode already are.

## Design options (pick in implementation)

1. **Extend the connection system-reminder**: the client/shim already injects device info + permission mode on each connection; add 'Serving model: lmstudio/claude-fable-5' + context window config. Cheap, zero new frames. Gap: doesn't cover mid-session swaps until next reminder.
2. **Model-change event frame**: when the serving model changes mid-conversation, inject a system-reminder into the next turn ('model switched: M3 → fable-5'). Covers the swap case precisely.
3. **Both (recommended)**: baseline in connection reminder + delta event on change.

## Scope of introspectable state (passive tier)

- Serving model handle (the critical one)
- Permission mode (already present)
- Context window: max + current utilization % (currently requires a curl to /v1/agents/:id/context — fine as active introspection, but a one-line summary in the reminder would prevent surprise compactions)
- Session role: main thread vs fork vs subagent (load-bearing for lcp-wd3i fork-verdict exemptions)

## Acceptance

- [ ] Agent can state its serving model correctly at any point without a tool call
- [ ] Mid-session model swap surfaces to the agent within one turn
- [ ] Works for both WS mobile clients and CLI connections
- [ ] Session-role discriminator included (main/fork/subagent)

## Relations

- Pairs with letta-mobile-g5hyz (model visibility for the HUMAN in drawer UI) — this is the AGENT-side mirror
- Supports lcp-wd3i (fork verdict needs session-role awareness)
- Evidence: letta-mobile-ujz3x misattribution correction

title: feat(shim): 'fork' verdict in permissions engine + agent-actuated override (front-man architecture)
description:
## Context

Emmanuel's front-man interaction model (2026-06-10): a cheap/fast model owns the conversation thread and NEVER blocks on work. Anything needing tools gets FORKED — the fork (warm cache, full conversation context) either handles the work or dispatches fresh light-context subagents. Conversation latency is the product; the main thread must stay unblocked.

Rather than a classifier, use the model's own behavior as the classifier and the permissions engine as enforcement: a tool call on the main thread is the signal that work is starting, and the rule engine routes it.

## Design

Extend the server-side permissions model (lcp-indw, landed PR #36) with a fourth verdict: **fork** (alongside allow/ask/deny).

Semantics:
- Rule matches a tool call on the MAIN conversation thread → verdict 'fork'
- Shim does NOT execute the tool inline. Instead returns a structured denial instructing the agent to dispatch Agent(subagent_type: 'fork', run_in_background: true) with the intended work as the deliverable spec — or (stretch) auto-spawns the fork seeded with the intercepted tool call
- Forked/subagent sessions are EXEMPT from fork rules (workers must work) — verdict applies only to the front-man thread. Needs a session-role discriminator (main vs fork vs subagent) in rule evaluation context.

Example policy:
- Bash(*) -> fork
- Edit(*) -> fork, Write(*) -> fork
- Read(*) -> allow (single fast reads are fine inline)
- Bash(bd show:*) -> allow, Bash(git log:*) -> allow (trivial-inline allowlist)

## Agent-actuated override (sudo semantics)

The fork verdict must be bypassable BY THE AGENT consciously, with audit:

1. Fork-verdict denial response includes override instructions: re-issue the same tool call with an override token + one-line justification (e.g. permissions_override: { rule: 'Bash(*)', reason: 'single fast status check, conversational answer depends on it' })
2. Shim honors the override, executes inline, and LOGS the override event (rule, justification, timestamp, conversation) to an audit trail queryable later
3. Rate-limit overrides (e.g. N per turn / M per hour) so a misbehaving cheap model can't lapse into inline-everything; over-limit overrides escalate to 'ask' (human approves)
4. Config flag to disable overrides entirely for hardened deployments

This mirrors sudo: the rule is the default, conscious bypass is possible, every bypass is logged and bounded.

## Cache discipline (load-bearing constraint)

Fork economics depend on prompt-cache reuse: a fork's context MUST be strictly conversation-prefix + appended directive. Nothing inserted/reordered upstream of the history, or the cached prefix breaks and every fork pays full input. Acceptance test should assert prefix-stability of forked context.

## Acceptance

- [ ] 'fork' verdict evaluable in rules; main-thread-only (session-role aware)
- [ ] Structured denial with fork instructions returned to agent
- [ ] Override path: token + justification -> inline execution + audit log entry
- [ ] Override rate-limiting with escalate-to-ask on breach
- [ ] Audit trail queryable (REST mirror consistent with lcp-indw pattern)
- [ ] Fork-context prefix-stability regression test
- [ ] Default-off behind env flag (SHIM_FORK_VERDICT=1), byte-identical behavior when off

## Relations

- Builds on lcp-indw (server-side permissions, PR #36)
- Pairs with delegation_rules.md in Meridian's system memory (the instruction-layer half)
- Related: turn-silence watchdog, agent-pool worker TTL (turn-lifecycle enforcement family)

title: REGRESSION: inbound images omitted — model.input vision gate lost from patch-loader/bundle
description:
SYMPTOM: user-sent images arrive to the model as '(image omitted: model does not support images)' — inbound vision broken again. Reported 2026-06-07.

ROOT CAUSE (two-gate problem, confirmed): the bundled letta.js gates Read/attachment images on the resolved model.input including 'image'/'vision'. Our local/custom handles (e.g. lmstudio/opus-4-8) resolve to input:['text'], so images are stripped to the NON_VISION_USER_IMAGE_PLACEHOLDER before reaching the model. This was previously fixed via a patch-loader bundle injection (globalThis.__lcpFixLocalVisionInput rewriting model.input to include 'image'/'vision'), tracked lcp-qi2f / lcp-taqw. That fix is now GONE: grep of admin-shim/scripts/letta-code-patch-loader.mjs shows 0 references to __lcpFixLocalVisionInput, and the live /root/.bun/.../@letta-ai/letta-code/letta.js bundle has 0 references — the patch is not present/applied. Likely lost across a patch-loader rewrite or letta-code version bump (now 0.27.3).

KEY POINT (do not be fooled): admin-shim/lib/model-catalog.ts DOES mark claude/opus as ['text','vision',...] — but the CATALOG gate is SEPARATE from the BUNDLE's model.input gate. Catalog being correct is necessary but NOT sufficient; the bundle model.input patch is the one that actually re-enables inbound images. Both gates must pass.

FIX: restore the patch-loader vision-input injection so local/custom vision handles get model.input including 'image'/'vision' (re-apply the lcp-qi2f/lcp-taqw mechanism, or its equivalent for the current bundle token shape). VERIFY in the LIVE bundle (grep the running letta.js for the injected symbol) — 'written in patch source' != 'applied to running bundle'; restart shim and confirm grep>0 and an actual Read/attachment image reaches vision.

DEPLOY NOTE: the running shim is currently the stale Jun-6 dist build; merged capability work (cron/permissions/search/skills) is also not live. A rebuild+restart from clean master is needed regardless — fold the vision-input patch restore into that deploy and verify on-device.

RELATED: lcp-qi2f, lcp-taqw, catalog 7b93141, image_pipeline_regressions.md.
notes: HOW IT REGRESSED (traced, not guessed): the patch-loader vision fix was NEVER merged into the master line this admin-shim now tracks. The fix exists in commits aa6a405 / 6540af3 (lcp-qi2f "inbound user images reach vision — patch image gates") and e9c9902 (#17 "restore image vision support"), but `git merge-base --is-ancestor` confirms ALL THREE are NOT ancestors of current master, and master patch-loader has 0 vision/image refs. They landed on a DIVERGENT branch (image-pipeline / lcp-gukg-era line) that master never absorbed. Master DID carry the catalog fix 7b93141 (vision-capable in model-catalog.ts) but NOT the patch-loader BUNDLE gate fix — so the catalog gate passes while the bundle model.input gate still strips images. Same dual-history loss documented in image_pipeline_regressions.md ("verify landed/deployed ancestry before re-fixing"). FIX = cherry-pick/replay the patch-loader portion of aa6a405 + e9c9902 onto current master (NOT rewrite from scratch), adapt token-match strings to the current bundle (letta-code 0.27.3), then VERIFY in the live running letta.js bundle (grep>0) after rebuild+restart. The patch-loader test from aa6a405 should come along.

title: Runtime: structured context compaction (token budget + threshold summarization + /compact)
description: REAL PROJECT, most strategically important — this is a CORRECTNESS fix, not an optimization. We already filed lcp-0p0x: backend appears to do sliding-window, NOT summary-plus-tail, so agents silently lose old decisions as context fills and users don't notice until responses get weird. ADD a structured compaction layer: per-conversation token-budget tracking; automatic archival of old messages to a passage store; summarization triggered at thresholds (e.g. 50/75/90 percent of context window); explicit POST /v1/conversations/{id}/compact endpoint. ACCEPTANCE: token-budget visible (ties to lcp-0p0x introspection); summarize+archive trims active context without losing recoverable history; explicit compact endpoint; configurable strategy (sliding_window vs summary_plus_tail). HARD: summarization quality, what to archive, when to trigger — treat as a project, not a quick win. OUR backlog, not upstream. Source: lettacode-agent runtime feedback (#3); related lcp-0p0x.

title: Shim: server-side permissions model (allow/ask/deny per tool) with durable approval state
description: Move tool-call permission decisions server-side so trust levels are configurable per-agent and global, enforced consistently across Android and desktop. Mobile already has approval UX; relocate the DECISION to the shim. MODEL: per-agent permissions json plus a global fallback; fields version, default (ask/allow/deny), rules list of tool+action+reason; first match wins; prefix match; star equals any tool. ENDPOINTS: GET/PUT/PATCH agent permissions; GET/PUT global permissions; GET tool permission preview; POST/DELETE approvals by runId; GET pending approvals. FLOW: evaluate before invoking the CLI; allow executes, deny errors without executing, ask emits pending_approval and waits. CRITICAL ACCEPTANCE (hard 80 percent is distributed state, not the evaluator): pending approval state durable and replayable across WS reconnect, app backgrounding, multi-client, and shim restart; ONE canonical contract (existing mobile WS approval frames canonical, REST a thin mirror); evaluate before the CLI subprocess; align with the shared chat runtime so both clients render identically; document that prefix-match deny rules are a UX guardrail not a security boundary. Tests: rule precedence, allow/deny/ask, reconnect replay, two-client approval, restart survival. FILES: server.ts, lib/permissions.ts, lib/chat.ts, lib/mobile-channel-host.ts. Parent: shim capability epic. First real feature after the cron warm-up.
notes: 2026-06-10 status: implementation is complete and dark-shipped — evaluator (lib/permissions.ts), durable pending approvals (lib/pending-approval.ts), REST config/preview/approvals endpoints (live, verified), canUseTool enforcement path in sdk-adapter, 20 tests incl. reconnect-replay/two-client/restart-survival/dark-ship. Runtime channel plugin at /root/.letta/channels/mobile was missing the approval_resolved cross-client push (lcp-9ldv drift); ported by hand + shim restarted. REMAINING TO GO LIVE: set SHIM_SERVER_PERMISSIONS=1 in /etc/systemd/system/lettashim.service + restart (edit blocked by permission classifier; awaiting operator). No rule files exist in prod so enabling is behavior-preserving (hardcoded default=allow).
close_reason: Live in production 2026-06-10. title: Epic: admin-shim capability layer (skills, hooks, search, permissions, cron REST)
description:
Surface five Letta-Code-style capabilities on the admin-shim as REST/WS APIs so BOTH the Android and Windows desktop clients (and, via interop, the official Letta client) get them server-side without app rebuilds. This is the 'thin native client over a capable core' thesis: build on the shim, not in the app.

DESIGN PRINCIPLE (load-bearing): model these against the shared chat runtime contracts merged in letta-mobile #382 (sharedLogic chat/runtime). Permission decisions, approval state, and search results should be modeled ONCE so Android + desktop render them identically. Do not re-fragment the layer we just unified.

FEATURES + PRIORITY (reordered from the source spec by strategic value):
1. Permissions model (first real one) — allow/ask/deny per tool, server-side, canonical approval contract.
2. Cron REST mutations (warm-up) — cheapest, infra exists.
3. Skills system — companion differentiator: extend agents without app rebuild.
4. Message search / recall — Phase 1 keyword, honest about phases.
5. Hooks — last, webhook-only first; shell hooks are RCE risk.

CROSS-CUTTING TRAPS (apply to acceptance of children):
- Durable, replayable approval/pending state across WS reconnect, app backgrounding, multi-client (desktop+mobile), and shim restart.
- Single serialized writer per store file; no WS-write + REST-write races on JSON (+fs.watch).
- Progressive disclosure for skills injection (descriptions always, body on demand) — not full SKILL.md every turn.
- No security theater: prefix-match deny rules and hook timeouts are UX guardrails, not security boundaries.
- One canonical contract per concern (prefer WS frames canonical, REST a thin mirror) — avoid dual sources of truth.

SOURCE: detailed spec transmitted by Emmanuel 2026-06-07 (other-agent recon of Letta Code internals).

title: Streaming stall: response freezes ~1min then dumps whole — upstream Anthropic call is non-streaming (stream defaults false)
description:
SYMPTOM (Emmanuel, 2026-06-05): assistant response shows the first word, freezes for ~1 minute, then the WHOLE response streams/dumps in at once. Classic buffer-then-flush — tokens generated but held, released in a batch.

ROOT CAUSE (traced): our turns hit the anthropic-claude-max-proxy at :8082 (systemd anthropic-claude-proxy.service, /opt/stacks/anthropic-claude-max-proxy, cli.py --headless). The shim env routes there: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8082 (-> proxy /v1/messages, the path opus/Anthropic turns use) and LMSTUDIO_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8082/v1 (-> /v1/chat/completions).

BOTH proxy paths DEFAULT stream=FALSE when the incoming request omits it:
- Anthropic-native: anthropic/models.py:49  . The handler then takes the for_streaming=False branch (anthropic/api_client.py:24/42) and makes a NON-STREAMING call to real Anthropic -> Anthropic generates the entire response (the ~1-min freeze) -> returns it whole (the dump).
- OpenAI-compat: openai_compat/request_converter.py:47  .

So if OUR provider request does not explicitly set stream:true, the proxy blocks on a full non-streaming generation. The 'first word then freeze then dump' matches: shim/mobile shows an optimistic head, then waits for the buffered whole.

(NOTE: the separate llmux-openai-shim container also has a _buffer_openai_stream_to_json non-streaming branch, but it is NOT in our path — it listens elsewhere and forwards TO 8082; our turns go straight to the :8082 max proxy.)

FIX — determine WHERE stream:true should be set/why it's missing:
1. Confirm empirically what our letta.js provider call sends to :8082 (enable the proxy STREAM trace / STREAM_TRACE_DIR in /opt/stacks/anthropic-claude-max-proxy/settings.py, or log request stream in proxy/logging_utils.py which already does logger.debug Stream:..., bump to info). Capture a live turn.
2. If letta.js sends stream:false (or omits it) on the local-backend provider path, fix the provider call to request streaming. The shim's own SSE coalescer (stream-coalescer.ts) and chat.ts (body['stream'] !== false) expect streamed frames; a non-streaming upstream defeats them.
3. If the request DOES set stream:true but the proxy still buffers, the bug is proxy-side (honor stream / ensure the streaming branch is taken for our model+path).

This interacts with perceived latency on EVERY turn and likely worsens with longer responses (more to buffer). High user-visible impact.

ACCEPTANCE: assistant responses stream token-by-token as generated (no ~1-min freeze-then-dump). Verify on device with a long response.

RELATED: stream-coalescer.ts, chat.ts:650, the multimodal llmux routing note (memory), the timeout work (same proxy layer).

comments.author: Claude Code
comments.text:
CORRECTION — my non-streaming/buffering theory was WRONG, disproven empirically. Enabled STREAM_TRACE_ENABLED on the anthropic-claude-max-proxy (:8082) and captured a live turn (stream_traces/20260606T014135Z_openai-chat_*.log):

- Proxy DISPATCHES STREAMING upstream: 'dispatching POST api.anthropic.com/v1/messages for streaming'; Anthropic responds status=200 and streams content_block_delta chunks; proxy converts + emits OpenAI chunks token-by-token. ENTIRE stream completed in ~3.3s (chunk #1 @ .751 -> [DONE] @ 43.079), 20 chunks, NO mid-stream stall. The proxy + upstream are fast and genuinely streaming. The 'stream defaults to false' / _buffer_openai_stream_to_json theory does NOT apply — our requests DO stream.
- The admin-shim SDK-Transport wire log ALSO shows assistant_message frames flowing continuously with real-time timestamps as they arrive (not after completion); the stream-coalescer window is only 200ms (smoothing, not a 1-min stall). Shim is streaming too.

SO THE ~1-MIN FREEZE IS CLIENT-SIDE RENDER, not proxy and not shim wire. Pattern 'first word -> ~1min freeze -> whole reply dumps' with fast upstream (3s) + fast shim wire = the CLI/mobile client is BUFFERING THE RENDER: it shows the first chunk then withholds the rest until some condition (likely end-of-turn / stop_reason / a render gate), then dumps. NOTE: this was observed in the Letta Code CLI chat (Emmanuel clarified he means the live chat in front of him), so the suspect is the CLI render path (and/or the mobile render if it shares the gate).

ALSO SEEN: proxy.log had '[<id>] Error converting stream:' in openai_compat/stream_converter.py:535 — worth checking if a conversion error on some turns forces a fallback that buffers; but the captured good turn streamed fine, so the freeze may correlate with that error path on SOME turns.

NEXT: instrument the CLI/render leg, not the proxy. Determine whether the client renders assistant deltas incrementally or waits for turn completion. The proxy debug/trace was left ENABLED (LOG_LEVEL=debug + STREAM_TRACE_ENABLED via systemd drop-in /etc/systemd/system/anthropic-claude-proxy.service.d/debug-stream.conf) — DISABLE it after investigation to avoid trace disk growth.

Retitle suggestion: 'Streaming stall is CLIENT-SIDE RENDER buffering (proxy+shim stream fine)'.

comments.author: Claude Code
comments.text:
NARROWED with timing data (a few seconds, not a minute — Emmanuel corrected). Measured across legs:

1. PROXY emits SMOOTHLY: latest traces show inter-chunk gaps mostly <500ms (one 511ms). NOT the source of the multi-second freeze.
2. SHIM frame Fri Jun  5 09:44:53 PM EDT 2026 timestamps show ~3s gaps then BURSTS of chunks (e.g. 10.247 -> 13.407 -> 16.370 -> burst of 6 in ms -> 20.244). So the gap appears between proxy-emit and the shim's wired frames.
3. The SDK-Session/SDK-Transport stream logging is INSIDE the letta.js bundle (not shim source). The bundle has stream  +  knobs — candidate batching.
4. CRITICAL NEW EVIDENCE: the proxy trace shows opus is doing EXTENDED THINKING — 18 thinking events + 18 text_delta interleaved in one turn. So some 'gaps' are THINKING blocks (model reasoning, no visible text), then visible text bursts after the thinking block.

TWO REMAINING HYPOTHESES (both client/render-side, NOT proxy):
  A. THINKING NOT SHOWN AS ACTIVITY: during a multi-second thinking block the client renders nothing -> looks frozen -> text appears in a burst when reasoning yields visible tokens. This is a render/UX gap (model is working, UI shows idle), not a transport buffer.
  B. A genuine batch flush in letta.js (flushInterval/batchSize) holding text deltas and releasing them periodically.

NEXT DIAGNOSTIC (instrument the RENDER leg, stop bundle-spelunking): determine whether the CLI/mobile renders (i) reasoning/thinking deltas as live activity and (ii) text deltas incrementally vs on a flush boundary. If thinking isn't surfaced, the fix is to show a 'thinking…' indicator / stream reasoning so the gap reads as activity not freeze. Separately, check letta.js stream flushInterval/batchSize defaults and whether they can be lowered.

Proxy debug+trace still ENABLED (systemd drop-in debug-stream.conf) — disable after.

Supersedes earlier 'upstream non-streaming buffering' theory (disproven).

comments.author: Claude Code
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND (proven by upstream-vs-emit timing comparison). The few-second pause is LENGTH-CORRELATED (Emmanuel: short response no pause; long response shows first word/letters then a few-second pause then the rest bursts).

DEFINITIVE MEASUREMENT (stream trace of a long turn, comparing the proxy's RAW ANTHROPIC receive timestamps vs its OPENAI downstream emit timestamps):
- ANTHROPIC raw upstream: pause of 5.76s present
- OPENAI proxy emit: same pauses (5.76s, 5.15s)
The gaps are IDENTICAL on both sides -> the proxy faithfully passes through pauses that REAL ANTHROPIC ITSELF produces. The pause is NOT in our stack (not proxy, not shim, not client transport). It originates at api.anthropic.com.

WHY: opus-4-8 runs with extended thinking (trace showed interleaved thinking + text_delta events). On longer/harder responses Anthropic interleaves THINKING blocks (no text_delta emitted) between text blocks. During a multi-second thinking block, no visible token is sent -> the client shows the first words then appears frozen -> the next text block bursts in. Shorter responses don't hit a mid-stream thinking block so there's no pause. This is EXPECTED MODEL BEHAVIOR surfaced as a freeze because the CLIENT DOES NOT RENDER THINKING ACTIVITY.

SO THIS IS A UX GAP, NOT A TRANSPORT BUG. Fix direction (client/render side):
- Surface reasoning/thinking as live activity: when the stream is in a thinking block (thinking deltas arriving but no text), show a 'thinking…' indicator / animate, OR stream the reasoning text, so the pause reads as the model actively working rather than a frozen UI.
- Optionally lower extended-thinking budget for short turns, but the real fix is rendering thinking state.
- Verify the shim forwards thinking/reasoning frames to the client (reasoning content blocks) so the client CAN show activity during the gap.

Supersedes both prior theories (upstream non-streaming buffering; letta.js flushInterval — that was telemetry, a red herring). The proxy debug+trace (systemd drop-in debug-stream.conf, LOG_LEVEL=debug + STREAM_TRACE_ENABLED) can now be DISABLED.

Retitle: 'Long-response mid-stream pause = Anthropic interleaved thinking, not rendered as activity (UX, client-side)'.

comments.author: Claude Code
comments.text:
SMOOTHER AS CO-SUSPECT (revisit 2026-06-06). Earlier I attributed the 'first word -> pause -> burst' ENTIRELY to upstream Anthropic interleaved thinking (proven: the multi-second gaps DO exist in the raw upstream stream). But I did NOT audit the mobile StreamingDisplayTextSmoother as a co-conspirator, and it just produced a confirmed HEAD-CLIP bug (streamed 'Filed' rendered as 'ed:' — see the mobile head-clip bead). The smoother is a CHARACTER-REVEAL ANIMATION that meters text at an estimated rate (charsPerMs, backlog catch-up, velocity tween) — it DECOUPLES on-screen text from actual token arrival. Possible smoother-caused artifacts distinct from the upstream gaps:
1. 'freeze then burst' may be PARTLY the smoother's backlog catch-up animating a big chunk in at a clamped rate, not only the raw upstream gap. I never compared the smoother's reveal timing vs arrival timing.
2. updateTarget resets revealedCount=0 on any non-append update (!text.startsWith(oldTarget)). If coalesced/reordered deltas (post-#360 coalescing) ever deliver a non-append target, the smoother REWINDS to 0 and re-reveals -> flicker / re-typing / text jumping.
3. velocity tween + backlog clamp can produce uneven reveal cadence -> reads as janky streaming even when frames arrive smoothly.
DEEPER QUESTION: is the smoother worth its complexity/bug surface? #360 already coalesces the stream to frame cadence at the TRANSPORT layer. The smoother may be re-solving 'make streaming smooth' on top of that while adding head-clip + rewind + jitter bugs and decoupling display from reality. Consider whether a simpler 'render coalesced arrived text directly' beats the metered-reveal smoother. AUDIT: instrument the smoother's reveal timestamps vs frame-arrival timestamps on a real turn; check whether the on-screen pause/burst correlates with the smoother's backlog/catch-up rather than (or in addition to) the upstream gap. RELATED: mobile head-clip bead (StreamingDisplayTextSmoother seed/cursor), #360 coalesce, RememberStreamSmoother, MessageContentFactory hasStreamed/initialText.

comments.author: Claude Code
comments.text:
CONFIRMED POST-SMOOTHER-FIX (2026-06-06 ~02:50): the 'first word -> long pause -> burst' symptom PERSISTS after the smoother fix (#365 / letta-mobile-1kz40) is live on device (APK 0.1.0-301-g688f5c72). This DEFINITIVELY isolates the surviving symptom to UPSTREAM, not the smoother. Shim wire-log timing of a real long turn shows tokens genuinely STOP arriving from Anthropic for multi-second stretches: measured pauses of 3.57s, 5.69s, 11.11s, and 29.38s in assistant_message arrival (4 pauses >1s in 29 intervals). During these gaps NO text is sent upstream — the model is doing extended thinking/reasoning between text blocks. The smoother cannot help: there are no tokens to reveal.

So the smoother fix correctly addressed its scope (throttle/keep-up + head-clip), and this remaining symptom is the Anthropic interleaved-thinking pause — a UX gap, not a bug. The model is ACTIVELY WORKING during the pause but the UI shows nothing -> reads as a freeze.

FIX (render-side UX, the model is reasoning during the gap): (1) STREAM THE THINKING — Anthropic IS sending  content_block_delta events during the gap (proven in the earlier proxy stream trace: 18 thinking events interleaved with 18 text_delta); surface them (e.g. a collapsible/greyed 'thinking…' stream) so the pause shows reasoning activity instead of nothing. (2) OR a subtle animated 'thinking…' indicator during any text-arrival gap so it reads as active, not frozen. Verify the shim FORWARDS reasoning/thinking frames to mobile so the client CAN render activity during the gap (check reasoning_message handling end to end). ACCEPTANCE: during an upstream thinking pause, the UI shows the model is working (thinking stream or indicator), not a frozen first-word. This is now a pure render-the-thinking-activity task; the transport/smoother are exonerated.

title: Subagent model override (non-default model) fails: thinking.enabled.budget_tokens Field required
description:
Dispatching a background subagent with an explicit non-default model (e.g. model:'sonnet') fails INSTANTLY (0 tool uses, ~5s) with: invalid_request_error 'thinking.enabled.budget_tokens: Field required' (local_backend_error). Three parallel Sonnet-routed chrome agents all died identically 2026-06-05.

CAUSE: when a model is requested with extended thinking enabled but no thinking budget is set, Anthropic's API requires thinking.budget_tokens. The DEFAULT subagent path works because the shim sets LETTA_CODE_THINKING_BUDGET_TOKENS=10000 (env on lettashim) which flows into the default model's thinking config. But an EXPLICIT model override on the Agent/subagent dispatch path does NOT carry/inject the thinking budget -> malformed request -> immediate failure.

IMPACT: blocks strategic model routing for subagents (route mechanical+gated work to Sonnet/Codex, reserve Opus). Currently you can ONLY use the default model for subagents; any override that needs a thinking budget 400s. This directly blocks the model-budget-aware routing intent (lcp-1lod).

FIX: when a subagent/Agent dispatch specifies a model, ensure the thinking config is populated for that model — either inject the default thinking budget (LETTA_CODE_THINKING_BUDGET_TOKENS) into the override path, or set thinking.enabled.budget_tokens appropriately per the resolved model, or disable thinking when no budget is configured for the override. Trace the subagent dispatch -> model resolution -> request construction (the Agent tool path / subagent spawn in letta.js + the shim's model handling) and ensure budget_tokens is present whenever thinking is enabled.

ACCEPTANCE: dispatching a subagent with model:'sonnet' (or any non-default) succeeds and runs, with thinking budget correctly applied.

RELATED: lcp-1lod (model:auto -> role/task/budget-aware routing), the thinking-budget patch-loader work, debug_loop model routing policy.
close_reason: Fixed at egress proxy (anthropic-claude-max-proxy request_sanitizer): inject ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_THINKING_BUDGET (default 10000, clamped < max_tokens) when thinking.type=enabled lacks budget_tokens; downgrade to disabled when max_tokens<=1024. Unit cases pass; proxy restarted. Live validation on next non-default-model subagent dispatch.

title: DECISION: iroh-based device<->shim pairing transport; single Kotlin impl in sharedLogic; shim-language port deferred to lcp-59c
description:
GOAL: secure device<->shim pairing. Emmanuel wants iroh (https://iroh.computer, n0/number0 — Rust p2p QUIC library), NOT a traditional VPN. Concern raised: 'VPN gives insulation at the cost of friction.' iroh resolves that tension: it is p2p connection-by-NodeId (Ed25519 keypair = identity), automatic NAT hole-punching + relay fallback, QUIC/TLS1.3 mutually-authenticated-by-NodeId transport. There is NO network to join — connection is to a node identity, so the PAIRING IS THE PERIMETER (no open :8291 reachable by anyone on a network; shim only accepts allowlisted NodeIds). This replaces BOTH the currently-stubbed app-layer auth (MOBILE_CHANNEL_TOKEN unset; logs show 'auth skipped (no token configured)', any hello-frame token accepted) AND the VPN perimeter with one stronger mechanism: cryptographic per-device identity, instant revocation (remove NodeId from allowlist), encrypted-by-default transport, NAT traversal so off-LAN/cellular Just Works without a static VPN following the device.

CURRENT SECURITY STATE (must fix): device->shim /shim/v1/mobile is effectively OPEN on the LAN — no real auth. Fine behind own walls today; not a pairing model. Do not ship beyond personal LAN without this.

KEY ARCHITECTURE DECISION (the reason for this bead): Emmanuel asked — since the runtime is being embedded into Kotlin hosts (Android + Desktop via sharedLogic), how much work to make the SHIM Kotlin too so the SAME iroh impl works in both locations? Analysis:
- iroh has first-class Kotlin/JVM bindings (iroh-ffi via UniFFI, JVM+Android targets). So the iroh transport+pairing (the precious, security-critical code) can be written ONCE in sharedLogic/commonMain Kotlin and run on BOTH the Kotlin hosts AND a JVM shim. This eliminates the Node<->iroh binding maturity risk.
- BUT a full shim port is large: the admin-shim is thousands of lines of stateful, recently-perf-tuned TS (WS transport, agent pool + turn lifecycle/idle reaper, run/frame persistence with byte-offset tailing, conversation store/cursors/replay, subagent registry, the whole self-todo machinery just stabilized, mobile-channel host + .mjs plugin, SDK adapter to letta.js, model catalog, cron, secrets, healing). Rewriting it risks re-introducing bugs we just fixed.
- LOAD-BEARING: the shim exists to front letta.js (TS/Node). A Kotlin shim re-introduces a cross-language boundary to the runtime — just moved. THEREFORE the shim-language question is DOWNSTREAM of lcp-59c (embed-Node-runtime-via-nodejs-mobile vs KMP-native): if on-device runs its own embedded letta.js, the shim's on-device role shrinks to a thin remote/cloud broker (small to port); if KMP-native wins, Kotlin-everything is natural.

DECISION (what to commit now):
1. iroh pairing transport implemented ONCE in Kotlin sharedLogic/commonMain, behind a clean transport interface (ports-and-adapters — agent core untouched; transport swappable). Desktop + Android hosts use it directly.
2. DEFER the shim-language port: decide it as a CONSEQUENCE of the lcp-59c runtime outcome, not in isolation. Do NOT do a big-bang TS->Kotlin shim rewrite now.
3. Honest middle path option: keep the heavy cloud shim as TS (fronts cloud letta.js, stable), but make the DEVICE-FACING pairing/transport layer a shared Kotlin component both the Kotlin hosts and (via a thin JVM sidecar) the shim consume — getting the 'one iroh impl' win without rewriting agent-pool/persistence/self-todo.

PAIRING HANDSHAKE SKETCH: shim is an iroh node w/ stable NodeId. Device generates its own NodeId on first run. Pairing: device shows NodeId (QR) -> shim authorizes (one-time code / local-network confirm) -> adds to paired-devices allowlist; shim NodeId handed to device. Thereafter device dials shim by NodeId; iroh hole-punches/relays; mutual keypair auth; shim checks dialing NodeId vs allowlist. Revoke = remove from allowlist. Pairing = the onboarding ritual (fits product north-star: every system moment a relationship moment).

SPIKES TO DE-RISK (gate the decision):
- SPIKE A: validate iroh-ffi Kotlin binding on JVM (shim/desktop) AND Android — can a JVM/Android process be an iroh node cleanly, dial by NodeId, hole-punch, fall back to relay? This is the load-bearing risk (same shape as node-pty risk in lcp-59c).
- SPIKE B: stand up a SELF-HOSTED iroh relay (do not depend on n0 public relays — no traffic metadata to third parties for a private/self-hosted posture). Confirm both ends use it.
- SPIKE C: tunnel the existing /shim/v1/mobile protocol over an iroh bi-stream (QUIC stream) instead of WS — confirm the transport is swappable without touching agent core.

SEQUENCING: (1) lcp-59c resolves (determines shim future shape) -> (2) iroh spikes A/B/C in sharedLogic -> (3) decide shim language informed by both. Commit NOW only to: iroh pairing + single Kotlin transport impl in sharedLogic.

RELATED: lcp-59c (embed runtime decision — this is downstream), lcp-b02 (rewrite/local-runtime strategy), letta-mobile-m26c5 (LiteRT bridge — same sharedLogic locus), the multiplatform_roadmap (multi-host agent-core-canonical, ports-and-adapters).

title: admin-shim test runner reports false-green — node --test swallows failures (exit 0)
description:
FIXED in PR #27 (branch lcp-a0rl-fix-test-runner-false-green off lcp-gukg-terminal-stop-reason).

ROOT CAUSE: package.json test ran `node --import tsx/esm --test test/*.test.ts`. Command-line --import applied only to the PARENT runner; node:test spawns each test file in its OWN child process which does NOT inherit a command-line --import. Children never loaded the TS subtests, so each file = 1 phantom pass and all failures/throws were swallowed -> exit 0.

FIX: moved loader to NODE_OPTIONS="--import tsx/esm" (inherited by children). Real subtests now run (473 vs phantom 41); failing test exits non-zero with loud diff. Proven: injected failure -> exit 1; reverted -> exit 0.

SILENTLY FAILING (surfaced by fix): (1) mobile-conversation-cursors.test.ts set env above a STATIC import (ESM hoisting -> default cap 1000 not 50) — FIXED via dynamic import(). (2) sdk-compat live-CLI session probe — CLI now needs --new-agent/--agent, SDK passes neither — gated behind SHIM_TEST_LIVE_CLI=1 + filed lcp-lzap.

CI: .github/workflows/test.yml now runs typecheck+test on every PR; intent both checks REQUIRED via branch protection (admin must set). 

VERIFIED: typecheck clean, build clean, suite green (473 tests / fail 0 / exit 0).
notes: Observed during lcp-53e8 validation: npm test and isolated NODE_OPTIONS=--import tsx/esm node --test test/subagent-registry.test.ts both print all subagent-registry assertions as passing, then the node:test process stays alive until external timeout (120s isolated, 600s full suite). Focused changed-surface tests and typecheck pass; hang appears unrelated to mobile frame stamping.

title: Subagent registry can miss a dispatch ingest (running subagent invisible in bar), esp. around reconnect/restart
description:
Observed 2026-06-04 after the SHIM_POOL_IDLE_SEC restart: a freshly dispatched subagent (linger/navigate task) ran for 10+ min (confirmed live CLI process, idle-reaper fix holding) but NO chip appeared in the active bar. Registry logs show the last ingest HIT was the PRIOR dispatch (toolu_01MDk3..., already 'completed'); task_1's Agent dispatch produced NO 'ingest HIT' and no started/running emit. Meanwhile repeated subscribe->unsubscribe churn (phone reconnecting). The subagent's TODO is still visible via the timeline subagent CARD (reads run/message data), but the BAR chip depends on the live registry which never registered the dispatch.

SO: the agent is alive and working (not orphaned — idle fix worked), but the registry MISSED its dispatch ingest, leaving a running subagent invisible in the bar. Likely the Agent dispatch frame fired during/around the shim restart window and the ingest hook didn't observe it, OR a stale 'completed' snapshot wins on resubscribe.

THIS IS DISTINCT from the idle-reaper orphan bug (that's fixed) and from the chip-render bugs. Same CLASS as the 'ingest HIT missing' issues during 73o2h bring-up.

FIX DIRECTIONS: (1) registry must ingest dispatches reliably even across shim restart / right after boot (replay/scan recent runs for in-flight Agent tool calls on startup, not just live frames). (2) on resubscribe, push the CURRENT active set (snapshot) to the new listener, and don't let a stale terminal entry mask a newer running one. (3) reconcile registry state from run records periodically so a missed live frame self-heals.

ACCEPTANCE: a subagent dispatched at any time (including right after restart) appears in the bar; reconnecting the phone re-hydrates the current active set.

title: Async tool execution decoupled from turn lifecycle (don't block turns on long tool calls)
description:
PROBLEM: tool calls are synchronous within a turn — the turn cannot reach a terminal stop_reason until the tool returns. A long tool call (CI wait, build, web fetch, long subagent) holds the turn open for minutes and hits the turn/stream timeout, surfacing as 'turn failed/timed out' to the user (see related requires_approval/lcp-gukg beads). The CI-poll tax and orphan-and-rescue tax are the same root issue.

GOAL: make tool EXECUTION async from TURN lifecycle. Turn emits the tool call, the turn closes cleanly (end_turn, not 'waiting forever'), the tool runs out-of-band, and when it completes the result is injected as a NEW event that starts a continuation turn. The user/agent is never blocked on a long-running tool.

IMPORTANT — DON'T STEP ON LETTA: this is very likely an UPSTREAM concern, not a fork. Letta Code already ships run_in_background + TaskOutput + <task-notification> for background tasks; the gap is that FOREGROUND synchronous tool calls still block the turn. Before building anything in the admin-shim:
1. Confirm whether upstream letta.js already supports (or plans) async/non-blocking foreground tool calls, or whether the intended pattern is 'use run_in_background for anything long'. If the latter, this is a DISCIPLINE fix (agent should background long tools + return, not poll), not a code change.
2. If a genuine gap exists, prefer an upstream contribution / issue over a shim-local hack, so we don't diverge from Letta.
3. Only implement shim-side if upstream won't and it's safe to decouple at our transport boundary.

SHORT-TERM MITIGATION (no code): agent must STOP poll-blocking. For anything >~30s (CI waits, builds), use run_in_background and END the turn, then react to the completion notification. Most 'turn failed' cases today are self-inflicted by while-pending sleep loops keeping the turn alive past timeout.

ACCEPTANCE: a long-running tool call does not hold a turn open past the timeout; either (a) the agent backgrounds it and the turn ends immediately with a later continuation, or (b) the runtime supports async tool results that resume a turn. Document the chosen mechanism and whether it lives upstream or in the shim.

RELATED: requires_approval stop-reason misclassification, lcp-gukg terminal stop_reason, the background-agent lifecycle research (RESEARCH_background_agent_lifecycle.md, intended but the research task itself orphaned).

title: Turn timed out notification shown to user during active mobile session
description: Observed on device 2026-06-04: user received a 'turn timed out' notification while using the mobile chat. This is distinct from normal subagent completion/failure chrome and reads like a runtime/turn-driver reliability failure surfacing to the user. Need to investigate whether the timeout came from the shim turn pool, Letta Code background task lifecycle, WS/A2UI stream timeout, or mobile rendering of a terminal error. Collect logs around the event: /tmp/admin-shim.log, backend run frames, and mobile logcat. title: Shim deploy does not sync repo channel plugins to runtime HOME — silent .mjs drift
description: INFRA RELIABILITY (high leverage): the admin-shim loads channel plugins from $HOME/.letta/channels (the running shim has HOME=/root, so /root/.letta/channels/mobile/), but ALL channel-plugin source lives and is git-tracked at /opt/stacks/letta-code-parallel/home/.letta/channels/mobile/. There is NO deploy/build step that syncs the repo copy to the runtime HOME copy. Result: every change to plugin.mjs / lib/ws-handler.mjs etc is silently IGNORED by the running shim — it keeps loading a stale copy. This cost ~hours on 2026-06-04: the entire 73o2h subagent-bar WS wiring (multiple merged PRs touching ws-handler.mjs + plugin.mjs) never reached the running shim because /root/.letta/channels/mobile/ws-handler.mjs was dated May 28 with zero subagent code. Diagnosis only surfaced via live registry logging showing listeners=0. Manually cp'ing the files to /root + restart fixed it. ACCEPTANCE: a deploy step (or the systemd ExecStartPre, or a build script) must sync home/.letta/channels/** to the runtime HOME .letta/channels/** before the shim starts — OR the shim should load channel plugins directly from the repo path, not HOME. Also: detect/warn on drift (compare mtimes/hashes at boot and log a loud warning). Add to the deploy SOP. This is a whole CLASS of silent failure: any .mjs channel change appears merged+deployed but is not live.
notes: 2026-06-10: drift confirmed bidirectional. Runtime /root/.letta/channels/mobile has subagents_updated + self-todo push (letta-mobile-73o2h.1/gnyf7) missing from repo copy; repo copy has lcp-indw approval_resolved push missing from runtime — the RUNNING shim therefore lacks the approval cross-client push. lcp-4d5f reflection frames were added to BOTH copies by hand. Reconciliation still needed.

title: Background task ID/log-path collisions across session reconnects (silent task loss)
description: RELIABILITY: background Agent/Task dispatches can be silently lost because background task IDs (task_N) are not globally unique. Evidence from /tmp/letta-background on 2026-06-04: an overnight shim-registry dispatch (assigned task_1) had its log file overwritten by a later 'reflection' subagent (subagent-1780579101736-1, conversation 'default') that was also assigned task_1 and completed at 09:22. task_2.log contains TWO stacked '[Task started: Implement subagent registry shim]' headers (slot re-entered). task_5.log shows the same doubling the prior night. Root cause hypotheses: (1) task_N counter is per-session/per-connection and re-bases on each Letta Code CLI reconnect (every system-reminder new-connection event), so a fresh dispatch reuses an id a still-running task owns; (2) multiple agents (the dispatching agent + auto-run reflection subagent + sibling dispatches) draw from the same task_N namespace and write to the same /tmp/letta-background/task_N.log path with no uniqueness guard; (3) reflection/scheduled agents firing during active background work greatly increase collision odds. Impact: (a) a long-running task's log is clobbered; (b) its completion notification + tracking slot are lost, so it appears 'interrupted' even when it actually ran (the 73o2h.2 mobile-bar work finished on disk but its result notification was lost; the 73o2h.1 shim-registry task produced nothing and its slot vanished). Acceptance: background task identifiers must be globally unique (e.g. include conversation/session id + uuid, not a re-basing counter); log paths must never collide; a completed/running task's log + result must not be overwritable by a later task; ideally surface a durable task registry so reconnects can re-attach to in-flight tasks rather than orphaning them. Investigate the task manager in the letta-code bundle (background process/agent task spawning + /tmp/letta-background/task_N.log path scheme) and the reflection scheduler. Add a regression test that two concurrent dispatches across a simulated reconnect get distinct ids/log paths.

title: P1: Add seq-to-byte offset index for high-cursor subscribe replay
description: Remaining shim perf follow-up: optimize subscribe/replay when clients reconnect with high cursors by indexing seq_id to byte offsets so tail replay does not scan or parse the full frames log.
acceptance_criteria: High-cursor subscribe/replay seeks near the requested cursor via seq-to-byte offset index; replay work is proportional to tail bytes/frames, not total log size; long-log regression coverage verifies behavior.
close_reason: Implemented in PR #21 (commit 226f3a2): sparse seq->byteOffset index in runs.ts (RunHandle.frameBytes + frameIndex, checkpoint every 256th frame + seq 1, frames.index.jsonl sidecar, findFrameOffsetForCursor binary search), subscribeToRun seeks to nearest checkpoint <= cursor. Scale test: 50k frames/cursor 49900 -> parsed lines 50000->337 (~148x) warm+cold, emit parity verified. Merged + deployed live (shim pid 2233955). Cold-run-without-index falls back to full scan (correct, slower). Merged, built, restarted.

title: P1: Avoid full transcript scan for inline tool-return synthesis
description: Remaining shim perf follow-up: inline tool-return synthesis should avoid scanning the full transcript on each streaming frame or replay path. Cache/index the needed tool-return state or move full scans to cold/reconcile paths.
acceptance_criteria: Inline tool-return synthesis hot path avoids full transcript scans; behavior remains correct for long tool-heavy conversations; regression coverage demonstrates per-frame work is bounded by new data or indexed lookup.
close_reason: Implemented in admin-shim PR #20 (commit 3ea7b68): inline tool-return synthesis now tail-scans messages.jsonl from the pre-turn boundary via listNewToolResultsSync instead of full transcript parse. 20k-message scale regression test added. Merged + deployed live.

title: Audit shim streaming/replay hot paths for unbounded work
description: Audit admin-shim hot paths that run per streamed frame, per subscribe/reconnect event, or per mobile cursor replay for accidental O(total run/conversation) work. The recent frames.jsonl subscribe regression showed that functionally-correct replay code can become O(n^2) only in long real conversations. Scope includes subscribeToRun, conversation cursor replay/stamping, run frame persistence, run summary/message mapping, listMessages usage in streaming paths, and any per-frame readFileSync/JSON.parse/filter/map/sort over full logs. Acceptance: identify and file/fix concrete hotspots; add or update tests/bench-style fixtures that simulate long runs/conversations and assert tail/replay work is proportional to new bytes/frames rather than total history; document safe streaming invariants for future changes.

title: Mobile channel: implement server-pushed sendMessage (proactive push) — the relay channel for fork/relay + the linchpin of non-blocking chat
description:
## The need
The companion fork/relay paradigm (letta-mobile-3aqu8, reference/companion_ui_paradigm.md) requires that when a background subagent (native Task) finishes, its result is PUSHED into the conversation even when the user is idle / no turn is active — the 'I'll take a look … [later] … btw, here's the result' relay. Emmanuel's architecture (correct): do NOT invent a new proactive-push primitive — TREAT IT AS A CHANNEL PUSH. Mobile is already modeled as a channel (home/.letta/channels/mobile/), and channels have a sendMessage/sendDirectReply adapter (Matrix's is fully implemented). The relay = the completion notification emitting via the mobile channel's sendMessage; the app receives it as an inbound channel message. No new tool/primitive — reuse the channel send path.

## The gap (pinpointed in code)
home/.letta/channels/mobile/plugin.mjs:
- line 45 comment: 'sendMessage hook is a no-op until Phase 3 introduces server-pushed [messages]'
- line 47  — NO-OP
- line 50  — NO-OP
- messageActions support() returns: 'mobile channel: send via adapter.sendMessage not supported in Phase 1'
So proactive push is explicitly a planned-but-UNBUILT phase. The mobile channel today only receives inbound + emits turn-responses; it cannot push an unprompted message to an idle app. Matrix's plugin.mjs HAS this (sendMessage/sendDirectReply implemented, lines ~230-262) — use it as the reference implementation.

## Confirmed working context (so this is the ONLY missing piece)
Verified live 2026-06-02: native Task fork + auto-injected completion notification reaches the AGENT's context through the shim fine (the relay mechanism works agent-side). What's missing is the AGENT → APP push for the idle case. Within an active turn the response already flows; the gap is strictly proactive/idle delivery.

## Work
1. Implement mobile channel sendMessage / sendDirectReply to deliver a server-pushed message over the /shim/v1/mobile WS to subscribed clients (and trigger a push/ntfy wake when the app is backgrounded, like the notification path).
2. Wire the fork-completion relay to call it: when a Task completion notification lands, surface it into the mobile channel as an inbound message (the 'btw…' relay) + the small animation cue.
3. Mirror Matrix's adapter contract; keep it channel-agnostic so the same path serves any future channel.

## Acceptance
- The agent can push an unprompted message into a mobile conversation when the user is idle, delivered to the app (foreground WS + background push wake).
- A completed background subagent relays its result into the chat with no user action, rendered as a normal inbound message + animation cue.
- Reuses the channel sendMessage abstraction — no bespoke proactive-push primitive.

## Refs
letta-mobile-3aqu8 (.3 non-blocking — this is its delivery linchpin; without it the relay degrades to 'seen next time you message'), lcp-xbvp (frame tagging — tag the pushed relay so the app styles it as 'btw…'), reference/companion_ui_paradigm.md, Matrix plugin.mjs (reference impl), lcp-gukg (same run-lifecycle neighborhood).
notes: PR #15 opened and green: https://github.com/oculairmedia/letta-code-admin-shim/pull/15. Commits: 2867d95 mobile adapter push registry + test; a46b2bb scheduler relay push wiring. Local verification: node --import tsx/esm --test test/mobile-channel-push.test.ts; npm run typecheck; npm test; npm run build. Retrieval: bd show lcp-cq7x && GIT_MASTER=1 git status --short --branch && gh pr view 15
close_reason: Implemented mobile channel push delivery, wired background scheduler relay frames over adapter.sendMessage, opened green PR #15.

## APP-SIDE VERIFIED (read letta-mobile source 2026-06-02): app needs NOTHING for the functional relay

Traced the app's WS ingestion path. The functional relay (pushed message appears even when user is idle) is ALREADY SUPPORTED — no app change needed:

- TimelineSyncStreamSubscriber.kt:25-26: 'Runs the PERSISTENT SSE stream subscriber for a single conversation.'

title: REGRESSION: Read-tool images no longer render inline on mobile (PNG + WebP both broken) — lcp-d780 regressed
description:
## Symptom (2026-06-02 ~18:40)
Images surfaced via the Read tool stopped rendering inline in the mobile chat tool card. Both formats fail:
- WebP (Mobbin reference screens saved to ~/.letta/skills/mcp-images/*.webp): no render.
- PNG (fresh adb screencap, 1280x2856 RGBA, 294KB): also no render.
So it is NOT format-specific — the whole Read-image inline-render path regressed. (Agent-side vision is fine: Reading the image into the agent's own multimodal context still works; only the mobile DISPLAY-back is broken.)

This was WORKING and verified on device earlier (lcp-d780 fix, shim commit 71a1897 + mobile 25ff3021). It has regressed.

## Strong suspicion: collateral from the in-flight lcp-gukg shim work
At the time of the regression, admin-shim had a large uncommitted working tree from another agent's lcp-gukg (turn stop_reason / run-lifecycle) work:
  M admin-shim/lib/agent-pool.ts, chat.ts, mobile-channel-host.ts, runs.ts, types/wire.ts + several tests
The image-attach logic lives in exactly those files (attachReadImageToToolReturn in mobile-channel-host.ts + chat.ts; tool_return synthesis in mobile-channel-host.ts). The lcp-gukg changes reworked stop_reason/terminal handling and the end-of-turn frame flush — which is the SAME path that synthesizes + emits tool_return frames (where Read images are attached). The shim was being rebuilt/restarted repeatedly during that work.

Verified the image-attach CALL SITES were not directly edited (git diff showed no image/d780 lines changed), so the regression is likely INDIRECT: the reworked terminal-state / tool_return flush ordering now drops or mis-times the image-bearing tool_return frame for completed turns.

## Diagnostic asks
- Compare tool_return frame emission for a Read-image turn BEFORE vs AFTER the lcp-gukg working-tree changes (git stash the lcp-gukg edits, rebuild, retest Read image render).
- Confirm whether the image tool_return frame is still emitted over WS at all (capture frames), or emitted but without the attached image content part, or emitted after the terminal stop so mobile ignores it.
- Check whether the new last-wins/terminal stop_reason flush at end-of-turn (mobile-channel-host.ts ~line 706 area) now races/precedes the inline tool_return synthesis that attaches the Read image.

## Repro
1. Read any image file via the Read tool on a mobile-connected conversation.
2. Expected: image renders inline in the tool card (tap-to-zoom).
3. Actual: no image renders (both PNG and WebP).

## Acceptance
- Read-tool images render inline again on mobile (PNG and WebP), as they did after lcp-d780.
- Add a regression guard (test/fixture) so the tool_return image-attach path is covered against future stop_reason/flush reworks.

## Refs
lcp-d780 (the original fix that regressed), lcp-gukg (suspected cause — concurrent shim turn-lifecycle work), system/language.md 'How I actually show images now' (the contract this breaks). Meridian relies on this path to show the user design references / screenshots — it is load-bearing for the current design-research work.

title: Mobile/shim: persistent 'thinking' run blocks new message — user must send twice (cancel then resend)
description:
## Symptom (reported 2026-06-02, recurring)
When the agent appears to be in a persistent 'thinking'/running state, the user cannot just send a new message — they have to send TWICE: the first send cancels the stuck/in-flight run, and the second send actually delivers the message. This is a recurring friction bug, not a one-off.

## Likely cause (hypotheses, ranked)
1. A run/turn is left in an active (non-terminal) state on the conversation — the agent shows 'thinking' but the run never cleanly finished, so the next send is interpreted as a cancel of the active run rather than a new user turn. (Related to the 'turn timed out' toast on long turns — the client display gives up but the server-side run/turn state isn't reconciled to terminal.)
2. The WS/transport send path treats a send-while-active as cancel-first, so the first message is consumed as the cancel signal and only the second creates a user message.
3. Stuck reasoning/thinking stream: the agent's thinking phase doesn't emit a terminal turn-done, so the conversation stays 'busy' (cf. 409 conversation busy semantics) and the client must clear it first.

## Repro
- Have a long/heavy turn (or one that hit the mobile 'turn timed out' toast).
- Try to send the next message.
- Observe: first send does nothing visible except clear the thinking/cancel the run; second send actually posts.

## Suspect surfaces
- letta-mobile send coordinator (WsChatSendCoordinator / TimelineWsSubscription externalTransportActive) — send-while-active handling.
- admin-shim mobile WS turn lifecycle — whether a turn is reconciled to terminal when the client times out / disconnects.
- Run/turn terminal-state reconciliation: is there a turn left 'in_progress' that blocks the next send?
- Relation to lcp-98y8 (turn timeout false-negative) and the mobile 'turn timed out' display gap (letta-mobile-xzhkm) — same family: client thinks turn ended, server state disagrees.

## Acceptance
- Sending a message while the agent appears to be 'thinking'/running either (a) cleanly queues/sends as one action, or (b) cancels-and-sends in a single user action — NEVER requires two separate sends.
- A stuck/timed-out thinking run is reconciled to terminal so it doesn't block the next user message.
- Add a diagnostic: surface the active run/turn state so we can tell whether a turn is genuinely in-flight vs orphaned.

## Diagnostic asks
- Capture the conversation's active run/turn state when the double-send happens (GET run status / the /context or conversation busy state).
- Determine whether the first send is being consumed as a cancel by the client or rejected as 409-busy by the shim.
close_reason: Fixed: completed auto-approved tool turns now summarize with the terminal stop_reason while per-step records preserve intermediate requires_approval stops.

comments.author: Claude Code
comments.text:
## Correction — precise mechanism (2026-06-02)

Reframe: this is NOT 'double send by design'. The real bug is a PHANTOM stuck in-progress turn on the CLIENT:

- The app keeps showing 'working / response coming' (turn appears in-progress) when the agent has actually finished.
- It HANGS FOREVER — no late response ever arrives. The indicator just never clears.
- Because the UI thinks a turn is active, the FIRST send tap is consumed as 'stop the (phantom) ongoing turn', and only the SECOND tap actually sends the message.
- It is INTERMITTENT — does not happen every turn (did not reproduce on the immediately following turn).

So the symptom is: client-side turn state gets stuck non-terminal with nothing actually streaming, and never reconciles to done. The 'two taps' is a downstream consequence (tap 1 = clear phantom active state, tap 2 = send).

## Refined root-cause hypotheses (ranked)
1. **Lost terminal frame**: the turn-done/terminal event (or final WS frame) is occasionally dropped/not applied on the client, so the timeline's active-turn flag is never cleared. Server-side the run is terminal; client never learns. (Intermittent => race/dropped-frame, not a deterministic logic bug.)
2. **WS frame race on turn completion**: terminal frame arrives interleaved/out-of-order with other frames and the reducer fails to flip the in-progress flag to done.
3. **externalTransportActive / send-coordinator flag** stuck true after a turn that completed, so the next send is treated as cancel-first.

NOT likely an orphaned server run that keeps streaming — since nothing ever arrives, it is a client display/state-reconciliation issue, not a genuinely-live run.

## Diagnostic asks (to catch the intermittent case)
- When it hangs: query the server-side run/turn state (is the run actually terminal while the client shows active?). If terminal server-side + active client-side => confirms lost-terminal-frame hypothesis.
- Log/inspect the timeline reducer's active-turn flag + the last WS frame received for that turn. Did a turn-done frame arrive? Was it applied?
- Check whether externalTransportActive (TimelineWsSubscription) is left true after the hung turn.

## Acceptance (refined)
- The client never gets stuck showing 'working/response coming' indefinitely when no response is streaming.
- Client turn state reconciles to terminal even if the terminal frame is dropped (e.g. a watchdog/timeout that probes server run state and clears the active flag, or REST reconcile on idle).
- Sending while the agent looks busy does not silently consume the first send as a cancel.

Related family: lcp-98y8 (turn timeout false-negative), letta-mobile-xzhkm (turn-timed-out display gap), 409 conversation-busy semantics.

comments.author: Claude Code
comments.text:
## LIVE CAPTURE (2026-06-02 21:17) — root cause is APPROVAL-RUN reconciliation, NOT a dropped terminal frame

Caught it live via GET /v1/runs?agent_id=...:
- run-d6ccd2b5 status=running stop=None (the current in-flight turn — 'working' was truthful at that instant)
- run-18359490 status=completed stop=requires_approval (the PRIOR turn — ended in a tool-APPROVAL gate)
- earlier runs: stop=end_turn (normal) and one stop=user_cancelled (a prior double-send clear)

Pattern: the hangs cluster on runs that stop with stop_reason=requires_approval. Plain end_turn turns do NOT hang. That explains the intermittency (only tool-approval turns hang) and 'didn't happen this time' (that was an end_turn turn).

## Refined root cause
Per the Letta connection contract: in background mode an approval creates a NEW run, and the tool_return lands on the APPROVAL run's stream — the original paused run will NOT deliver it. If the mobile client keeps waiting on the original paused (requires_approval) run, it hangs FOREVER with 'response coming' and nothing arrives. The first send tap cancels/clears that stuck paused run (see the user_cancelled run in history); the second tap sends.

So this is the approval-stream-cursor anti-pattern, NOT a dropped turn-done frame. The client must:
- open approval UI on approval_request_message
- approve/deny via tool_call_id
- then FOLLOW the approval run's stream for the tool_return + continuation, not wait on the original paused run

## Suspect surfaces (revised)
- letta-mobile approval handling: does it surface approval_request_message and switch its stream cursor to the approval run? (letta-mobile-iab2d territory)
- admin-shim mobile WS: when a run stops requires_approval, does it route the continuation/tool_return back over the same WS for the conversation, or onto a new run the client isn't subscribed to?
- If approvals are being auto-approved server-side, the continuation run's frames may never reach the client's active subscription.

## Decisive next diagnostic
Next hang: confirm the CURRENTLY-DISPLAYED-as-active turn's run has stop_reason=requires_approval and that there is a newer approval/continuation run the client is NOT subscribed to. If so, fix = client follows approval-run stream (or shim fans the continuation back onto the conversation WS).

## Acceptance (revised)
- A turn that hits requires_approval surfaces the approval prompt on mobile AND the client follows the approval run's stream so the continuation/tool_return arrives — no infinite 'working' hang.
- If no approval UI is intended (auto-approve), the shim must deliver the continuation run's frames over the conversation's active subscription.

comments.author: Claude Code
comments.text:
## CORRECTION 2 (2026-06-02 21:23) — runs stop requires_approval under UNRESTRICTED/auto-approve mode (the real cause)

Earlier I mis-said 'text-only turn'. The hung turn (run-d6ccd2b5, the 'Caught it live' response) DID run tools (bd comment + run-state curls) then emitted text. Message tail confirms: tool_call_message -> tool_return_message -> assistant_message.

Key facts from live capture:
- Permission mode is 'unrestricted — all tools auto-approved' (per the session reminder).
- YET run-d6ccd2b5 and run-18359490 both have stop_reason=requires_approval.
- Older runs (run-5738596f, run-3940a3c4) = stop_reason=end_turn (clean). One run = user_cancelled (a prior first-tap clear).
- The hung runs completed their assistant text (user sees the response) but the run terminated in requires_approval limbo instead of end_turn.

## Corrected root cause (two defects; #1 is the cause)
1. **Tool calls are hitting the approval gate even though permission mode is unrestricted/auto-approve.** Turns that should end_turn instead stop requires_approval. This is a server/shim/permission-config contradiction — the actual origin of the hang. The intermittency = only turns that invoke a gated tool path hit it; pure end_turn turns don't.
2. **The client never reconciles a requires_approval run that has no actionable/auto-approvable request**, so it shows 'response coming' forever. First send tap cancels the limbo run; second send delivers. (Defensive fix — should self-heal even if #1 is fixed.)

## Why this matters
The user already SEES my full text response, so it 'looks done', but the run is stuck pending-approval. So this is not a display-only bug — the run genuinely terminates in the wrong terminal state under auto-approve.

## Decisive diagnostics to run next hang
- Confirm the displayed-active run's stop_reason=requires_approval while permission mode=unrestricted.
- Identify WHICH tool call triggered the approval gate (was it a specific tool the auto-approve policy didn't cover — e.g. Bash, a write, an MCP call?). The approval policy may auto-approve some tools but not all even in 'unrestricted'.
- Check the shim/agent permission config: does 'unrestricted' actually map to auto-approve for ALL tool kinds, or are some still gated?

## Acceptance (corrected)
- Under unrestricted/auto-approve mode, tool calls do NOT produce requires_approval stops; turns end_turn normally.
- If a requires_approval stop occurs with no surfaced/actionable approval, the client reconciles it to terminal (no infinite 'response coming').

Supersedes the previous 'approval-run cursor' framing: the cursor issue is real for genuine approvals, but THIS hang is a spurious requires_approval under auto-approve.
