comments.text:
DISK-CONFIRMED — fix path is now actionable (2026-05-24 18:00 EDT)

Confirmed via direct inspection of the conv's messages.jsonl: the tool result IS persisted to disk even though it never crosses the WS. So the data exists; the WS layer simply doesn't surface it.

**Probe disk dump** (`migrator/out/conversations/<b64conv>/messages.jsonl` for the probe turn):

```
ui-msg-6478  role=user       (the prompt)
ui-msg-6479  role=assistant  (toolCall: Bash {command:"date && uptime", ...})
ui-msg-6480  role=toolResult toolCallId=toolu_01UCSezcD6e7pUNDbGoRarVt  content=["Sun May 24 05:50:24 PM EDT 2026\n 17:50:24 up 3 days, 16:29..."]
ui-msg-6481  role=assistant  (the reply text)
```

So the path forward is:

**Recommended fix shape:** the shim already has `subscribeToRun(runId, cursor, cbs)` infra (mobile-channel-host.ts:633). Extend the WS streaming layer to ALSO project new `role:"toolResult"` disk entries to wire `tool_return_message` frames as they appear after each auto_approval wire event. Specifically:

1. The shim's SDK adapter already sees the `auto_approval` wire event (currently dropped by the SDK pump, but VISIBLE on the transport — we can intercept it before the SDK pump filters)
2. After observing an `auto_approval` for tool_call_id X, the shim should:
   - Tail the conversation's messages.jsonl for the matching `role:"toolResult"` entry with `toolCallId=X`
   - Synthesize a `tool_return_message` wire frame from it
   - Push it through the same `onFrame` path the wire-shaped tool_return would have taken — chat.ts:reshapeFrame already knows that shape (lines 339-362)
3. This avoids any change to the SDK or to letta-code itself

Alternative cleaner option: instead of disk-tailing, register a stderr/control hook on the CLI subprocess that catches the `auto_approval` and queries the result via a control_request. But the disk path is already authoritative and reads are cheap.

**Bonus confirmation for lcp-wqy:** every disk entry's `metadata.created_at` is `2026-01-01T01:48:00.000Z` (and increments per message). So the Jan-1 timestamp leak is on disk too, not just the wire. The CLI's `--backend local` mode uses a deterministic monotonic clock and writes that to both the wire `date` field AND the persisted `metadata.created_at`. Fix needs to be at reshape/projection time on the shim: detect dates matching `^2026-01-01T` and replace with real timestamps, OR have the mobile UI fall back to receive-time when the date is suspiciously near the local-mode epoch.

**Status:** root cause is now triply confirmed (wire trace + disk dump + CLI source code). The fix is shim-side, doesn't need upstream changes, and the existing `subscribeToRun` machinery is the natural home. Ready for implementation in a follow-up session.

title: SessionManager.rebuild() not synchronized with current getter
description: rebuild() sets _currentGraph.value = next then cancels the old scope. The `current` getter is unsynchronized. A concurrent suspend call can capture current (session A), then rebuild() cancels session A's scope mid-operation. Practical impact is limited because most suspend functions run on the caller's coroutine context, not the repository's scope — but init-block coroutines get interrupted. Fix: use a Mutex or AtomicReference to synchronize rebuild() with current reads.
close_reason: All fixed in PR #212

title: Shared Room DAOs cause cross-session data leakage on backend switch
description: SessionGraphFactory injects the same singleton AgentDao/ConversationDao into every SessionGraph. On backend switch, the new session's repository loads stale data from Room (written by the previous session) before refreshAgents() overwrites it. Brief window where UI shows agents/conversations from the wrong backend. Fix: either clear the Room tables on session switch, or use a session-scoped qualifier on the DAO data so stale rows are ignored.
close_reason: All fixed in PR #212

title: TOCTOU race: current-delegated suspend functions orphan writes on session switch
description: All SessionScoped* wrappers delegate suspend functions through a `current` property snapshot: `override suspend fun refreshAgents() = current.refreshAgents()`. If rebuild() fires mid-flight, the mutation completes against the old session's state — the result is written to session A's StateFlow but flatMapLatest has already switched the UI to session B. The write is silently lost. Dangerous for createAgent(), createConversation(), deleteAgent() — the server-side effect persists but the UI never reflects it. Fix: capture the session graph reference at call start and verify it's still current before committing results, or use a session-aware coordinator that discards stale completions.
close_reason: All fixed in PR #212

title: a2ui-adapter clobbers agent-curated system/a2ui_protocol.md on every process start
description:
## Summary

`ensureA2uiBlockAttached()` in `admin-shim/lib/a2ui-adapter.ts` writes a synthetic `<storageDir>/memfs/<agent>/memory/system/a2ui_protocol.md` from the in-memory `buildA2uiBlockContent()` template whenever the on-disk file content differs. This destroys any agent-curated edits to that file the next time the shim attaches the block (once per process per agent).

## Where

- `admin-shim/lib/a2ui-adapter.ts:262` — `ensureA2uiBlockAttached(agentId)`
- `admin-shim/lib/a2ui-adapter.ts:269-272` — read existing, write if differs, no merge

## Failure mode

The template is treated as canonical. Any drift on disk (including drift caused by the agent itself correcting bugs in the template, refining examples, or annotating current bd state) is reverted on next shim startup with that agent loaded. Symptoms include:

- **Component shape examples wiped.** The template still contains the WRONG shape `{ id: "rootCard", Card: { child: "greeting" } }` at a2ui-adapter.ts:215. The agent learns the correct flat-discriminator shape `{ id, component, ...props }` on first use, edits the memory file, then the shim clobbers it back to the broken shape.
- Profile rule corrections wiped.
- Current bd status annotations (open bugs, recent PRs) wiped.
- Expanded-catalog acknowledgments wiped — template still advertises the original 18 widgets even though renderer landed list templates / form widgets / numeric inputs / dropdown / chip+badge / tabs+accordion / schedule-catalog widgets May 18-19, 2026.

## Evidence

Memory git log on the affected file (in agent memfs repo):

```
926b4d6 refresh: a2ui_protocol — current bd status (mvon + 92wq closed, c3h4/16li in_progress, xhkw added)
46d2033 fix: a2ui_protocol — correct component shape + acknowledge expanded catalog
f22868d Fix catalogId — shim wants negotiated string "basic", not the full URL
47ae968 pickup: add frontmatter to a2ui_protocol.md
```

Every one of those commits is the agent correcting drift from the synthetic template. The clobber happened immediately before this session's `memory(create)` call landed, requiring a `git checkout` to restore the curated content. Observed live 2026-05-23.

## Why this is P1

It's an **agent identity bug**. The agent learns the real shape of the protocol from production failures (validation warnings, mobile renderer rejections), writes the lesson into memory, and the shim systematically destroys the lesson. The agent then re-learns the same lesson next session — wasted work, wasted tokens, and degraded mobile UX forever because the broken example keeps regenerating.

It also poisons memfs git history: every clobber-then-restore cycle creates noise commits.

## Proposed fix shape

Pick one, in order of preference:

1. **Don't overwrite an existing file at all.** Write canonical content only if file doesn't exist, then never touch it again. Agents own their memory; the shim's responsibility ends at scaffolding.
2. **Write to a different filename** (e.g. `system/a2ui_protocol.shim.md` or `system/_generated/a2ui_protocol.md`) and let the agent author the human-curated companion. Two files, two ownerships, no collision.
3. **Add a frontmatter marker** like `shim-managed: true` and only overwrite files carrying that marker. Once the agent edits and removes the marker, the file becomes agent-owned.
4. **Diff-and-merge** instead of overwrite — harder, probably not worth it.

Recommend (1). The shim already gates on `a2uiBlockAttachedAgents` Set per-process for in-memory dedupe; making the disk write strictly create-not-update is one line.

## Bonus: fix the template too

While we're here, update `buildA2uiBlockContent()` to use the correct component shape (`{ id, component, ...props }`, NOT `{ id, Card: { ... } }`) so newly-bootstrapped agents start with valid examples:

- `{ id: "root", component: "Card", child: "col" }`
- Buttons require `child` (Text/Icon ID) + `action: { event: { name, context } }`
- catalogId must be the negotiated string (`"basic"`), NOT the full URL
- Surface envelope is `{ surfaceId, catalogId }` at top level of `createSurface`, not nested `{ surface: { id, root } }`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `ensureA2uiBlockAttached` no longer overwrites an existing on-disk `system/a2ui_protocol.md`
- [ ] Template content in `buildA2uiBlockContent()` updated to correct component shape + catalogId guidance + correct createSurface envelope
- [ ] Document the ownership model: agent owns the file post-bootstrap; shim never re-asserts

## Linked context

- Memory file path: `$MEMORY_DIR/system/a2ui_protocol.md` (in agent memfs repo)
- Memory commits 47ae968, f22868d, 46d2033, 926b4d6 — all are agent-side corrections of shim-generated content
- A2UI initiative epic context: lcp-uo5.x series
close_reason: ensureA2uiBlockAttached changed to write-if-absent only; template shape corrected to flat-discriminator format

comments.author: root
comments.text:
## Diagnosis update — root cause is broader than initially reported

After tracing call sites I found:

1. **The original "clobber the agent's memory file" callsite was already removed yesterday.** Commit `ead1c0c` (lcp-sdk.10, May 22) excised the subprocess transport and dropped both the import and the call in `agent-pool.ts`:

   ```
   -import { augmentUserInputForA2ui, ensureA2uiBlockAttached, type A2uiCapability } from "./a2ui-adapter.js";
   +import { type A2uiCapability } from "./a2ui-adapter.js";
   ```

   So the clobber behavior I observed at the start of this session was the result of a shim run **from before May 22** writing stale content to disk. Today's `git checkout` restored the curated version, and nothing has re-clobbered it since.

2. **Both A2UI bootstrap functions are now dead code.** `ensureA2uiBlockAttached` and `augmentUserInputForA2ui` have zero live callers in the shim. They were orphaned by the SDK migration (`lcp-sdk.10`) along with the subprocess transport.

3. **The SDK adapter does NOT re-implement the bootstrap.** `letta-sdk-adapter.ts` receives `a2uiCapability` and stashes it on the adapter (used for approval-related code paths at line 399+), but does **not**:
   - call `ensureA2uiBlockAttached(agentId)` to ensure the `system/a2ui_protocol.md` memory file exists
   - call `augmentUserInputForA2ui()` to inject the per-turn A2UI hint

   So **A2UI bootstrap is currently broken on freshly-provisioned agents on the SDK path.** Existing agents (like Meridian) have the file in their memfs from the pre-sdk.10 era so they're unaffected, but new agents will never get the scaffold.

## Revised scope

This bead now covers two related issues:

### A. The original clobber bug (now historical but fixable for safety)
- Even though no callsite hits it today, `ensureA2uiBlockAttached` still uses overwrite-on-mismatch semantics.
- If any future caller is added, it will re-introduce the agent-memory-clobber bug.
- Fix: change to **write-if-absent only** so that even if the function gets re-wired, it can't destroy agent edits. (Done in this branch.)
- Also: fix the in-template examples that still use wrong shape (`Text.value` should be `Text.text`, `updateComponents.surface` should be `surfaceId`, `deleteSurface.surface` should be `surfaceId`, `createSurface` should NOT include `components`). (Done.)

### B. A2UI bootstrap is broken on the SDK adapter path
- New agents created post-lcp-sdk.10 don't get `system/a2ui_protocol.md` scaffolded.
- Per-turn A2UI prompt augmentation is also not running (though the `system/*` file is the durable source of truth, and `augmentUserInputForA2ui` is currently a no-op anyway per the existing comments — check this).
- Fix: re-wire `ensureA2uiBlockAttached` in the SDK adapter at the point where `currentA2uiCapability` is set (around `letta-sdk-adapter.ts:246`).

## Updated proposal

1. Land the write-if-absent + template fix in this branch (defense in depth, even though no callsite hits it today).
2. Re-wire `ensureA2uiBlockAttached` from `SdkBackedLettaSessionAdapter._runTurnInner` so the bootstrap actually happens for new agents on the SDK path. Spec: call it once per (agent, capability presence) — capability-gate so non-A2UI clients don't scaffold the file.
3. Update tests in `test/a2ui-adapter.test.ts` to cover the new write-if-absent behavior.

## Acceptance criteria (revised)

- [x] `ensureA2uiBlockAttached` no longer overwrites an existing on-disk file
- [x] Template examples corrected
- [ ] `ensureA2uiBlockAttached` is wired into the SDK adapter path so new agents get scaffolded
- [ ] Tests cover both first-time scaffold AND no-op on existing file
- [ ] Document the ownership model: agent owns the file post-bootstrap; shim never re-asserts

## What this session committed already

Both A. fixes (write-if-absent + template correction) are in the working tree as edits to `admin-shim/lib/a2ui-adapter.ts`. Not yet committed. B. (SDK adapter re-wire) is queued.

title: lcp-LET-9054: patch letta-code's executeConversationTurn settle to pass agentId (load-time mutation in SDK wrapper)
description: Upstream letta-code bug (v0.26.1, letta.js:196391): `this.store.settleInterruptedToolCalls(conversationId, { reason: TURN_DID_NOT_COMPLETE })` omits agentId. For conversationId="default", toolSettlementTargets falls back to findConversation("default") which looks up key default:<defaultAgentId>=agent-local-default. Migrated agents (agent-<uuid>) miss this lookup and settle silently no-ops — leaving orphan tool_use messages on disk forever. Every subsequent turn fails Anthropic validation: 'tool_use ids were found without tool_result blocks immediately after'. Meridian was the trigger case (35 orphans, 8-iter cascade heal). The clean fix is a runtime patch in our letta-cli-sdk-wrapper.mjs: install a Node --import loader that string-replaces the buggy call site to pass agentId: body.agent_id. Sits at the same layer as the --backend local injection, fixes upstream's bug without forking, and the upstream's own settleInterruptedToolCallsForConversation then takes care of synthesizing the error tool_result records on every turn boundary.
design: Approach: ESM loader hook via module.register() / --import file://<loader>. Loader exports a load(url, ctx, nextLoad) hook that, when url matches LETTA_CLI_PATH_REAL, reads the source via nextLoad, applies a literal string replacement at the bug site, returns the patched source. String replacement must be exact-match — if the source doesn't contain the expected literal (letta-code version drift), the loader logs a warning and returns the original source unchanged (fail-safe, never block startup). The wrapper appends '--import file://<absolute-loader-path>' to the node args. Patched call site: { agentId: body.agent_id ?? this.store?.resolveAgentIdForConversation?.(conversationId), reason: TURN_DID_NOT_COMPLETE }.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Loader runs at letta.js load time and applies the patch (verifiable by logging line). 2) When the source doesn't contain the expected literal, loader logs a warning and falls back to original. 3) End-to-end: send a turn through the SDK adapter against Meridian's conv — orphan toolu_01Ebk... gets a synthetic error tool_result on the next turn boundary, and the subsequent Anthropic call succeeds. 4) Regression: turn against an agent-local-default agent still works (the patch is benign when agentId resolution already succeeds). 5) Loader file lives at admin-shim/scripts/letta-code-settle-patch-loader.mjs and is referenced by wrapper via absolute path resolved from import.meta.url.
close_reason: upstream settle agentId patch landed via Node --import loader; verified against Meridian (settle synthesized expected toolResult for orphan)

title: Wire conversation-healer auto-recovery into the turn driver
description: conversation-healer.ts (lcp-ezv) implements detection + healing in isolation, but is not yet invoked automatically. Add a hook in the SDK adapter's post-result path: when result.success===false and detectDanglingToolUses(...) returns ids, the shim should DRAIN the affected pool entry, apply healConversation, restart the session, and retry the turn ONCE. If the retry also fails with dangling ids, log + return a structured turn_done(status:failed, error_code:transcript_unhealable) so mobile sees a clear terminal state.
design: Operational caveat from lcp-ezv validation: the heal must run while NO CLI session is alive for the target conversation. The shim's pool keeps long-running letta-code sessions that load messages.jsonl on init and write back at end-of-turn; healing the disk while a session is alive causes that session's stale in-memory state to clobber the heal at end-of-turn. Integration plan: (1) Detect in SDK adapter when result frame carries stop_reason='error' with the dangling-tool-use signature. (2) Call pool.evict(conversationId, agentId) to close the active SDK session (adapter.close() + remove from workers map). (3) Loop: applyHeal → spawn fresh CLI via the SDK to retry → repeat until either success or no progress. Cap iterations at SHIM_HEAL_MAX_ITER (default 5) — Meridian's case took 7-8, so the default should be higher OR no-progress check should kick in. (4) Audit every iter to state/runs/<runId>/heal.jsonl (already wired). (5) Mobile-visible: emit a synthetic turn_started for the retry attempts so mobile lifecycle stays clean.
acceptance_criteria: 1) SDK adapter detects dangling-tool-use error and triggers heal+retry automatically. 2) Pool entry is drained before heal so the disk edit isn't clobbered. 3) Cascade heal converges within SHIM_HEAL_MAX_ITER attempts; structured failure if it doesn't. 4) Mobile sees a single turn_done at the end (success after recovery, or failed with error_code if unrecoverable). 5) Test exercises both the success path and the max-iter-exceeded path. 6) heal.jsonl audit covers every iteration.
close_reason: Merged in PR #3: turn driver now routes through runTurnWithHeal with adapter eviction and conversation-healer recovery.

title: Synthetic settlement on tool-call interrupt or cancel
description: Specific tactic from the 'persist tool_call and tool_return as a matched pair' invariant. When a tool_call_message has been emitted to disk and the turn is interrupted (mobile cancel, REST cancel, worker SIGTERM, watchdog timeout, stream drop) BEFORE the corresponding tool_return_message lands, the shim must synthesize a tool_return record with status='error' / 'cancelled' / 'interrupted' and content='Tool execution interrupted by <reason>.' Without this, partial turns leak dangling tool_use into messages.jsonl and break every subsequent API call (see lcp-ezv for the manifesting failure mode).
design: Track per-turn the set of emitted-but-not-returned tool_call_ids. Apply on every interruption path in agent-pool.ts / letta-sdk-adapter.ts and chat.ts cancel handlers: (a) before finalizeTurnLifecycle runs after a cancelled/dead/timeout turn, scan frames[] for tool_call_message frames whose tool_call_id has no matching tool_return_message frame in the same turn; (b) append a synthetic LocalMessage with role='toolResult', toolCallId=<id>, isError=true, content text=interruption-reason to messages.jsonl for each. Source the reason from turnResult: 'cancelled by user' / 'turn timeout' / 'worker exit'. Auditable via state/runs/<id>/settlements.jsonl with timestamps.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Cancel a turn between tool_call_message and tool_return_message; verify a synthetic error toolResult lands on disk for each dangling tool_call_id. 2) Same for watchdog timeout, worker exit, and stream drop. 3) Synthetic settlements appear in state/runs/<id>/settlements.jsonl. 4) After settlement, the next turn on the same conv succeeds without invoking the lcp-ezv healer (preventive). 5) Tests cover each interruption path.
close_reason: settleDanglingToolCallsFromFrames wired into finalizeTurnLifecycle; 6 unit tests pass; full suite green

title: Auto-heal conversations with dangling tool_use blocks
description: Recovery for the recurring failure mode: Anthropic API rejects requests with invalid_request_error 'tool_use ids were found without tool_result blocks immediately after' even when messages.jsonl on disk has matching toolResult records for every toolCall. Letta-code's context-window serializer drops toolResult-role messages while keeping the preceding assistant message with tool_use blocks, leaving the API call with dangling tool_use ids. Affects long-running conversations (e.g. Meridian default — 613 messages, 270 tool calls, observed 2026-05-22 during lcp-sdk.9 smoke). Conversation is permanently unusable until manually patched. The shim must detect this pattern and self-heal.
design: Frame the conversation transcript as an append-only state machine with invariants (per upstream guidance 2026-05-22), not a best-effort chat log. Tool calls create obligations; every runtime/client must either fulfill or explicitly settle them before another turn is allowed. Detection: hook into the turn driver's post-result path. When result.stop_reason='error' and result carries an Anthropic invalid_request_error matching 'tool_use ids were found without tool_result blocks immediately after', extract the dangling tool_use ids via regex. Recovery preference order (per upstream — surgical mutation of hidden history is dangerous unless schema is fully understood): (a) settle by appending synthetic error tool_return records for each orphaned tool_call_id ('Tool execution interrupted; no result available'). (b) only if settlement fails or cannot be applied (e.g. the toolResult already exists on disk but is being dropped by serialization), fall through to fork-the-conversation: clone the agent's useful memory into a fresh conversation and route mobile there. (c) hard deletion of orphaned assistant tool_use records is LAST RESORT and must be audited. Retry the same turn once after recovery; if it errors AGAIN with the same pattern, log + give up (avoid loops). Idempotent — repeated calls with no work just propagate.
acceptance_criteria: 1) The shim detects Anthropic invalid_request_error matching the dangling-tool_use pattern on stop_reason=error. 2) Healer strips orphan toolCall parts + their toolResult messages from messages.jsonl atomically. 3) Original turn is retried automatically; retry succeeds for the Meridian default case observed in the smoke. 4) No infinite-loop: a second consecutive same-error short-circuits with a logged turn_done(status:failed). 5) Test: seed a conv with a dangling tool_use, drive a turn, assert healer fires + retry produces an assistant_message. 6) No silent data loss: heal events log to state/runs/<id>/heal.jsonl with before/after diff so the action is auditable.
close_reason: Closed

title: Idle-evict heartbeat: bump lastUsedAt per inbound frame
description: Pre-existing uncommitted changes to admin-shim/lib/agent-pool.ts (DirectSubprocessLettaSessionAdapter) and admin-shim/lib/letta-sdk-adapter.ts (SdkBackedLettaSessionAdapter) heartbeat lastUsedAt on every inbound frame, not just at turn start/end. Comment cites '56 idle-evictions in a single log session, each killing an in-flight turn' — any turn longer than SHIM_POOL_IDLE_SEC (default 300s) was getting SIGTERMed mid-stream by the pool housekeeper. Both adapters fixed symmetrically. Needs a bead + commit.
close_reason: Two-layer fix: (1) Added 'busy' getter on SdkBackedLettaSessionAdapter — returns true while a turn is in flight (currentRunHandle !== null). housekeep() skips eviction for busy adapters regardless of lastUsedAt staleness. (2) Added pool.touch(convId, agentId) method exposed as host.touchAdapter on the WS handler. Every inbound WS frame (pong, user_action, etc.) now bumps the adapter's lastUsedAt, keeping it alive as long as a mobile client is connected. Both layers are defense-in-depth: busy prevents mid-turn kill, touch prevents idle eviction between turns.

title: shim: SSE keep-alive on /v1/conversations/:id/stream had no duration cap; pool housekeeper killed in-flight turns
description:
Two related bugs in admin-shim that combined to make conversations appear to crash from the user's seat: a streaming POST that sat open for 20-78 minutes with no agent reply.

## Bug 1: /v1/conversations/:id/stream had no max duration

server.ts:650 (handleConversationStream) opens an SSE keep-alive that pings every 25s and only closes on req.on('close'). No max-duration cap. When the underlying socket goes into a half-closed state (Android backgrounding, NAT timeout, wifi flap), the request stays alive on the server side until something at the kernel/proxy layer finally tears it down.

Evidence from /tmp/admin-shim.log on prod shim (PID 1218170, 2026-05-22):
- 202 of 301 POSTs (67%) took >60s
- Multiple POSTs sitting open for 20-78 minutes before unwinding
- Six requests all returned at the EXACT same wall-clock instant (21:18:46.94x) which is a server-side socket cleanup sweep, not graceful response completion
- ~46-minute hang observed on Meridian's own conversation (conv-a2a583b3-...)

## Bug 2: agent-pool idle reaper killed long in-flight turns

agent-pool.ts:1085 checks 'now - lastUsedAt > IDLE_EVICT_MS' (default 300s). lastUsedAt is stamped at turn start (line 670) and turn end (line 894), but NOT updated during the turn. Any turn longer than 5 minutes gets its worker SIGTERMed mid-stream.

Evidence: 56 idle-evictions in the prod log session, one of which hit Meridian's own conversation at 20:37:32 mid-turn ('evicting (idle) conv=...a2a583b3... idle=320.69s'). The frameHandler traps __exit__ and the turn-resolve path mostly handles it, but the SSE shim has no shared state with the pool, so it stays open even after the worker is gone.

## Fixes (landed in working tree on branch a2ui-stream-splitter, not yet committed/deployed)

1. admin-shim/server.ts handleConversationStream: hard cap via setTimeout(60s) calling res.end(). Env tunable via SHIM_STREAM_MAX_MS.
2. admin-shim/lib/agent-pool.ts collector: this.lastUsedAt = Date.now() on every inbound frame.
3. admin-shim/lib/letta-sdk-adapter.ts stream loop: mirror heartbeat for SDK transport parity.

TypeScript clean, dist rebuilt. Production shim PID 1218170 still on old build — needs restart to pick up the fix.
acceptance_criteria:
1. No SSE POST to /v1/conversations/:id/stream stays open longer than SHIM_STREAM_MAX_MS (default 60s).
2. Workers actively producing frames are NOT idle-evicted by housekeep() regardless of total turn duration.
3. Production shim restarted onto rebuilt dist; admin-shim.log shows POST durations bounded near the cap.
4. No regression in existing test suite (excluding the pre-existing sdk-conversation-stability.test.ts failures, which are an independent SDK-transport bug).
notes:
Discovered while diagnosing Emmanuel's report 'conversations seem to be crashing at a certain point after which no answer is received from the agent' on 2026-05-22.

Related but independent: sdk-conversation-stability.test.ts (untracked test file in the same tree) fails on turn 2+ with 'expected turn_done in []' — matches the run_id-filter hazard the letta-mock.mjs comment describes for SHIM_LETTA_TRANSPORT=sdk. The production shim is currently on direct transport (no SHIM_LETTA_TRANSPORT set) so this is not what was hitting the user, but should be tracked separately before flipping the SDK flag.

title: Shim: last_message_at/updated_at not bumped on message append
description: Conversation metadata (last_message_at, updated_at) is not updated when new messages are appended via the shim's message-write path. Concrete repro: conv-268193bb-df18-4f6a-a0a8-86808e7ae097 has 167 messages on disk with mtime 2026-05-22 09:23 EDT and a real assistant reply at 2026-05-22T13:20:52Z, but the shim's conversation list endpoint reports last_message_at=2026-01-01T01:13:27.000Z (a Jan-1 placeholder). Because the app sorts conversations by last_message_at, this buries live conversations at the bottom of the list and makes them look deleted/missing. Per-message storage is correct; only the parent conversation.json (and the in-memory index backing GET /v1/conversations) is stale. The _real-times.json side-table present in each conv dir is likely the file the shim should be deriving these timestamps from. Fix: in the message-append code path in admin-shim/server.ts, bump last_message_at and updated_at on the parent conversation record (both on-disk JSON and in-memory cache invalidation, similar to lcp-5ky's last_message_at cache invalidation work).
acceptance_criteria: After appending a message to a conversation, GET /v1/conversations returns last_message_at and updated_at matching the new message's timestamp; existing conversations with Jan-1 placeholder metadata are healed on next append; mobile/web app sorts the conversation to the top of the list as expected.
close_reason: Fixed via read-time substitution from _real-times.json sidecar. Root cause was a ~4s write race: shim's bumpConversationLastMessageAt (lcp-pwz) wrote the real timestamp, then letta-code's in-process LocalStore rewrote conversation.json with sentinel dates post-turn. Patched admin-shim/lib/store.ts: new withRealTimes() helper substitutes last_message_at/updated_at from the sidecar max in listAllConversations, listConversationsForAgent (now async), and getConversation. Cache invalidation moved into stampNewMessages so it fires independent of the write race. bumpConversationLastMessageAt kept as best-effort persistence. Self-healing — verified on conv-268193bb-df18-4f6a-a0a8-86808e7ae097 (last_message_at went from 2026-01-01T01:13:27 to the real 2026-05-22T13:20:52 after restart). Regression test lcp-dfz added; 323/323 pass.

title: Admin-shim: capability metadata exposed on /v1/health/ per upstream
description:
Mobile's CapabilityRepository (letta-mobile-7y1zb.2) probes capabilities per workspace. For shim-fronted workspaces, the source of truth is the shim itself — it knows which upstream(s) it talks to and what it layers on top.

**Shim should expose on GET /v1/health/:**
- `shim_version` — for client compat checks
- `upstreams` — list of { mode: local-cli | remote-proxy, base_url, status }
- `capabilities` — { a2ui_dispatch, approval_gate, mobile_ws, cron, local_mcp_reach } per upstream mode
- `agent_origin_map` (optional, may be too expensive at probe time) — quick lookup of agent → upstream

**Why centralize at shim:** the capability picture for a shim-fronted workspace depends on shim's configuration (which upstreams attached, which features enabled), not just the upstream itself. Mobile probing api.letta.com directly cannot detect that A2UI is available 'because the shim adds it.'

**Reference:** $MEMORY_DIR/system/letta_cloud_unification.md (Headline architecture — capability negotiation per workspace, capabilities exposed by the layer that provides them).
acceptance_criteria:
- GET /v1/health/ returns full capability metadata
- Mobile CapabilityRepository can consume health JSON to populate capability flags
- Capability differences between local-CLI and remote-proxy modes correctly reflected
- Health endpoint authenticated (don't leak topology to unauthorized callers)

title: Admin-shim: bearer-token forwarding with per-workspace scoping (no cross-pollination)
description:
When the shim proxies to a remote Letta upstream, it must forward the bearer token belonging to that workspace — and ONLY that workspace.

**Security requirements:**
- Bearer tokens stored per workspace, not globally
- Tokens never logged (existing sanitizeHeader pattern in mobile applies here too)
- Cross-workspace requests in the same shim instance use isolated token contexts
- Token refresh / invalidation per workspace (if/when Letta supports OAuth in future)

**Implementation:**
- Workspace config carries { workspaceId, upstreamUrl, bearerToken }
- Request context propagates workspaceId through the routing path (lcp-9he.2)
- UpstreamLetta adapter looks up token by workspaceId at request time
- Health endpoint redacts token in any debug output

**Per Ezra ($MEMORY_DIR/system/letta_cloud_unification.md §1):** assume {base_url, bearer_token} for now. No OAuth roadmap to design against.
acceptance_criteria:
- Two workspaces with different bearer tokens can coexist in one shim instance
- Logs never contain raw bearer tokens
- Token revocation / change in one workspace doesn't affect the other
- Request context carries workspaceId end-to-end

title: Admin-shim: approval gate layered on remote-proxy responses
description:
Approval gate work (lcp-uo5.x) currently assumes a single Letta upstream. Phase 2 requires approval to work uniformly across local-CLI agents AND Cloud-proxied agents.

**Per Ezra ($MEMORY_DIR/system/letta_connection_contract.md):**
- HITL approval is triggered by approval_request_message (NOT stop_reason)
- Approve / deny is keyed on tool_call_id (canonical)
- In background mode, approval creates a NEW run_id; tool_return_message lands on the approval run's stream, NOT the original paused run
- ConversationStateHolder needs primaryRun + approvalRuns list shape

**Phase 2 implementation:**
- Approval interceptor sits in the proxy pipeline (after UpstreamLetta adapter)
- Detects approval_request_message in upstream stream → routes to mobile approval UI
- Mobile decision → shim sends approve/deny back to upstream using tool_call_id
- Tool return arrives on approval run's stream → shim merges into mobile's primary timeline view (mobile shouldn't need to know about two runs unless we expose it)

**Per-workspace bearer:** approval decisions must go back through the SAME workspace + auth context that originated the approval request. Workspace ID propagated end-to-end through the approval event.

**Reference:** $MEMORY_DIR/system/letta_connection_contract.md (rules 4 + follow-up Q&A on approval run-switching).
acceptance_criteria:
- Cloud-proxied agent triggering tool call with approval policy raises approval UI on mobile
- Mobile approve/deny sends correct tool_call_id to upstream (not approval_request_id)
- Tool return from approval run merged into mobile timeline view
- Workspace identity preserved through approval round-trip
- E2E test: Cloud agent with HITL tool, approve from mobile, verify tool executes

title: Admin-shim: A2UI stream-splitter layered on remote-proxy responses
description:
The existing a2ui-stream-splitter (lib/a2ui-stream-splitter.ts) works on local-CLI assistant output. Phase 2 needs it to also work on Cloud-proxied assistant output, so Cloud agents that emit <a2ui-json> blocks render as native Compose UI on mobile.

**Today:** stream splitter is wired into the local-CLI path. Cloud-proxied responses bypass it.

**Wanted:** when a request routes to remote-proxy (lcp-9he.2), the response stream is piped through the same a2ui-stream-splitter before being framed for mobile WS.

**Implementation:**
- In UpstreamLetta adapter (lcp-9he.1), wrap the response SSE consumer with a2ui-stream-splitter middleware
- Same dispatch logic: detect <a2ui-json> envelopes, route to A2UI dispatcher, strip from text stream
- Mobile receives identical frame format regardless of upstream

**Capability dependency:** mobile's a2ui_dispatch capability flag (letta-mobile-7y1zb.2) reflects 'shim is in front' not 'agent is local'. Cloud-proxied agents through shim → a2ui_dispatch=true. Direct Cloud (no shim) → a2ui_dispatch=false.

**Reference:** $MEMORY_DIR/system/a2ui_protocol.md (component shape, ordering rules — must survive proxy intact).
acceptance_criteria:
- Cloud-proxied agent emitting <a2ui-json> renders correctly on mobile
- Surface lifecycle (createSurface, updateComponents, deleteSurface) works through proxy
- A2UI capability advertised in shim /v1/health/ regardless of upstream
- E2E test: Cloud agent emits A2UI through shim, mobile renders

title: Admin-shim: per-request routing — local-CLI vs remote-proxy
description:
Once the shim supports both upstream modes (lcp-9he.1), it needs to decide per-request which upstream to use.

**Routing inputs:**
- Agent ID — agents created via local Letta Code spawn → local-CLI. Agents existing on the Cloud upstream → remote-proxy.
- Workspace config — request carries workspace identity (which upstream URL + bearer token).
- Request type — health/capabilities probes may need both upstreams.

**Routing strategy:**
- On startup, shim enumerates known agents from each configured upstream (local CLI agent registry + remote /v1/agents call)
- Maintains an agent→upstream map, refreshed periodically or on cache miss
- New agent creation requests route based on user intent (request body indicates target workspace)
- Conversation continuation routes to whichever upstream owns the agent

**Per-workspace bearer token isolation:** when proxying to remote, use the bearer token attached to the workspace that owns the target agent. Never cross-pollinate tokens.
acceptance_criteria:
- Agent lookup correctly returns upstream-of-record for any known agent
- Routing decision logged per request (for debugging)
- New conversations on existing Cloud agents route to remote-proxy
- New conversations on local agents route to local-CLI
- Mixed workload (some local + some Cloud agents) works in same shim instance

title: Admin-shim: add remote-Letta upstream mode alongside local-CLI
description:
Today admin-shim is a local-Letta-Code-CLI multiplexer. It spawns letta children via LETTA_BIN (lib/agent-pool.ts, lib/chat.ts). It has zero notion of a remote Letta HTTP API.

**Add a second upstream mode: 'remote-proxy'.**

The shim must be configurable to accept a remote Letta base_url + bearer token, then forward HTTP+SSE requests to that upstream while preserving:
- agent / conversation targeting
- ordered stream event delivery
- run cursor / resume (run_id + seq_id, background mode)
- approval messages (approval_request_message, tool_call_id-keyed responses)
- cancellation
- raw error visibility

**Implementation surface:**
- New `UpstreamLetta` adapter interface (parallel to existing LettaSessionAdapter for CLI)
- HTTP/2-friendly Fetch + SSE consumer
- Bearer token forwarding from request context
- Per-conversation upstream stream management (one per active conversation, multiplexed onto our mobile WS frame format)

**Reference:** $MEMORY_DIR/system/letta_connection_contract.md (rule 6 — shim MUST preserve all the above through proxy). $MEMORY_DIR/system/letta_cloud_unification.md (admin-shim is the right place for capability negotiation).
acceptance_criteria:
- New UpstreamLetta adapter implemented with same interface contract as local-CLI adapter
- HTTP+SSE proxying preserves stream order and event types end-to-end
- Bearer token forwarded per request, never logged
- Cancellation propagates upstream
- Errors surface raw to mobile (no flattening)
- Test against actual api.letta.com endpoint

title: GA Epic B: Phase 2 — shim-proxied developer mode (Cloud + local)
description:
Phase 2 of unifying Letta Cloud + self-hosted. Builds on Phase 1 (mobile direct to Cloud).

**Goal:** user installs Letta Code + admin-shim alongside the mobile app. Points mobile at the shim instead of api.letta.com. **Shim proxies to Letta Cloud upstream** so their existing Cloud agents still appear — no UX rupture. Shim layers on A2UI, approval gate, mobile WS, local MCP, cron, agent-pool.

**The critical change:** admin-shim today is a local-Letta-Code-CLI multiplexer (spawns letta children). Phase 2 makes it a **dual-upstream gateway**:
  1. Local CLI mode (current) — spawn letta child per (agent, conversation)
  2. Remote proxy mode (new) — forward HTTP+SSE to api.letta.com (or any Letta server) with user's bearer token, layer our envelope on top

**Per-request routing:** decide local-CLI vs remote-proxy based on agent origin. User's Cloud-configured agents → remote-proxy. User's locally-spawned Letta Code agents → local CLI. Both appear in the same mobile UI.

**Reference:** $MEMORY_DIR/system/letta_cloud_unification.md (Ezra 2026-05-22 guidance), $MEMORY_DIR/system/letta_connection_contract.md (transport rules — preserve agent/conversation targeting, ordered stream events, run cursor/resume, approval messages, cancellation, raw error visibility through the proxy).
acceptance_criteria:
- Shim accepts a Letta Cloud bearer token as an upstream config
- Shim proxies messages/runs API to Cloud upstream preserving stream contract
- A2UI stream-splitter applies to proxied responses
- Approval gate intercepts approval_request_message on proxied stream
- Mobile WS frames carry Cloud-proxied events identically to local-CLI events
- Per-request routing correctly directs local-CLI vs remote-proxy traffic
- Phase 1 mobile user can switch to shim URL without losing Cloud agent visibility

SDK migration must not preserve that failure mode. May fix it if resumeSession(convId) reliably binds CLI to intended conversation.

SDK path should explicitly select resumeSession(convId) for real conversation IDs and resumeSession(agentId) only for default conversations.

ID under SDK transport. 2) All three user messages + assistant replies land in same conversation. 3) No new conversation directory created for that sequence. 4) GET /v1/conversations returns one stable updated conv, not new freshest each turn. 5) Same stability test passes across worker restart or session close/reopen. 6) If SDK path doesn't fix lcp-cm5, file narrower follow-up explaining remaining resolver/local-backend cause.

description: Switch all send paths from direct pool internals to the new adapter seam: REST/SSE chat dispatch and mobile WS send_message. Keep direct path available via SHIM_LETTA_TRANSPORT=direct until cleanup.

title: Preserve shim Run records, frame replay, and message attribution on SDK path
description: SDK may expose Letta Code run IDs, but mobile currently relies on shim-created /v1/runs/* records. Preserve the shim run lifecycle while using SDK sessions underneath.
design: Treat SDK run IDs as upstream metadata, NOT primary mobile ID (unless later decision bead changes contract). Store SDK run IDs in RunRecord.metadata.sdk_run_ids if useful. Preserve first-wins semantics for run-level stop_reason and usage. Ensure SDK transformed result.runIds and raw stream_event run IDs don't break stale-run filtering or frame grouping. If SDK only yields transformed events for some message types, reconstruct raw frame shape for existing reshapeFrame+A2UI code. Preserve: createRun() pre-turn, turn_started carries non-null runId, every WS frame stamped, frames.jsonl append, message_ids attribution, finalizeRun() w/ status+stop_reason+duration+usage+steps, buildMessageRunMap projection.
acceptance_criteria: 1) SDK path creates exactly one shim run record per turn. 2) Mobile-facing frames carry shim run ID, not mix of SDK+shim IDs. 3) /v1/runs/{id}, /messages, /usage, /metrics, /steps work for SDK-backed turns. 4) frames.jsonl replay works. 5) buildMessageRunMap() attributes SDK-persisted messages correctly. 6) Existing run tests pass under direct + focused equivalents pass under SDK.
notes: Files: lib/runs.ts, lib/agent-pool.ts, lib/mobile-channel-host.ts, test/runs.test.ts, test/ws-subscribe.test.ts, test/ws-protocol.test.ts. Verify: npm test -- test/runs.test.ts && npm test -- test/ws-subscribe.test.ts + focused SDK run-lifecycle tests.

Refactor lifted two pure helpers from DirectSubprocess.runTurn into module scope of agent-pool.ts: applyFrameRunSideEffects (per-frame markRunFirstToken/recordRunTool/recordRunStep + pendingStepUsage tracking) and finalizeTurnLifecycle (stampNewMessages + recordRunMessage + first-stop_reason/usage extraction + finalizeRun). Both adapters now call them — DirectSubprocess refactored to the new seam (behavior-identical to pre-extraction; 112/113 direct-path lifecycle-sensitive tests pass with no regression), and SdkBackedLettaSessionAdapter.runTurn rewritten to: (1) resolve or pre-create runHandle (mirrors lcp-99a pattern — mobile WS can supply, REST creates fresh), (2) register cancellation hook via setRunCancelHandler (session.abort as SDK analog of subprocess SIGTERM; spec-boundary caveat re cancellation surfaces in lcp-sdk.5), (3) snapshot pre-turn message ids, (4) apply per-frame run side effects inside the stream loop, (5) finalize via shared helper. Adapter return shape now carries run_id (from runHandle, not SDK), cancelled, newUserMessageId. Tests: 2 new lcp-sdk.4 cases in test/sdk-adapter.test.ts (full run record observable via getRun after a stub turn: status=completed, stop_reason=end_turn, num_steps=1, Run.usage propagated; pre-supplied runHandle is honored without firing onRunCreated). Full suite: 334/335 (1 pre-existing TODO unchanged). Build clean. Approvals + cancellation-surface + REST/SSE/WS dispatcher wiring still owned by lcp-sdk.5 + lcp-sdk.6.

title: Port approvals, permission callbacks, and A2UI user actions to SDK path
description: Current hand-rolled pool intercepts approval_request_message frames and blocks tool execution until mobile WS user action resolves the approval gate. SDK also has canUseTool, permissionMode, and approval-conflict recovery. Need one coherent approval model on SDK path.
design: Current behavior: approval requests → mobile A2UI cards; gate keyed by shim run ID + tool call ID; mobile user_action resolves with Once/Session/Forever/Deny; Session+Forever persist in approvals.json; decisions append audit under run sidecar; non-approval A2UI user actions inject synthetic user turns. SDK mapping: use canUseTool to block tool execution → convert canUseTool(name,input) into existing approval gate → preserve existing mobile A2UI approval card frame shape → continue recording via runs.ts → disable/bound SDK auto-approval recovery if it conflicts with explicit mobile approvals.
acceptance_criteria: 1) SDK path emits mobile approval cards for tools requiring approval. 2) Once allows exactly the pending tool call. 3) Session auto-allows later calls to same tool in same conv. 4) Forever auto-allows across conversations. 5) Deny blocks tool, returns error to agent without execution. 6) Approval timeout auto-denies + audits. 7) Non-approval A2UI user_action still triggers synthetic agent turn. 8) Approval behavior documented with SDK mapping + disabled SDK recovery settings.
notes: Files: lib/agent-pool.ts, lib/mobile-channel-host.ts, lib/runs.ts, docs/MOBILE_WS_PROTOCOL.md, test/a2ui-ws.test.ts, test/ws-protocol.test.ts. Verify: focused approval tests under SDK path + existing A2UI WS tests + full npm test.
close_reason: Approvals wired on the SDK path via canUseTool callback. admin-shim/lib/letta-sdk-adapter.ts: (1) start() registers canUseTool on resumeSession options — the SDK invokes it from its background pump for every approval-required tool call (letta-code is approval-by-default). (2) _runTurnInner sets per-turn context fields (currentRunHandle, currentOnFrame, currentApprovalScopeCache, currentA2uiCapability) before the stream loop and clears them in finally{}. Turn serialization via this.chain guarantees at most one turn alive, so single fields suffice — no per-turn map. (3) _handleCanUseTool method: checks scope cache first (Session/Forever auto-allow with NO frame emission — divergence from direct adapter, but better UX: no transient approval card flicker for already-approved tools), then synthesizes an approval_request_message wire frame matching the upstream ApprovalRequestMessageEvent shape (synthetic-<uuid> toolCallId, monotonic seq_id starting at 1_000_000 to avoid collision with upstream-allocated ids), emits via opts.onFrame, blocks on waitForApprovalDecision (the SAME gate the direct adapter uses — mobile-channel-host.handleUserAction → resolveApprovalGate(runId, decision) resolves it identically), records decision/policy via runs.ts helpers, returns CanUseToolResponse{ behavior: allow|deny }. No-A2UI short-circuit: default-allow without emitting a card (matches direct adapter's a2uiCapability ? ... : null behavior). Known limitation: the synthetic tool_call_id won't match the CLI's real id on the eventual tool_return_message — mobile UI correlation by tool_call_id is visually broken. Functional gate (keyed by run_id) works correctly. Filed follow-up. Tests: 3 new lcp-sdk.5 cases in test/sdk-adapter.test.ts (synthetic frame + gate resolution → allow; Session-scope cache → no second frame; no-A2UI → default-allow without frame). waitForApprovalDecision + ApprovalDecision exported from agent-pool.ts. Full suite 341/342 (1 pre-existing TODO).

title: Implement SDK-backed session adapter behind feature flag
description: Implement a second adapter that uses @letta-ai/letta-code-sdk for process/session management. Keep it disabled by default (SHIM_LETTA_TRANSPORT=direct|sdk) until parity beads land.

Explicit cwd, memfs, skillSources, systemInfoReminder, permissionMode, memfsStartup if behavior depends on them. Shim depends on raw Letta stream frames for projection+A2UI splitting — first impl should preserve raw stream_event payloads.

(2) Stream pass-through — every SDKStreamEventMessage forwards the raw wire 'event' payload verbatim into a StreamEventFrame, so the existing collector logic in DirectSubprocess (cases on event.message_type for assistant_message/tool_call/usage_statistics/stop_reason) keeps working unchanged. title: Introduce a Letta session adapter seam above agent-pool

title: Audit SDK runtime compatibility and add dependency
description: Add @letta-ai/letta-code-sdk to admin-shim and prove the SDK can drive the same Letta Code runtime as the current hand-rolled pool. Critical question: does the SDK path respect the shim's local backend without our explicit --backend local arg? SDK spawns: node <@letta-ai/letta-code> --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json. Current pool: letta --backend local --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --include-partial-messages.

title: REST /messages mid-turn races WS deltas — cumulative snapshot gets appended as delta, produces incoherent text
description:
## Observed (2026-05-19 22:28-22:32 EDT, live repro on Pixel 9 Pro)

After shipping lcp-pro (seq_id alias on assistant_message frames), the original incoherence symptom **still repros**. User typed 'this is what I received' and pasted back this exact garbled output from my response:

> StandStanding by. Send a message that previously would have looked broken — long enough toing by. Send a message that previously would have looked broken — long enough to span multiple deltas, ideally — and we'll see if the merge st span multiple deltas, ideally — and we'll see if the merge stays clean.ays clean.

Segmenting that output reveals the failure shape:
- delta 1: 'Stand'
- delta 2 (cumulative snapshot, starts with 'Stand'): 'Standing by. Send a message that previously would have looked broken — long enough to'
- delta 3 (delta from inside the snapshot): 'ing by. Send a message that previously would have looked broken — long enough to span multiple deltas, ideally — and we'll see if the merge st'
- delta 4: ' span multiple deltas, ideally — and we'll see if the merge stays clean.'
- delta 5: 'ays clean.'

Two streaming contracts collided on the same logical message id (cm-stream-<otid>). Some frames are pure deltas (lcp-cv3 contract); one frame is a cumulative snapshot. The client appends both as deltas.

## Where the snapshot came from — log evidence

/tmp/admin-shim.log around the offending turn:

> [2026-05-20T02:30:39.815Z] 192.168.50.235  GET    200 75ms req=0B res=577410B auth✓ /v1/conversations/conv-617e458d-5a3c-4fb5-b295-6531344a3298/messages?limit=250&order=desc ua='ktor-client'
> [pool] stdin.write conv=conv-617e458d-5a3c-4fb5-b295-6531344a3298 shape=string(24ch)

A REST GET /messages call landed at 02:30:39 — **during the active turn that produced the garbled response**. 577 KB of message snapshot, returned in 75ms, including a cumulative assistant_message that the client merged into the same serverId already accumulating WS deltas. The non-Client-Mode merge in TimelineSyncIngest.kt:212 is pure 'oldText + newText' — no defensive check that the incoming content is a strict prefix of what's already there.

This is the c3h4 transport race firing live. WS + REST both deliver to the same serverId; nothing reconciles their contracts.

## Why lcp-pro alone doesn't fix this

lcp-pro stamped seq_id on WS deltas so the client's hasAlreadyIngestedStreamFrame gate could dedup *duplicate* frames. But the REST hydration path doesn't go through the WS frame log; it's a separate code path with no seq_id at all. The dedup gate doesn't fire against it. And even if it did, the REST hydrate isn't a duplicate seq — it's a different shape entirely (snapshot vs delta).

## Proposed shim-side fixes

### Primary fix (the right one): gate REST /messages during active WS turns

When a WS session is active for conv-X with inFlight=true, REST GET /v1/conversations/X/messages either:
- (a) returns 409 Conflict with a 'wait for turn_done' hint, OR
- (b) blocks until turn_done before responding, OR
- (c) returns the pre-turn snapshot deterministically (no in-flight assistant content).

Option (c) is least disruptive: keep the request flowing, but exclude any messages whose otid matches a currently-streaming WS turn. The hydrator gets a consistent snapshot that does NOT collide with the live stream; the WS turn finishes and the next hydrate naturally picks it up.

### Defense in depth: shim emit dedup by content

Track recently-emitted content per cm-stream-<otid>. Before emitting an assistant_message delta, check:
- If new content equals existing accumulated content → drop (duplicate emit).
- If new content is a strict prefix of accumulated content → drop (stale/redundant snapshot).
- If accumulated content is a strict prefix of new content → emit as a delta containing only the suffix.
- Otherwise → emit as-is.

This catches the case where upstream letta-code or any caller emits a snapshot mid-stream by accident, and ensures the WS path stays in pure-delta shape regardless of upstream behavior. Does NOT fix the REST race (different path) — that's the primary fix above.

### Documentation

MOBILE_WS_PROTOCOL.md §12 (WS-canonical) needs an explicit rule: 'REST /messages MUST NOT return content that is currently being streamed via WS for the same conversation. The two transports MUST NOT race on the same serverId.'

## Acceptance

- During an active WS turn, REST GET /messages does not return the in-flight assistant_message content (or returns it but flagged as in-flight so the client doesn't merge it).
- Repro test: open WS to conv-X, send_message, immediately hit GET /messages for conv-X. Assert no overlap between the streamed deltas and the GET result, OR assert the GET result has a 'pending_run' marker.
- Live test on device: send a multi-delta response; observe no garbled merging.
- 'StandStanding by...' shape never appears in user-visible text again.

## Related

- lcp-pro (P1, OPEN, this rig) — shim-side seq_id alias. Necessary but insufficient — landed but symptom persists.
- letta-mobile-c3h4 (P1, IN_PROGRESS) — three-way transport race. This bead is the shim-side companion fix for the same disease.
- letta-mobile-16li (P1, IN_PROGRESS) — hydration misses latest user prompts. Same family.
- letta-mobile-wq8v (P1, OPEN epic) — Conversation state SSoT. This bead is one of the concrete pieces of work toward closing it.

Reporter context: Emmanuel, 2026-05-19 ~22:35 EDT, after my live attempt to verify the lcp-pro patch: 'this is what I received [garbled]'.
close_reason: snapshot-based inFlightMessageIds + per-handle messageIdsAtTurnStart wired into REST handlers; 8 new tests + 365-test suite green

title: WS assistant_message deltas have no seq_id — client merge appends duplicates, produces incoherent text
description:
## Observed (2026-05-19 evening, Pixel 9 Pro, REST-letta → shim WS path)

After switching from the REST letta server to the shim+WS path, assistant responses render **incoherently** — duplicated chunks, garbled fragments, text appearing twice. Doesn't happen on the REST path.

## Root cause

The shim was rewritten (lcp-cv3) to stop coalescing assistant_message chunks server-side. Instead, it emits **pure deltas** with a stable per-otid id (cm-stream-<otid>) and expects the mobile client to merge by id.

Source: admin-shim/lib/mobile-channel-host.ts lines 210-225:

> 'lcp-cv3: stream assistant_message and reasoning_message chunks as they arrive — DO NOT coalesce server-side. Mobile's stream ingest [...] To merge correctly each chunk must share the same id, so we stamp a stable per-otid id (cm-stream-<otid> for assistants, cm-reason-<otid> for reasoning).'

Problem: the WS wire schema for assistant_message does NOT include a seq_id field. Verified in:
- android-compose/core/src/main/java/com/letta/mobile/data/transport/MobileWsFrames.kt lines 500-512 — AssistantMessage has v/type/id/ts/agentId/conversationId/turnId/runId/content/otid. No seq, no seqId.
- shim emit path doesn't set it either.

The mobile client's stream-frame dedup gate uses seqId exclusively:

> android-compose/core/src/main/java/com/letta/mobile/data/timeline/TimelineSyncModels.kt lines 142-149:
> internal fun TimelineEvent.Confirmed.hasAlreadyIngestedStreamFrame(incoming: TimelineEvent.Confirmed): Boolean =
>     messageType == TimelineMessageType.ASSISTANT &&
>     incoming.messageType == TimelineMessageType.ASSISTANT &&
>     seqId != null && incoming.seqId != null &&
>     incoming.seqId <= seqId

Because every WS frame has incoming.seqId == null, the dedup check **always returns false on the WS path**. Every delta is treated as novel.

Then the merge logic at TimelineSyncIngest.kt lines 197-212:
- For Client Mode (CLIENT_MODE_HARNESS), there is defensive logic: startsWith / endsWith / equality checks before appending.
- For everything else (REST-letta → shim WS path the user is on now): pure 'oldText + newText'. Always append.

## Failure modes this produces

1. **WS delta replayed** (transport hiccup, reconnect-resume, race on the path) — appends a duplicate of recently-emitted text. User sees 'Hello worldHello world'.
2. **WS + REST race** — WS accumulated 'Hello world' via two deltas, then REST hydrate lands with the same serverId and the cumulative 'Hello world'. Without defensive merge, this becomes 'Hello worldHello world'. (Per letta-mobile-c3h4 the transport race is still open.)
3. **Reasoning content leaking into visible stream** if cm-reason-<otid> deltas land before the cm-stream-<otid> dedup window. (Probably not the primary cause here but possible.)
4. **A2UI splitter leftover bytes** — if the per-otid splitter holds bytes waiting for a close tag and a stream interruption flushes the buffer mid-content, fragments emit incorrectly.

## Proposed fixes

### Shim side (primary fix)

admin-shim/lib/mobile-channel-host.ts:

1. **Add seq_id to every WS frame** that participates in client-side merge: assistant_message, reasoning_message, and any other delta-shaped emit. Per-otid monotonic counter, starts at 0 per turn, increments on every delta emitted for that otid.
2. **Update MOBILE_WS_PROTOCOL.md §4.2 and §2.2** to document the post-cv3 reality: the shim does NOT coalesce; it streams pure deltas; every delta carries 'seq' (or 'seq_id'); clients must merge by id and dedup by seq.
3. Add a regression test in admin-shim/test/ws-protocol.test.ts asserting seq is monotonic per otid and present on every delta frame.

### Mobile side (defense in depth)

android-compose/core/src/main/java/com/letta/mobile/data/timeline/TimelineSyncIngest.kt:

1. **Add seqId parsing** in WsFrameMapper.toLettaMessage() for AssistantMessage / ReasoningMessage frames (reading the new shim field).
2. **Backport the Client-Mode defensive merge to the default branch** (lines 197-212). The startsWith/endsWith/equality checks aren't Client-Mode-specific — they defend against the same WS-vs-REST race for any path that has two producers on the same serverId. This makes the merge safe even before seq_id lands on the wire.
3. **When seqId is present, use it.** Once the shim ships seq_id, prefer it over the content-prefix heuristic.

### Telemetry

Telemetry call already exists at TimelineSyncIngest.kt:163 ('streamSubscriber.duplicateSeqSkipped'). Add a sibling event 'streamSubscriber.contentDuplicateSkipped' that fires when the defensive merge would otherwise have produced a 'Hello worldHello world' shape. Surface as a dashboard counter — this lets us see how often the race is firing in the wild.

## Acceptance

- Shim WS frames for assistant_message and reasoning_message carry a 'seq' field (or 'seq_id'; pick one, document).
- Mobile WsFrameMapper extracts seqId; merge path honors it; defensive content-prefix checks also apply on the non-Client-Mode branch.
- Switching from REST letta to shim+WS produces coherent assistant text — no duplicated chunks, no inline repeats, no fragment garbling.
- Regression coverage: shim emits monotonic seq per otid; client unit test feeds in duplicate WS deltas with same id/seq and asserts only one append; client unit test feeds in WS deltas followed by a REST hydrate with cumulative content and asserts no duplication.

## Related

- letta-mobile-c3h4 (P1, in_progress) — three-way transport race; fixing this bead is independent but the test cases overlap.
- letta-mobile-mge5 + the wucn-snapshot-recovery cascade — prior eras of this same merge logic being subtly wrong (referenced in TimelineSyncIngest.kt lines 157-196). This is the same class of bug, new manifestation.
- letta-mobile-81kk (in_progress) — 'hydrator fetches messages but doesn't render history' — related to the same merge-and-render path.
- MOBILE_WS_PROTOCOL.md §4.2 — currently says coalescing happens server-side; out of date after lcp-cv3 and needs updating as part of this fix.

## Reporter context

Emmanuel, 2026-05-19 ~22:30 EDT: 'I switched from the rest letta server to the shim enabled one with ws and your responses look incoherent.'
close_reason: seq_id explicit alias of run-frame seq stamped on assistant_message + reasoning_message in emit(); regression test enforces seq_id===seq; doc already documented the contract

title: Conversation reopen still reloads incorrect state — renders incorrectly even after hydration fix attempts
description:
## Repro (2026-05-19 ~13:03 EDT, Pixel 9 Pro)

After landing in-progress work on letta-mobile-16li (hydration misses latest prompts) and letta-mobile-c3h4 (three-way transport race), coming back to a chat conversation **still** reloads incorrect state. The rehydration does not render correctly.

Emmanuel's framing: 'coming back to a chat still reloads incorrect state that does not render correctly'.

(Screenshot referenced but not in agent context.)

## Why this is in the shim rig, not letta-mobile

Hydration on reopen pulls from the admin-shim's REST surface — GET /v1/conversations/{id}/messages projected by lib/translate.ts. If the disk projection emits malformed or inconsistent state, the renderer renders incorrectly regardless of how clean the Android side is.

Sibling beads being addressed elsewhere:
- letta-mobile-16li (P1, in_progress) — hydration misses latest user prompts on reopen.
- letta-mobile-c3h4 (P1, in_progress) — three-way transport race (SSE + WS + REST).
- letta-mobile-xhkw (P1, open) — tool cards regress to plain text on hydration.

This bead exists because **even with those in flight, reopening a chat still does not render correctly** — implying the disk projection or REST response shape itself is part of the problem, not just the client-side reconciliation.

## Suspected shim-side causes

1. **translate.ts loses fidelity that the live stream preserved.** Tool calls flatten into assistant text; A2UI surface frames don't survive the disk projection; otid sidecar doesn't bind on every path.
2. **stop_reason / usage_statistics / turn_done bare envelopes on REST disagree with the WS-wrapped versions.** Per §4.7 they should match; verify on a hydration response.
3. **Frame ordering on disk does not match emit order.** Per-type ms offsets (§4.3) only guarantee in-turn stable sort; cross-turn ordering depends on real-time stamping which may be racy on writes.
4. **A2UI surface state is not persisted in the message stream at all.** If a2ui_frame messages only exist as transient WS frames and never land in the messages table or its sidecar, then nothing brings them back on hydration — surfaces simply vanish on reopen.

## Acceptance

- Open a conversation, exercise: assistant message, tool call, A2UI surface, second assistant message. Close. Reopen.
- GET /v1/conversations/{id}/messages returns a payload that includes every visible element in the correct order with the correct discriminators.
- Tool calls re-render as cards (overlaps with letta-mobile-xhkw acceptance).
- A2UI surfaces either re-render in their final state OR are explicitly absent (governed by lifecycle field once letta-mobile-rw5s lands; auto-dismissed ones don't come back, manual/wait_for_response ones do).
- otid round-trip survives across reopen.
- Unit test: fixture conversation with mixed frame types → hydration response → assert byte-shape against a golden file.

## Source pointers

- admin-shim/lib/translate.ts — primary disk projection.
- admin-shim/lib/store.ts — otid sidecar, projection helpers.
- admin-shim/lib/chat.ts — reshapeFrame; verify the same transform applies (or its inverse is sound) on the projection path.
- For A2UI: check whether a2ui_frame is persisted anywhere on disk; if not, the surface vanish-on-reopen behavior is by design and we need to decide policy.

## Related

- letta-mobile-wq8v (epic, SSoT for conversation state) — this bead is the shim-side instance of the same disease.
- letta-mobile-16li, letta-mobile-c3h4 (in_progress, client + transport sides).
- letta-mobile-xhkw (open, tool cards regression — likely overlaps).
- letta-mobile-rw5s (open, A2UI surface lifecycle — needs to be resolved before deciding what 'correct hydration' means for surfaces).
- MOBILE_WS_PROTOCOL.md §6 reconciliation, §4.7 bare envelope shape, §12 WS-canonical conversation state.
notes:
## 2026-05-22 repro (lcp-ith follow-up session)

Concrete reproducer from Emmanuel during pressure-test of the lcp-ith settle-agentId patch:

1. Open the mobile app, start a new conversation against Meridian (agent-597b5756-…) or any agent.
2. Send an initial prompt.
3. Swipe away to another screen in the app while the turn is in progress (or shortly after).
4. Swipe back to the conversation.

Observed:
- Conversation renders broken — the **initial prompt ends up at the END of the message list** instead of at the top where it was sent.
- The agent goes dead (no further responses received). Subsequent turns return stop_reason:error in <1s with ttft_ns=null (model never called).

Shim-side notes:
- lcp-ith (settle agentId fix) is firing correctly on every spawn — visible in /tmp/admin-shim.log as '[letta-code-patch] applied executeConversationTurn settle agentId fix'. So this is NOT the dangling-tool-use class.
- Run records for the affected conversations show status:completed, stop_reason:error, num_steps:1, no usage — the failure is BEFORE the model call, suggesting either (a) malformed history hits the executor's pre-flight, or (b) the mobile WS state desyncs the UI without the disk being damaged.
- 'Initial prompt at end' strongly smells like the cumulative-snapshot-as-delta pattern from lcp-r0m: a REST GET /v1/conversations/{id}/messages returns the full ordered list, but the WS resubscribe pushes deltas the client appends WITHOUT realizing they're already in the snapshot — so the newest user message lands at index 0 of the WS-delta tail rather than reusing its REST position.

Cross-refs: lcp-r0m, lcp-pro, lcp-7bq. Gateway / mobile-as-channel work (lcp-gj2) is in flight per Emmanuel and may obsolete this repro path.

title: admin-shim: push notification emitter via UnifiedPush + existing ntfy
description:
## Goal

Server-side implementation of the UnifiedPush push notification path. Companion to letta-mobile-t1ik (epic) and letta-mobile-8kd0 (Android receiver). This is the off-device half of the push system.

## What lands here

Three sub-pieces — likely become child issues once this lands and we slice:

### 1. Pusher registry

- Extend WS 'hello' frame schema with optional fields:
  - 'unifiedpush_endpoint' — string URL the mobile distributor handed the app.
  - 'pusher_kind' — discriminator: 'unifiedpush' for now; reserved for 'fcm' later.
- Persist per-device alongside existing device-state sidecar ('home/.letta/channels/mobile/lib/state.mjs').
- Add WS frame 'pusher_register' / 'pusher_unregister' so the mobile app can update or revoke its endpoint without a full reconnect.
- Update admin-shim/docs/MOBILE_WS_PROTOCOL.md §2.1 with the new hello fields + new frame types.

### 2. Push policy module

- New: admin-shim/lib/push-policy.ts
- Single function entry: 'shouldPush(event, deviceState): PushDecision'
- Inputs: an internal event (new assistant message, run completion, approval request, cron fired) + the device's registered policy.
- Outputs: either 'drop' with reason, or 'push' with payload (title, body, conv_id, importance hint).
- Rules to support at v1:
  - Per-conv mute list.
  - Quiet hours (per-device tz from existing device state).
  - Event-type filter (push for assistant_message + approvals + cron by default; not for tool_return).
  - Foreground-state suppression: don't push to a device whose WS is currently OPEN — they're already seeing it live.

### 3. ntfy emitter

- New: admin-shim/lib/push-emitter-ntfy.ts
- POSTs to the existing ntfy instance: 'http://matrix-tuwunel-deploy-ntfy-1:80' (already healthy on this host, port 2586 on the docker host).
- Topic naming convention TBD in P1 of the epic — placeholder: 'lm-<device_id>'.
- Auth: ntfy supports per-topic ACLs + bearer tokens; reuse whatever scheme is already on that ntfy instance, or add a dedicated 'letta-mobile-push' user.
- Payload: ntfy JSON format with 'title', 'message', 'tags', 'priority', 'click' (deep-link URL the Android app parses).
- Coordinate with existing ntfy bridge ('matrix-tuwunel-deploy-ntfy-bridge-1' which currently watches 'alerts','failures','deploys') — our new topics must not collide.

## Event sources to hook into

These already exist in admin-shim — we just need to tap them:

- New assistant_message frames (hook in mobile-channel-host.ts or chat.ts post-stamp).
- turn_done with status that warrants notification (approval gates, errors).
- Cron task fires (cron-scheduler.ts).
- User-action outcomes that surface results (user_action_outcome with detail).

## Out of scope here

- The Android-side receiver and notification builder — see letta-mobile-8kd0.
- Retiring the mobile-side foreground service — see epic P6.
- FCM fallback — epic P8, deferred.

## Acceptance

- Mobile app registers via 'hello' with 'unifiedpush_endpoint'; admin-shim persists.
- When a notification-worthy event fires AND the device's WS is not OPEN, admin-shim POSTs to ntfy.
- ntfy delivery is observable in admin-shim logs + ntfy access logs.
- Per-conv mute and quiet hours respected (unit tests on push-policy.ts cover the matrix of rules).
- Existing ntfy PM bridge keeps working — letta-mobile additions do not interfere with 'alerts','failures','deploys' topic flow.
- Documentation: MOBILE_WS_PROTOCOL.md updated; new section in admin-shim/docs on the push architecture.

## Source pointers

- New: admin-shim/lib/push-policy.ts
- New: admin-shim/lib/push-emitter-ntfy.ts
- Modify: admin-shim/lib/mobile-channel-host.ts — wire push hooks into event paths.
- Modify: home/.letta/channels/mobile/lib/state.mjs — persist pusher registry alongside device state.
- Modify: home/.letta/channels/mobile/lib/protocol.mjs — add 'pusher_register' / 'pusher_unregister' frame types.
- Modify: home/.letta/channels/mobile/lib/ws-handler.mjs — accept new hello fields, route new frames.
- Modify: admin-shim/docs/MOBILE_WS_PROTOCOL.md — protocol additions.

## Related

- Parent epic (letta-mobile rig): letta-mobile-t1ik.
- Mobile companion (letta-mobile rig): letta-mobile-8kd0.
- Existing ntfy infra: matrix-tuwunel-deploy-ntfy-1 (port 2586), bridge container 'matrix-tuwunel-deploy-ntfy-bridge-1'.
- Reference: Matrix push spec (https://spec.matrix.org/v1.10/push-gateway-api/) for the policy-vs-transport separation we're mirroring.

Vanilla Letta serves tool_call_message + tool_return_message rows from GET /v1/agents/{id}/messages and GET /v1/conversations/{id}/messages; admin-shim has drifted somewhere in the localMessageToLettaMessage translation or upstream in how the agent-pool persists assistant turns. Need to (1) restore tool card emission on history reads, and (2) add a schema/contract check so regressions surface early instead of waiting for visual breakage.

Added test/onfdisk-translate.test.ts as a fixture-driven drift gate that asserts (1) every toolResult row projects to a tool_return_message, (2) every tool-shaped part produces a tool_*_message in the fan-out, (3) no tool-shaped source silently degrades to assistant_message, and (4) any FUTURE unknown 'tool*' part emits a translate.unknown_tool_part console.warn so the next drift surfaces in logs/CI instead of as visual breakage.
