title: Architecture: prefer reusable project agent pools over massive single-use subagent generation
description:
Emmanuel (2026-06-06): we are generating a massive number of single-use agents for side/delegated work, which does not make sense for ongoing projects. These codebases benefit from PRIOR EXPERIENCE and accumulated project context. We should consider a delegation model where subagent generation can be single-use OR reuse a project-scoped pool of agents set up by VibeSync.

PROBLEM:
- Current delegation tends to spawn one-off subagents. They do not carry durable experience with the target repo/codebase beyond whatever is in the prompt.
- This creates agent sprawl, loses accumulated context, and makes repeated work on the same project less efficient.
- It also weakens continuity: a new agent may miss prior architectural decisions, known traps, bead history, repo-specific SOPs, and project memory.

PROPOSED DIRECTION:
- VibeSync should set up reusable project agent pools per project/codebase. Example: two project-manager agents and maybe two dev agents per project.
- When delegating side work, choose from the existing pool based on the target project/repo and task type instead of blindly spawning a fresh single-use agent.
- Keep single-use agents available for truly isolated/throwaway tasks, but make project-pool reuse the default for recurring project work.

ROUTING MODEL:
- Delegation request includes target project/repo/worktree/bead.
- Resolver maps target to a VibeSync project profile and eligible agent pool.
- Select an agent by role (PM/reviewer/dev/perf/debug), availability, recent context, and ownership.
- Start a NEW conversation with that existing agent for the task (so task context is clean) but retain the agent's durable memory/manifest.
- Record the task/conversation mapping so mobile chips can route to BOTH the correct agent AND the correct active work conversation.

PRODUCT REQUIREMENTS:
- Agent creation policy: single-use vs reusable-pool should be explicit, not accidental.
- UI should show whether a task is handled by a reused project agent vs a disposable one.
- Avoid unbounded agent sprawl; maintain lifecycle/retirement policy for project agents.
- Project agents should have durable project memories: repo topology, recurring beads, prior PRs, known regressions, testing/build SOPs.

ACCEPTANCE:
- VibeSync can declare a project agent pool for a repo/project.
- Delegation to that repo reuses an existing project agent by default.
- Single-use remains possible via explicit override.
- Mobile/active-chip routing records agent_id + active conversation_id so tapping opens the correct active work conversation.
- Agent reuse improves continuity: repeated tasks on letta-mobile/letta-code-admin-shim go to agents with prior project memory instead of cold one-offs.

RELATED: mobile subagent chip wrong-conversation bug (letta-mobile-xm8qk), VibeSync project management, agent deployment vs conversation context distinction, reusable-agent memory/manifest model.

comments.author: Claude Code
comments.text: CORRECTION (Emmanuel 2026-06-06): VibeSync currently creates a SINGLE project-manager (PM) agent per project, and that is CORRECT. Do NOT propose two PM agents per project. The architecture should preserve exactly one canonical PM/project for ownership, continuity, routing, and project memory. The reusable-pool proposal should be refined to: one VibeSync PM per project (existing correct model) + optional small reusable role-specific worker pool (e.g. dev/debug/reviewer agents) per project, coordinated by or associated with that PM. Delegation should route through/with the project PM and then select an existing worker when appropriate; single-use remains explicit override. Update acceptance accordingly: one canonical PM per project remains invariant.

title: ENFORCEMENT: static lint/detekt rule for work-in-composition (cheap perf gate, no velocity tax)
description: Tonight's frame-budget regressions were the 'work in a @Composable body not behind remember' class (Regex compile per recompose, alloc per recompose, per-frame state reads, per-item size-floor work). The heavyweight CI macrobenchmark was removed for destroying velocity. The RIGHT replacement is a CHEAP static rule, not a runtime benchmark: a detekt/lint rule (or custom rule) that flags Regex()/.toRegex()/parse/buildAnnotatedString/BitmapFactory.decode/new List|Map|associateBy|sortedBy in a @Composable function body that is NOT wrapped in remember(...). Compile-time, milliseconds, non-flaky, non-blocking-friendly. This is the systemic enforcement of the render hot-path discipline (encoded in agent memory) — pushes the gate LEFT (write-time + compile-time) instead of the velocity-killing right-side benchmark. Scope to feature-chat render/screen packages. ACCEPTANCE: the rule flags a deliberately-introduced 'Regex() in a composable' and passes clean on current main after #361.

title: TEST COVERAGE: generate_image tool (lcp-vw2h) — extend tests for default-model + error path
description: The generate_image patch-loader tool has a happy-path test (registers + saves + returns image block). But the END-TO-END test tonight found the DEFAULT model 'gpt-image-2-medium' FAILS (Codex no-image-result) while 'gpt-image-2' works — and there is no test covering that. ADD: (1) a test asserting the tool's default model resolves to a WORKING handle (or, once the default is fixed, that a no-model call uses the working route); (2) a test for the error path — a non-OK / no-image upstream response surfaces a clear error, not a silent empty result; (3) assert the saved-to-disk + content-block shape for a non-default model arg. Pairs with the 'generate_image default model fails' bug bead. ACCEPTANCE: tests fail if the default model regresses to a non-working route or the error path swallows failures.
notes: PR #34 covers the default-model regression by exercising generate_image with no model arg and asserting gpt-image-2. Remaining coverage still needed here: explicit non-default model shape and non-OK/no-image error-path assertions.

title: generate_image tool default model 'gpt-image-2-medium' fails (Codex no-image-result); 'gpt-image-2' works
description:
End-to-end test of the native generate_image tool (lcp-vw2h) 2026-06-05: the tool is LIVE and validates correctly (rejects empty prompt). But generation with the TOOL DEFAULT model fails:

- model='gpt-image-2-medium' (the tool's DEFAULT_MODEL in the patch-loader) -> HTTP 500: {error: {message: 'ChatGPT image generation failed: Codex response contained no image_generation_call result'}}. Reproduced twice (not transient). This handle routes through the max-proxy's ChatGPT/Codex image path which returns NO image_generation_call result.
- model='gpt-image-2' (explicit) -> SUCCESS. Returns b64 PNG, saved to disk, renders. (Same handle that worked via raw curl earlier tonight: the Elora street + mascot images.)

SO: the tool wiring + validation + save/Read path all work; only the DEFAULT model handle is wrong. It points at a Codex-backed route ('gpt-image-2-medium') that doesn't return an image; the working route is 'gpt-image-2' on the anthropic-claude-max-proxy (:8082) /v1/images/generations.

FIX: change the generate_image tool DEFAULT model from 'gpt-image-2-medium' to 'gpt-image-2' (in admin-shim/scripts/letta-code-patch-loader.mjs, GENERATE_IMAGE_TOOL_HELPER_DEFINITION: model default = ... ?? 'gpt-image-2-medium'). OR fix the max-proxy so the -medium / Codex route returns an image. Verify: calling generate_image with NO model arg succeeds and returns a PNG.

NOTE: the tool source is in the patch-loader (uncommitted working-tree change in letta-code-parallel); this is part of the in-flight image-tool wiring. Whoever owns that should fix the default + commit.

ACCEPTANCE: generate_image with default args (no model) generates and saves an image successfully on the live shim.

RELATED: lcp-vw2h (generate_image tool), the :8082 anthropic-claude-max-proxy image route, request_converter.py / providers/chatgpt_provider.py (the Codex image path that returns no result).

title: Subagent dispatches default to Opus — implement budget-aware model routing (mechanical work -> Sonnet/Codex)
description:
Observed 2026-06-05 (Emmanuel): all subagent dispatches ran on OPUS (expensive), even mechanical, build/test-gated chrome tasks that should use a cheaper/faster model. Attempting to override (model:'sonnet') fails with the thinking-budget bug (separate bead: 'Subagent model override ... thinking.enabled.budget_tokens Field required'), so today there is effectively NO working way to route a subagent to a non-Opus model — everything falls back to Opus.

TWO COUPLED PROBLEMS:
1. (separate bead, P1) the model-override path 400s on missing thinking budget -> must be fixed first so override works AT ALL.
2. (THIS bead) once override works, dispatches should ROUTE BY TASK PROFILE, not default to Opus: mechanical + strongly-gated implementation (success guarded by tsc/tests/build/PR checks) -> OpenAI Codex (esp. 5.3 Codex Spark) or Sonnet; normal implementation -> Sonnet; complex repair / Sonnet-failed -> GPT-5.5 as the intermediate before Opus; architecture/state/transport/security/ambiguous design -> Opus. Emmanuel explicitly does NOT want Opus as the routine implementer.

This is the subagent-dispatch manifestation of lcp-1lod (model:auto -> role/task/budget-aware policy). The Agent tool / subagent spawn should accept a model (working, post fix #1) AND ideally resolve a sensible default per task risk/budget instead of Opus. At minimum: make a non-Opus model selectable and reliable for subagent dispatch so the orchestrator (me) can route mechanical work cheaply.

DESIRED: resolve subagent model by task profile + budget mode (VIBESYNC_MODEL_BUDGET-style conserve|balanced|premium) + provider availability; log resolved model + reason; don't silently collapse to Opus. Provide a clean way for the dispatching agent to specify intent (e.g. 'mechanical', 'normal', 'complex', 'architecture') that maps to a model.

ACCEPTANCE: a mechanical build/test-gated subagent task runs on Sonnet/Codex (not Opus); the dispatcher can specify model or task-class and it is honored + logged; Opus is reserved for architecture/ambiguous work.

RELATED: lcp-1lod (model:auto routing policy), the thinking-budget override bug (blocks this), debug_loop_methodology model routing policy, product cost posture.

title: sdk-compat live-CLI session resume fails: CLI now requires --new-agent/--agent (SDK passes neither)
description:
Surfaced by lcp-a0rl (test-runner false-green fix). The live-CLI integration test `sdk-compat: SDK Session resumes against project-local backend (no --backend flag)` in admin-shim/test/sdk-compat.test.ts fails: the SDK spawns the letta CLI via createSession(undefined,...) which passes neither --new-agent nor --agent, and the current CLI rejects this with "Use --new-agent to create a local agent, or pass --agent <local-agent-id> to choose one explicitly." -> "transport closed before init message received" -> "Failed to initialize session - no init message received".

This was SILENTLY FAILING (swallowed by the false-green runner, lcp-a0rl) — i.e. SDK env-only local-backend routing no longer auto-creates an agent. The two static sdk-compat tests (package/types load, CreateSessionOptions) still pass.

In lcp-a0rl this live-CLI test was gated behind opt-in env SHIM_TEST_LIVE_CLI=1 (mirrors the existing "channel smokes run against a real letta binary -> behind a manual trigger" precedent) so the unit suite stays deterministic/CI-safe. 

FIX: either (a) have the SDK/shim pass --new-agent (or resolve/pass an --agent) on initial local-backend session, or (b) update the test contract to the new CLI agent-selection requirement. Then re-enable it (drop the SHIM_TEST_LIVE_CLI gate or add it to the manual CI job).

title: perf(shim): cursor replay re-read entire log on every reconnect — O(total history) (lcp-02ri F1)
description: FIXED in PR off lcp-gukg-terminal-stop-reason. lib/mobile-conversation-cursors.ts readReplayFrames() did readFileSync + per-line JSON.parse over the ENTIRE append-only <conv>.frames.jsonl on every resumeConversation (WS reconnect), but only ever returns the most-recent MAX_FRAMES (sort+slice(-MAX_FRAMES)). Read+parse cost was O(total frames ever stamped) — the lcp-02ri streaming-replay class. Measured (plain node vs dist): 1.85ms@500, 6.8ms@2k, 17ms@8k, 64ms@20k, 115ms@50k — clearly linear in history. Fix: bounded tail read (readReplayTailLines) seeking from EOF in 64KiB chunks until MAX_FRAMES+1 complete lines, drop leading partial line, parse forward; frames are seq-ascending so the newest MAX_FRAMES live at the tail and output is identical. After fix: ~8-22ms flat across 500-50k frames (20k 64->8ms ~8x, 50k 115->22ms ~5x). Regression test test/mobile-conversation-cursors.test.ts. Residual on-disk file growth tracked by lcp-2s5e.
acceptance_criteria: Reconnect replay read+parse bounded to O(MAX_FRAMES); output byte-identical for realistic cases; regression test asserts tail-bounded behavior. (Met.)
close_reason: Fixed: tail-bounded readReplayFrames; verified by measurement + regression test. PR off lcp-gukg.

title: perf(shim): LRU/TTL-cap in-memory per-conversation maps (cursor states, self-todo) (lcp-02ri F2/F4)
description: Two in-memory Maps keyed by conversationId are never pruned (grow O(distinct conversations seen over process lifetime)): (1) lib/mobile-conversation-cursors.ts 'states' (getState populates, never deletes); each entry's replay[] IS bounded per-conv via pruneReplay, so it's one bounded bucket per conversation but unbounded bucket count. (2) lib/self-todo.ts '_byConversation' and '_sessionTasksByConversation' (only cleared by test-only __resetSelfTodo). Both are slow per-conversation heap leaks with no per-frame compute cost. The on-disk sidecar (cursors) and transcript (readSelfTodos) are authoritative fallbacks, so eviction is lossless for correctness.
acceptance_criteria: Both modules cap retained per-conversation state via LRU/TTL; evicted conversations transparently reload from disk on next touch; no behavior change for active conversations; tests cover eviction + reload.
close_reason: cursor states map now LRU-capped (default 256, lossless disk reload); dead in-memory replay buffer removed entirely. self-todo half obsolete: lib/self-todo.ts no longer exists.

title: perf(shim): bound subagent registry (terminal entries retained forever) (lcp-02ri F3)
description: lib/subagent-registry.ts _subagents Map never deletes entries — finalize() flips status to completed/failed but the entry stays forever (no _subagents.delete outside test reset). Heap grows O(total subagent dispatches over process lifetime). Worse, the read path snapshotSubagents() does [..._subagents.values()].map(clone).sort() on EVERY call, and listActiveSubagents()/handleSubagentList build on it — so the mobile subagent-bar enumeration is O(all-time dispatches), not O(active). Unbounded accumulator + history-wide map+sort on a per-poll read path. LOW severity today (modest dispatch counts) but a genuine instance of the lcp-02ri class.
acceptance_criteria: Retained terminal subagent entries are capped (ring buffer / LRU of last N, or dropped after a grace window); all 'running' entries always retained; enumeration cost no longer scales with all-time dispatch count; existing subagent-registry tests still pass.
close_reason: obsolete: lib/subagent-registry.ts was removed in a refactor; no subagent registry map exists in the current codebase

title: perf(shim): rotate/compact unbounded on-disk conversation replay log (lcp-02ri F1b)
description: Follow-up to the F1 read-side fix. lib/mobile-conversation-cursors.ts appendReplayFrame() appends to <conv>.frames.jsonl forever and the file is never rotated/truncated. The read path is now tail-bounded (PR off lcp-gukg), so reconnect read+parse no longer scales with history, but the FILE ITSELF still grows without bound on disk — a slow storage leak. Compact/rotate the replay file to the bounded TTL/MAX_FRAMES window (e.g. opportunistically rewrite-in-place on ack, keeping only frames within TTL and > last_ack_seq, capped at MAX_FRAMES). Slightly riskier than the read fix (rewrite-in-place vs append-only) so deferred to its own bead. Measured before read-fix: 50k-frame replay file cost 115ms to read+parse; after fix ~22ms but the 50k-line file remains on disk.
acceptance_criteria: Replay file size stays bounded by the MAX_FRAMES/TTL window over a long conversation; reconnect replay output unchanged; atomic rewrite (no torn file); regression test simulates a long conversation and asserts file line-count stays bounded.
close_reason: replay JSONL now compacted every 1000 appends to replay-eligible frames; deleted when fully acked. commit cad25a1

title: P2: Gate appendRunFrame async/batched persistence on profiling evidence
description: Remaining shim perf follow-up: evaluate appendRunFrame persistence cost under long streaming runs and only introduce async or batched persistence if profiling shows synchronous append/write cost is material.
acceptance_criteria: Profiling fixture measures appendRunFrame persistence cost under long runs; if material, implement async/batched persistence without weakening durability semantics; if not material, record evidence and close without code churn.

title: Shim: tag subagent/Task frames + expose live task status so the app can render fork/relay (enables companion non-blocking UI)
description:
## Why
The companion fork/relay model (letta-mobile-3aqu8 .3; spec reference/companion_ui_paradigm.md) is NATIVE in Letta Code: main agent spawns a subagent via the Task tool with run_in_background -> task_id; on finish a completion notification is auto-injected into the conversation; main reads it via TaskOutput. The clay glow + 'Working · N jobs' pill + 'btw…' relay message are the UI surfacing of that.

## Findings (admin-shim inspection 2026-06-02)
The mechanism already flows through the shim END TO END (the rig proves it — it spawns role subagents through this exact path). NOTHING is dropped. BUT the shim has NO semantic awareness of subagents:
- A Task-tool call arrives as a generic tool_call_message; its result as a tool_return_message. The shim cannot tell a subagent spawn from a Bash call.
- The background completion notification arrives as a generic injected message (likely user_message/system_message, or a tool_return when TaskOutput is called). No special handling.
- The shim's wire vocabulary is the 8 standard Letta message types (assistant/user/system/reasoning/tool_call/tool_return/approval_request/approval_response). There is NO task_id in the wire envelope and NO 'this is a fork/relay' tag.
- The only task_id handling in the shim is for CRON tasks, unrelated.
- Net: the app currently can't distinguish subagent activity from any other tool call without fragile tool-name sniffing.

## Work (this bead = the shim ENABLER; the app experience is letta-mobile-3aqu8)
1. **Tag subagent frames in the WS envelope.** When a frame corresponds to the Task tool / a background subagent, mark it with  + a  (e.g. subagent_spawn | subagent_status | subagent_complete) so the app keys off structure, not tool-name strings. Touch points: lib/translate.ts (frame reshape), lib/mobile-channel-host.ts (WS emission). Detect via the Task tool name + the run_in_background task_id + the completion-notification shape.
2. **Expose live task status for a conversation.** A read surface ('what subagent task_ids are running right now for this conversation', with status) so the app can drive the clay glow (active count + load) and the 'Working · N jobs ›' pill. Either a small endpoint (GET /conversations/:id/tasks or /v1/agents/:id/tasks) or fold task state into the existing mobile WS state frame. OVERLAPS lcp-61uj (vibesync rig fleet status is the rig-side analog — keep the shapes consistent; the glow consumes both).
3. **Do not gate sends on an active run.** Confirm the mobile WS send path is NOT blocked while a run/task is active (non-blocking composer). This also helps dissolve lcp-gukg.

## Acceptance
- Subagent spawn / status / completion frames are tagged with task_id + frame_kind on the mobile WS, distinguishable from ordinary tool calls without tool-name sniffing.
- The app can query/observe live active task_ids + status for the conversation.
- Sends are never blocked by an active run/task.
- The completion notification is identifiable so the app can render it as the 'btw…' relay message.

## Refs
letta-mobile-3aqu8 (companion paradigm epic; this is its shim dependency — build shim tagging FIRST, then app renders), reference/companion_ui_paradigm.md (DEFINITIVE native-subagent section), lcp-61uj (rig fleet status — keep task-status shape consistent), lcp-gukg (the hang this non-blocking model dissolves), docs.letta.com/letta-code/subagents.

comments.author: Claude Code
comments.text:
## Live experiment (2026-06-02) — the RELAY is the hard part, not the fork

Tested fork/relay empirically from Meridian's live session:

1. **codex shell-out fork (dispatching-coding-agents path):** spawned fine via background Bash, but I LOST THE RESULT — the codex output never made it back to a channel I could read (the bg log captured only my echoes + exit 0). Proves: the shell-out path has NO reliable return channel to the main agent. You can fork, but the relay silently fails. NOT suitable as the companion fork primitive.

2. **Native Task tool:** confirmed it IS plumbed into the shim-wrapped session. admin-shim/scripts/letta-cli-sdk-wrapper.mjs (vibesync-0u15) explicitly propagates the patch loader to NESTED subagent node processes via NODE_OPTIONS — comment: 'child node processes that letta.js spawns for Agent/Task subagents do NOT inherit explicit argv... without the loader the subagent's Anthropic request goes out with thinking:{type:enabled} and no budget_tokens... the exact error that fails every nested subagent dispatch.' So the deployment actively supports native Task subagents.

### Conclusion that sharpens this bead
- The companion fork MUST use the **native Task tool** (auto-injected completion notification = the relay channel), NOT shell-out coding agents (no return channel).
- The load-bearing question for THIS bead is therefore: **does the native Task completion-notification frame survive the shim and reach the mobile client (and the agent's own context) intact?** That is the relay. Frame-tagging (task_id + frame_kind) must specifically cover the auto-injected completion notification so the app can render it as the 'btw…' relay message and the agent reliably reacts to it.
- Relay surfacing is SIMPLE per Emmanuel: a completed fork = the agent just responds to the user with a small animation cue. No special result card. So app work = (a) animation cue on relay arrival, (b) glow/pill from live task_ids. The hard part is purely the shim faithfully carrying the completion notification.

comments.author: Claude Code
comments.text:
## RELAY CONFIRMED LIVE END-TO-END (2026-06-02) — the load-bearing unknown is answered: YES

Ran the full fork/relay paradigm live from Meridian's session via the native Task tool:
- Spawned task_1 (general-purpose subagent, run_in_background) to research the clay-glow Compose+AGSL pattern.
- Explicitly routed it to model lmstudio/gpt-5.3-codex-spark — VERIFIED it resolved to gpt-5.3-codex-spark (per-spawn model override WORKS; no silent opus-inherit fallback). NOTE: the prior spawn with default auto/inherit silently became opus-4-8 — concrete evidence for lcp-1lod.
- I stayed fully interactive with Emmanuel while it ran (non-blocking confirmed).
- **The completion <task-notification> was AUTO-INJECTED into my conversation on completion — no polling.** It arrived intact THROUGH THE SHIM with the full result. So: the native-Task completion-notification DOES survive the shim back to the main agent's context. This was the open question for this bead — answered YES.

### What this narrows lcp-xbvp to
The relay MECHANISM (notification → main agent) is proven working through the shim today. The remaining work is purely the APP/PRESENTATION layer:
1. Tag the notification + Task frames (task_id + frame_kind) so the MOBILE app can render it as the 'btw…' relay message + animation cue (vs a raw tool/system frame). The data reaches the agent; need it cleanly typed for the app.
2. Expose live task_ids/status for the glow + 'Working · N jobs' pill.
The fork/relay model is no longer hypothetical — it ran end to end. Implementation is now just tagging + UI.

Also: the Spark fork returned a real, code-grounded glow implementation spec (shader-first + gradient-as-mask via BlendMode.DstIn; ThinkingShader wave_speed/frequency are hardcoded not uniforms; bgColor uniform is dead). Captured for letta-mobile-3aqu8 .2.

title: Expose conversation context/compaction introspection — current utilization, in-context tail, summary state
description:
## Problem
Agents/users need visibility into conversation context utilization and compaction state. During conv-16c2f589-a3f9-438c-bb63-75023a4785ea, we tried to answer 'what is current context utilization?' and the backend only exposed partial metadata:
- in_context_message_ids: 624
- isolated_block_ids: 0
- summary_len: 0
- messages endpoint: ~1361 total messages
But no token count, no context window size, no utilization %, no compaction threshold, and no clear place where the earlier CLI/system compaction summary is stored.

This matters because data introspection is operationally important for an agent: the agent should know when it is near compaction, whether it is running on a summarized history vs raw tail, and how much working memory it has left.

## Desired endpoint / tool surface
Expose conversation context introspection for a conversation, e.g.:
GET /v1/conversations/:id/context
or equivalent internal API/tool returning:
- conversation_id, agent_id
- total_message_count
- in_context_message_count
- isolated_block_count
- summary_present + summary_token_count / summary_char_count
- current_estimated_tokens
- context_window_tokens
- utilization_percent
- compaction_threshold_percent / remaining_tokens_estimate
- oldest/newest in-context message timestamps
- compaction history: last_compacted_at, messages_compacted_count, summary_id/location
- source breakdown: messages vs memory blocks vs system prompt/tools

## UI affordance
Expose this in the app/dev surface as a lightweight status/introspection panel:
- 'Context: 72% used'
- '624 messages in context / 1361 total'
- 'No summary present' or 'summary active, 389 msgs compacted'
- warning before compaction

## Acceptance
- An agent can query exact current context utilization for its conversation without guessing.
- The response includes token estimates and compaction state, not just message counts.
- The compaction summary/history is discoverable from the conversation metadata or a linked resource.
- The endpoint is safe for UI display and debugging.

## Notes
This is not just UX — it is agent operational telemetry. Without it, agents cannot reason about whether to summarize, split work, shorten turns, or preserve important state before compaction.

comments.author: Claude Code
comments.text:
## Correction / reframing (2026-06-02)

The context-utilization data already exists; I initially queried the wrong endpoint.

Incorrect endpoint checked:
- GET /v1/conversations/:conversation_id
- This returns conversation metadata (id, agent_id, in_context_message_ids, summary, timestamps) but NOT context-token utilization.

Correct endpoint used by letta-mobile:
- GET /v1/agents/:agent_id/context?conversation_id=:conversation_id
- Mobile source: AgentApi.getContextWindow()
- UI source: ContextWindowCard / ContextWindowUiState in feature-chat.

Existing response model (ContextWindowOverview) already includes:
- context_window_size_max
- context_window_size_current
- num_messages
- num_archival_memory
- num_recall_memory
- num_tokens_external_memory_summary
- num_tokens_system
- num_tokens_core_memory
- num_tokens_memory_filesystem
- num_tokens_tool_usage_rules
- num_tokens_directories
- num_tokens_summary_memory
- num_tokens_functions_definitions
- num_tokens_messages

So this bead should NOT be 'build the data from scratch'. Reframe as:

## New problem statement
The data exists, but it is not discoverable/agent-accessible enough. An agent trying to introspect its own context naturally checks /v1/conversations/:id and sees only partial metadata. The useful utilization endpoint is agent-scoped and undocumented from the conversation resource.

## Updated desired fixes
- Add an alias or linked endpoint: GET /v1/conversations/:id/context (internally resolve agent_id and call existing agent-context logic), OR include a context_url/link in GET /v1/conversations/:id.
- Add an internal tool / CLI command so an agent can ask 'what is my current context utilization?' without knowing the agent-scoped endpoint.
- Document the relationship between conversation metadata and context-window overview.
- Keep the existing mobile endpoint as source of truth; do not duplicate token logic.
- Optionally extend ContextWindowOverview with window strategy / compaction config fields if not already available: strategy=sliding_window|summary_plus_tail, sliding_window_percentage, compaction mode/model, last_compacted_at if tracked.

## Updated acceptance
- Agent and developer can discover context utilization from a conversation id alone.
- Existing /v1/agents/:agent_id/context remains source of truth.
- The endpoint/tool exposes the existing token breakdown and, if available, compaction strategy/config.

This remains important because agents need operational visibility, but the task is discoverability + alias/tooling, not creating the metrics from scratch.

title: vibesync: make model:auto role-aware and budget-aware — Opus only for architecture, Sonnet for implementation
description:
## Problem
The Gastown role files say model:auto / letta/auto, but vibesync does not implement real auto model routing. RoleAgentBootstrapper currently resolves every role agent to one global default (VIBESYNC_ROLE_AGENT_MODEL or lmstudio/sonnet-4-5). That means 'auto' is decorative, not strategic.

We hit Claude allotment pressure because expensive reasoning needs to be routed deliberately. Opus should be reserved for architecture / high-risk reasoning, NOT used as a default implementer. Implementation should usually be Sonnet; tester/refinery should be cheap/local where possible.

## Current state observed
- packs/gastown/.letta/agents/{coder,reviewer,tester,mayor,refinery}.md all have model:auto.
- packs/gastown/roles/*.toml all use model='letta/auto'.
- RoleAgentBootstrapper ignores role-specific auto semantics and uses DEFAULT_MODEL = VIBESYNC_ROLE_AGENT_MODEL ?? 'lmstudio/sonnet-4-5'.
- Actual persisted role agents checked through the shim show coder/reviewer/tester using sonnet-4-5.

## Desired behavior
Implement a real ModelRouter for model:auto resolution, using role + formula/step + task risk + budget mode.

Suggested initial policy:
- mayor / architect: Opus only for architecture/high-risk tasks, otherwise Sonnet.
- coder: Sonnet by default.
- reviewer: Sonnet by default; Opus only for architecture/security/state/transport reviews or premium budget mode.
- tester: cheap/local model where possible.
- refinery: cheap/local model.

Add budget mode:
- VIBESYNC_MODEL_BUDGET=conserve|balanced|premium
- conserve: never auto-pick Opus.
- balanced: Opus only for explicit architecture/high-risk steps.
- premium: mayor/architect can use Opus more freely.

## Implementation direction
- Add a ModelRouter used by RoleAgentBootstrapper and/or session start.
- Honor explicit role frontmatter model when not auto.
- Resolve auto via role-aware policy.
- Log resolved model in role-agent bootstrap / dispatcher events so usage is visible.
- Handle persistent role agents: update/recreate existing agents if their stored model no longer matches policy, or document that policy applies only to newly-created agents.
- Add env overrides, e.g. VIBESYNC_MODEL_CODER, VIBESYNC_MODEL_REVIEWER, VIBESYNC_MODEL_TESTER, VIBESYNC_MODEL_ARCHITECT.

## Acceptance
- model:auto no longer collapses to one global default for every role.
- Coder implementation workers do not consume Opus by default.
- Opus is gated behind architecture/high-risk/premium policy.
- Tester/refinery can route to cheaper/local models.
- Resolved model is observable in logs/events.

## Addendum: GPT-5.5 as intermediate escalation / second-order implementer

User clarification: **GPT-5.5** should be part of the policy as a strong intermediate tier before escalating to Opus. It is strong in its own right and can replace Opus for some cases.

4. Architecture, state/transport/security, ambiguous product/design reasoning, or reviewer escalation: Opus.

ModelRouter should support retry/escalation policy based on prior attempt outcome:

title: vibesync: lcp-mj0h auto-heal broke 14 provider unit tests (mocks don't stub POST /v1/agents); make CI tests a required gate
description:
## Symptom
14 tests in tests/unit/orchestration/runtime/letta-code-subagent-provider.test.ts fail on main with: 'LettaCodeSubagentProvider: failed to auto-create parent agent agent-pm (POST /v1/agents failed with 404): not found'. Confirmed pre-existing on main (d908495), independent of any later PR.

## Cause
The lcp-mj0h fix (auto-heal phantom parent agent) added a POST /v1/agents call to create a missing parent agent. The provider's existing unit tests (AgentIdResolver Phase C suite) use a fetch mock that returns 404 for POST /v1/agents — they were written before auto-heal existed — so every test exercising the agent_id path now throws.

## Two fixes
1. Update the provider test mocks to stub POST /v1/agents (return a created agent) OR to assert the auto-heal path, so the suite reflects the new behavior. (The auto-heal logic itself is correct; the tests are stale.)
2. PROCESS: the CI 'test' job is currently continue-on-error / NOT a required status check — only 'typecheck' is required. That is why lcp-mj0h merged with red tests. Make the test job a required status check on origin/main too (or at least non-continue-on-error), so a PR that breaks tests is blocked. This is the test-coverage half of the lcp-uye8 safety gate.

## Acceptance
- Provider unit tests pass on main.
- CI test job is required on main (red tests block merge).

title: vibesync: rig live-activity — bootstrap snapshot + SSE deltas pattern for a live UI
description:
## Gap (observed 2026-06-02)
vibesync has a live event stream (GET /api/events/stream, SSE) emitting the full dispatcher lifecycle (formula.queued/started/completed/failed/cancelled/resumed; step.started/finished/failed/retry/cancelled/role_agent_bootstrapped/task_recorded/reattached). But a live UI needs BOTH: (a) an initial SNAPSHOT of current state on load, then (b) subscribe to SSE for deltas. Today only (b) exists — the UI cannot show current runs until something CHANGES.

## Ask
- Pair the SSE stream with a bootstrap snapshot (the fleet-status endpoint above, or an initial 'replay current state' event on stream connect).
- Document/standardize the bootstrap-then-stream contract so the mobile/desktop client can render live rig activity reliably (mirrors the Letta messages/runs bootstrap+resume pattern).
- Ensure event payloads carry enough context (projectIdentifier, formulaName, stepName, moleculeId, status, timestamp) to update a UI without extra lookups.

## Acceptance
- A client can connect, get the current fleet state immediately, then receive live deltas — no blank-until-change window.
close_reason: DONE + merged (PR #15). SSE snapshot-on-connect: SSEManager.addClient(res, snapshotFn?) sends an initial 'snapshot' event (molecules + fleet) immediately on /api/events/stream connect, then live deltas — no blank-until-change window. Produced by the rig, reviewed by Meridian (clean +80/-2, typechecks, backward-compat), passed the typecheck gate, merged via the PR-only flow. NOTE: rig molecule reported status=failed (lcp-98y8 timeout false-negative — tester step didn't run) but the work was sound; verified manually. Pairs with lcp-61uj for the rig-visibility data layer.

title: vibesync: add fleet-status endpoint — GET /molecules (list active + queued runs) for rig dashboards
description:
## Gap (observed 2026-06-02)
vibesync exposes per-molecule data (GET /molecules/:id, /trace, /events) but there is NO list/fleet endpoint. You can only query a molecule if you already know its id. A rig-status UI cannot answer 'what is running right now?' on load. The dispatcher HAS the data internally (getActiveMoleculeCount, getQueueDepth, activeMolecules, moleculeQueue) but only getQueueDepth is used (formulas.ts:25) and none is on the API.

## Ask
Add GET /molecules (or /api/rig/status) returning the live fleet:
- active molecules: id, projectIdentifier, formulaName, current step, status, startedAt, elapsed
- queued molecules + queue depth
- counts (active/queued)
Source from the dispatcher's existing active/queue state (expose getActiveMolecules()/getQueued() if needed).

## Why
First-class requirement for any rig dashboard / live-activity UI (mobile + desktop). Also feeds the paid-rig tier story ('see your coordinated dev team working').

## Acceptance
- One GET returns all currently-running + queued molecules with enough per-run detail to render a CI-style dashboard, without needing to know ids in advance.
close_reason: DONE + verified live + merged (PR #14). GET /molecules fleet-status endpoint: lists active+recent runs with UI-ready per-run summaries (formulaName, motivatingBeadId, status, stepCounts total/done/running, currentStep) + fleet counts (active/queueDepth). Query: ?status=open,in_progress (default active) | ?status=all | ?limit=N. Built store.listMoleculeRoots -> walker.listMolecules -> endpoint; test fixture updated. Verified against today's real molecules. Typecheck-gate green, merged through the PR-only safety flow. First of the rig-visibility API set; feeds mobile rig surface letta-mobile-n8zi5.

title: vibesync: per-project orchestration config is hardcoded to letta-code-parallel — every new project needs a code edit
description:
## Observed (lcp-yb3z fix, 2026-06-02)
Enabling letta-mobile dispatch required editing src/index.ts because packDirsByProject and storageDirsByProject were hardcoded literals: { 'letta-code-parallel': ... }. buildRoleAgentContextResolver returns null if a project is missing from these maps, silently breaking dispatch (coder times out with no agent). I had to add 'letta-mobile' by hand.

## Problem
Onboarding ANY new project to the rig requires a source edit + redeploy. Not scalable, easy to forget, fails SILENTLY (resolver returns null -> coder times out -> opaque failure). Three separate config sources had to agree (hardcoded maps + project_provider_routing DB row + a real PM agent) with no single 'enable project for rig' path.

## Fix direction
- Derive packDir/storageDir from project config (DB row / .beads metadata / a default) instead of hardcoded maps. Default packDir=packs/gastown, storageDir=the shared local-backend, overridable per project.
- A single command/endpoint to 'enable a project for orchestration' that sets routing + ensures a PM agent + validates the context resolves (instead of 3 manual steps).
- Make resolver-returns-null LOUD: log a clear warning naming the missing piece (packDir? storageDir? routing? PM agent?) instead of silently falling through to a timeout.

## Acceptance
- Adding a new project to the rig needs no source edit.
- One action enables a project end-to-end (routing + PM agent + context).
- Missing config produces a clear diagnostic, not a silent coder timeout.

title: vibesync: project letta_agent_id can point at a phantom (non-existent) PM agent — no validation, opaque 400
description:
## Observed (lcp-yb3z, 2026-06-02)
letta-mobile.letta_agent_id referenced agent-7e139a26 which did NOT exist in the shim store. The LettaCodeSubagentProvider passed it as parentAgentId to POST /v1/conversations, which 400'd: 'agent_id required (and must exist)'. The role agent itself was created fine, but the PHANTOM PM parent killed the run. I had to create a real PM agent + repoint by hand.

## Problem
Nothing validates that a project's configured PM/parent agent actually exists before dispatch. A stale/phantom letta_agent_id produces an opaque 'agent_id required (and must exist)' 400 deep in the conversation-create path, with no hint that the PARENT agent is the problem.

## Fix direction
- On project-enable (and/or at dispatch start), validate the PM/parent agent exists in the shim (probe it); if missing, auto-create it via the shim create endpoint (POST /v1/agents) and persist the new id — or fail with a clear message naming the phantom agent.
- The LettaCodeSubagentProvider should surface 'parent agent <id> does not exist' rather than the raw shim 400.

## Acceptance
- A phantom letta_agent_id is either auto-healed (PM recreated) or reported with a clear 'PM agent <id> missing' error, not a generic shim 400.

title: Pinch-to-zoom chat reflow: frame rate too low during the gesture — perf acceleration
description:
## Problem
The pinch-to-zoom live text reflow drops frames — FPS is too low during the gesture. This is the perf side of the live-reflow system (the correctness side is lcp-4fce: settled messages not reflowing + scale-down gap). Fixing the gap (per-frame re-measure of visible items) will ADD measurement cost, so perf must be addressed alongside.

## Why it's expensive
Every pointer frame during the pinch, in-window items re-measure + reflow real text (intentional, to avoid blurry bitmap scaling). MarkdownText overrides LocalDensity with a scaledDensity and the markdown lib re-lays-out sp text per frame. Step is fine-grained (PinchScalePreviewController step=0.02), so many distinct scale values -> many re-measures.

## Acceleration ideas (to evaluate)
1. Velocity-adaptive step: coarse step (e.g. 0.06-0.10) during fast pinch movement, fine step (0.02) only when the gesture is settling/slow. Cuts the number of distinct re-measures during fast zooms. Cheapest win.
2. Hybrid scale: graphicsLayer (bitmap) scale for the in-flight gesture frames, swap to real reflow only on a short debounce / on commit. PR #280 moved AWAY from bitmap scale due to blur — but a hybrid that bitmap-scales DURING fast motion and reflows when motion slows could keep crispness where it matters (steady state) while staying smooth during motion.
3. Pre-measure scale buckets: warm the geometry cache at a few common buckets (e.g. 0.85 / 1.0 / 1.15 / 1.3) so frequent zoom levels hit cached geometry instead of re-measuring.
4. Tighter viewport window: re-check scaleWindowIndexRange margins — re-measuring fewer off-screen-prefetch items during the gesture.
5. Cache the markdown PARSE (AST) across scale changes; only the layout/measure should change with scale, not the parse. Confirm the lib isn't re-parsing per frame.
6. Snap-to-bucket on release with a single final re-measure (already partly done via 8vivd cache re-seed) — ensure only ONE settle re-measure, not a cascade.

## Suggested approach
Profile first (systrace/Perfetto during a pinch) to find whether the cost is re-measure, re-parse, or recomposition. Then likely combine (1) velocity-adaptive step + (3) bucket warming as the low-risk wins, reserving (2) hybrid bitmap for if real reflow can't hit 60fps on target devices.

## Refs
lcp-4fce (gap/correctness), PR #280 (bitmap->real reflow), letta-mobile-6261e/8u662/8vivd/8vivd (the live-reflow system). Device: Pixel 9 Pro.

title: Pinch-to-zoom: settled messages don't live-reflow (geometry cache keyed on committed scale); scale-down leaves a transient gap
description:
## Symptoms
1. During a pinch-zoom of the chat, the USER's own (settled) messages do NOT reflow live — they stay at the pre-gesture size and only snap to the new size on gesture RELEASE. The agent's streaming/recent messages DO reflow live, creating a visible asymmetry.
2. On scale-DOWN specifically, a large empty GAP appears in the conversation (between the last message and the composer) and only disappears after a delay (when the deferred re-measure runs). Screenshot confirms a big mid-list void after pinching down.

## Root cause (traced, letta-mobile feature-chat)
The live pinch has TWO halves that must agree, and they disagree for cached items:
- TEXT scale: ChatMessageList provides  (live value for in-window items) — MarkdownText reads LocalChatFontScale.current and scales sp via scaledDensity. So text CONTENT wants to reflow live. (MarkdownText.kt:159/439, scaledDensity ~498.)
- GEOMETRY/measure cache: MeasuredChatRenderItem keys cached item geometry on chatGeometrySignature(...), which uses  — the COMMITTED scale (ChatMessageGeometry.kt:87). The call site passes  (ChatMessageList.kt:307), NOT perItemFontScale, even for in-window items during a pinch.

Result: settled/cached items keep their committed measured height through the whole gesture; only items that bypass the cache (streaming/live) reflow. The user's settled messages are fully cached -> frozen until commit. On scale-down, the measured heights stay LARGE while content shrinks -> phantom gap until the deferred re-measure (on release) collapses it.

## Fix
For items where itemSeesLiveScale is true (in the pinch window), build the geometry signature with  instead of , so the cache key changes per frame and the item re-measures live (no frozen height, no gap). Keep  for out-of-window items (cheap, cached). Change at ChatMessageList.kt ~301-307 (thread perItemFontScale into chatGeometrySignature when in-window).

## Perf caveat
This was deliberately bucketed on committed scale to avoid per-frame re-measure cost. The fix re-introduces per-frame measurement for VISIBLE settled items during a pinch — bounded by the existing viewport window (scaleWindowIndexRange), so only on-screen items. Acceptable but related to the separate FPS bead below; the two should be evaluated together so we don't fix the gap at the cost of frame rate.

## Refs
PR #280 (removed graphicsLayer bitmap scale to enable live LocalChatFontScale reflow), letta-mobile-6261e (real text re-layout during pinch), 8u662 (viewport-bounded scale window), 8vivd (cache re-seed on gesture end).

title: Regression: markdown image URLs in chat render as text, not images (streaming renderer path)
description:
## Symptom
A markdown image in an agent chat message — `![alt](https://...)` or a bare image URL — renders as TEXT/link, not an inline image. Emmanuel reports this as a REGRESSION (it worked before). Verified the feature is intended: MarkdownText.kt imports Coil3ImageTransformerImpl and wires imageTransformer=Coil3ImageTransformerImpl (line ~511), so markdown images are supposed to render via Coil.

## Located cause (mobile, letta-mobile)
MessageContentFactory chooses the renderer:
- Messages that STREAMED in this composition keep using StreamingMarkdownText even after settling, to avoid a handoff flash (letta-mobile-9hcg.b / yh0c). 
- Only HYDRATED (history-loaded) messages use MarkdownText (which has the image transformer).
StreamingMarkdownText (designsystem) splits content into completed-prefix blocks rendered via MarkdownText (line ~365, has transformer) and an active TAIL rendered as plain Text (line ~451, NO transformer).

So a live (streamed) message with an image URL renders via StreamingMarkdownText; the image either sits in the plain-Text tail or otherwise doesn't reach the Coil transformer. After app restart (hydrated) it should render via MarkdownText. That streaming-vs-settled split is the regression surface — a flicker fix traded away live inline-image rendering.

## Fix direction (verify on device first)
1. Confirm: does a streamed message's settled prefix-block MarkdownText (line 365) actually pass imageTransformer? If the prefix MarkdownText is a reduced/!image variant, restore the transformer there.
2. Ensure the active-tail plain Text path doesn't strip a completed image block.
3. Possibly: a standalone image-URL line should be treated as a completed block (not held in the plain-text tail).
4. Confirm Coil3ImageTransformerImpl loads remote https:// (not just data:/local) — and that it's not an auth/domain issue for the test URL.

## Acceptance
- An agent message containing `![](https://public-image-url)` renders the image inline in the chat bubble, live (not only after restart).

## Notes
Separate from the now-working Read-image / tool-result image render (commit 71a1897 shim + 25ff3021 mobile) and A2UI Image-by-URL (works). This is specifically the MARKDOWN image path in assistant chat text. No uncommitted/stashed changes are the cause (working tree clean on branch fix/tool-return-image-attachments); regression is in committed streaming-renderer logic.

title: VibeSync/beads Dolt port drift — multiple stale dolt servers, dispatch + letta-mobile bead rig broken
description:
## Symptom
1. Dispatching any formula for project letta-mobile via vibesync fails at start: { error: 'Failed to start formula run', 500, details: { error: 'connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:40771' } }. The dispatcher resolves a dolt port (40771) that nothing is listening on.
2. 'bd' commands against the letta-mobile rig fail: 'no issue found matching letta-mobile-x34f2' — the rig cannot resolve its issues because its dolt server port reference is stale/wrong. (Confirms earlier journal errors: 'database vibesync not found on Dolt server'.)

## Cause
Dolt port drift across multiple rigs. ps shows ~10 'dolt sql-server' processes on assorted ports (45495, 36297, 36945, 39123, 34771, 36427, 39249, 35773, 36315, 44265...), spawned at different times (May25, May31). Each beads rig spins its own dolt sql-server; ports get reassigned on restart; stale .beads/dolt-server.port references break. vibesync's project_provider_routing also reads via dolt and is unreachable on the resolved port, so persistent-role-agent routing for letta-mobile can't resolve.

## Impact
- Cannot dispatch fixes through the rig for affected projects (hit while trying to dispatch letta-mobile-x34f2; had to patch directly).
- Cannot read/write letta-mobile beads (so x34f2 couldn't be updated; its diagnosis lives in commit 25ff3021 message instead).
- General: bead tracking and rig orchestration unreliable until port references are reconciled.

## Fix direction
- Reconcile dolt server ports: one canonical dolt sql-server per rig, correct .beads/dolt-server.port + .pid, kill orphaned/duplicate servers. Re-bootstrap the letta-mobile beads rig (bd bootstrap) so it points at a live server.
- Consider a single shared dolt server / port registry to stop the per-restart drift (root cause: each rig self-spawns + reassigns).
- Verify vibesync project_provider_routing resolves after the dolt fix (it was empty in logs/sync-state.db; routing likely lives in dolt).

## Acceptance
- vibesync can start a formula run for letta-mobile (no ECONNREFUSED).
- bd commands resolve letta-mobile issues.
- No orphaned duplicate dolt sql-servers; each rig has one live server its references point at.

## Note
Accumulating since ~May 25 (oldest dolt procs). Worth a focused infra session — touches the data store the whole tracking + rig system depends on; do not rush.
close_reason: FULLY FIXED + verified. vibesync can now dispatch AND execute letta-mobile work end-to-end. Three stacked root causes fixed: (1) no-db port-sweep blocked dispatch entry — isNoDbBeads guard (commit 3fafce6); (2) letta-mobile missing from hardcoded packDirsByProject/storageDirsByProject + no provider_provider_routing — added both (commit 14e68d7 + DB row); (3) letta-mobile.letta_agent_id was a PHANTOM PM agent (agent-7e139a26 not in shim) causing POST /v1/conversations 400 — created real PM-letta-mobile agent (agent-c356b54a) + repointed. Verified: probe molecule completed, coder/reviewer/tester executed against the real repo (read branch, counted 113 .kt files, tester PASS). comments.author: Claude Code
comments.text:
## Root cause found — vibesync dispatcher assumes dolt-SERVER, letta-mobile uses EMBEDDED dolt (2026-06-02)

Tried to dispatch awbf (design-system refactor) for letta-mobile via vibesync; same ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:40771 at run start.

Traced:
- vibesync src/orchestration/store/dolt-client.ts:110 reads the dolt port from the DISPATCHED PROJECT's .beads/dolt-server.port and connects to a dolt SQL SERVER.
- letta-mobile's bd uses EMBEDDED dolt (in-process, no server): 'Dolt engine: embedded — Data: /opt/stacks/letta-mobile/.beads/embeddeddolt'. There is NO dolt-server.port for letta-mobile because it doesn't run a server. So the dispatcher resolves a stale/garbage port (40771, which corresponds to a dolt server that died May 30) and connection refused.
- So this is NOT just stale-port drift — it's an ARCHITECTURE MISMATCH: vibesync's dolt-client requires a per-project dolt SQL server, but letta-mobile (and possibly other projects) run embedded dolt. The port-drift symptom is downstream of that.

Additional findings:
- 49 'dolt sql-server' processes are currently running (major process leak / orphan accumulation). Ports 33xxx-35xxx live; the dispatcher wants 40771 (dead).
- letta-mobile/.beads has an embeddeddolt.corrupt-20260527-081309 dir — a prior corruption was quarantined. Worth noting for data integrity.

## Fix options
A. Run a persistent dolt SQL server for letta-mobile (bd dolt server / set port), record the port in .beads/dolt-server.port, and ensure vibesync reads the live one. Brings letta-mobile in line with vibesync's server assumption.
B. Make vibesync's dolt-client support embedded-mode projects (connect to the embeddeddolt data dir directly, or shell out to bd instead of a SQL port). More general — fixes ALL embedded-dolt projects.
C. Reap the 49 orphan dolt servers regardless (process hygiene) + a single canonical server per rig.

Recommend B for generality (vibesync should handle both engine modes) + C for hygiene. A is the quick unblock if we just need letta-mobile dispatchable now.

Until fixed, vibesync CANNOT dispatch letta-mobile work (e.g. the awbf design-system refactor). Direct/manual dispatch (goal agent without vibesync) remains the fallback.

title: Read-tool images render as placeholder, not model vision (local backend tool-result image path drops them)
description:
## Symptom
When Meridian uses the Read tool on a local image file (e.g. a saved Mobbin design ref PNG), the image does NOT reach the model's vision — the result is a placeholder tag (`[Image: file.png]` / '(see attached image)'), not viewable pixels. Chat-attached images from the user DO work (verified — the pierogi photo), so the multimodal model path itself is fine. The gap is specifically the Read-tool -> tool-result -> model-input conversion on the local backend.

## Why this matters
Blocks Meridian from viewing local images directly (design-reference audits, screenshots, any image-on-disk). Today the only way to see an image is the user attaching it in chat. Want Read(image) to feed vision too.

## Diagnosis so far (EMPIRICAL, 2026-06-01)
Traced the bundled letta.js (/root/.bun/install/global/node_modules/@letta-ai/letta-code/letta.js):
- Found toChatMessages(messages, supportsImages) at ~line 129353 — gates images on supportsImages; filters them to '(image omitted: model does not support images)' when false. It has a debug hook writing /tmp/imgdbg.log.
- **KEY: cleared /tmp/imgdbg.log, did a real Read of a PNG, log stayed EMPTY.** => toChatMessages is NOT the converter the local backend uses for tool-result images. The supportsImages/model.input gate I first suspected is the WRONG path. Do not patch toChatMessages.
- Other candidate converters (still to confirm which fires for local-backend tool results): line ~76552 Gemini functionResponse/inlineData path (gates on model.input.includes('image')); ~130987 responses path ('(see attached image)'); ~179003 the [Image / type:image construction.

## Also done (committed, correct regardless)
admin-shim model-catalog.ts: all Claude models (opus 4-5/6/7/8, sonnet-4-6, haiku-4-5) were capabilities:['text'] — fixed to ['text','vision'] (commit 7b93141). But /v1/models -> vanillaModel does NOT emit any vision/image field, and the local backend resolves model.input from the bundled provider registry, not from the shim — so the catalog fix alone does not flip the gate.

## Next step (focused)
Identify WHICH converter the local backend invokes for a Read tool-result containing an image (add a debug line to each candidate converter OR trace the local-backend turn-assembly call chain), then either (a) ensure that path includes image parts for our model, or (b) ensure the resolved model.input for lmstudio/opus-4-8 includes 'image'. The fix is likely a patch-loader injection (models.json is compiled-in, no external override) OR teaching local-backend model resolution to read vision capability.

## Acceptance
- Read on a local PNG/JPG/WebP results in Meridian actually describing the image content (pixels reach vision), not a placeholder tag.
notes: Post-completion recheck: reran npm run typecheck, node --import tsx/esm --test test/patch-loader.test.ts (9 pass), npm run build, systemctl restart lettashim.service, service active, health OK. Fresh strict acceptance conv-07dc35c6-c825-45a0-b6a7-299728151c9c returned strict-png.png: P-731 RED, strict-jpg.jpg: J-482 GREEN, strict-webp.webp: W-956 BLUE. Persisted storage check for that conversation found exactly 3 toolResult rows and all 3 include image parts with mime/data lengths: image/png 14044, image/jpeg 24020, image/png 66472.

title: Wire up letta-code-parallel project for vibesync rig dispatch — letta_base_url + parent_agent_id
description:
## Mandate

Vibesync rig dispatch fails for letta-code-parallel with ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:45455. Traced to two missing pieces:

1. **Stale letta_base_url in the projects row** — the dispatcher's per-project provider resolver reads projects.letta_base_url and dials it. Currently points at port 45455 which was an ephemeral admin-shim instance that has since died.
2. **No parent_agent_id set on the lcp project** — vibesync project shows 'Letta Agent ID: none'. The LettaCodeSubagentProvider needs a parentAgentId to spawn role agents.

When both are missing, the resolver falls back to the boot-default provider, which itself requires VIBESYNC_LETTA_CODE_SHIM_URL and VIBESYNC_LETTA_CODE_PARENT_AGENT_ID — neither set in the running vibesync process at PID 4048713 (verified via /proc/4048713/environ).

## What needs to happen

For the lcp project to dispatch formulas through vibesync:

1. Pick a long-lived admin-shim instance to route through. The lettashim systemd unit binds to 8291 by default. So:
   - letta_base_url = http://localhost:8291 (or wherever lcp wants its dispatcher to land)
2. Pick a parent_agent_id for lcp's letta-code subagent provider. This is the Letta agent that role-agents (coder, mayor, reviewer, tester) get spawned under via the shim.

The vibesync CLI exposes  for the URL piece. The agent id piece may need a direct DB update or a different verb.

## Boot-level fallback (alternative)

If per-project wiring isn't desired, set the boot-level env vars on the running vibesync process and restart it:

  VIBESYNC_LETTA_CODE_SHIM_URL=http://localhost:8291
  VIBESYNC_LETTA_CODE_PARENT_AGENT_ID=<some agent id>

This makes every project that doesn't have a per-project override use the same shim and parent.

## Why this is filed as a chore not a bug

This is operational wiring that's expected to need attention after the backend migration. Emmanuel flagged in earlier conversation: 'I have had to rebuild a few of the primitives but we're almost ready to stitch everything back together.' This bead documents the specific missing piece.

## Test for completion

Run: vibesync rig dispatch onboard-feature --rig letta-code-parallel --input 'test' --motivating-bead lcp-h7z

Should return moleculeId + status, not HTTP 500.

## Related

- lcp-h7z (P3) — the bead waiting for this wiring to be functional
- vibesync-ltqj (epic) — meridian agent tooling epic; this is operational follow-up after the CLI surface landed

comments.author: Claude Code
comments.text:
## Investigation update 2026-05-28 15:58 EDT

The 45455 ECONNREFUSED + the silent dispatch failure trace to a deeper issue:

1. The running vibesync server (PID 4048713) has uptime 6d18h — predates the meridian-tools rig CLI merge that landed today (commit 0cc344d).
2. The orchestration plane bootstrap is wrapped in try/catch (src/index.ts:398) that swallows errors as 'continuing without it' warnings. So if VIBESYNC_LETTA_CODE_SHIM_URL or VIBESYNC_LETTA_CODE_PARENT_AGENT_ID is missing at boot, the plane is silently disabled.
3. Reading the per-project resolver source (src/orchestration/boot.ts:253): parentAgentIds map is declared but never populated from projects.letta_agent_id. So setting projects.letta_agent_id in the DB has no effect — the resolver always returns null from the per-project branch.

The DB columns ARE now set correctly:
- letta_code_parallel.letta_base_url = http://localhost:8291
- letta_code_parallel.provider_kind = letta-code-subagent
- letta_code_parallel.letta_agent_id = agent-a9db7a7a-0ca7-4a3a-b124-11e8ab7fd7e1 (PM-vibesync)

But this alone is not sufficient because the resolver doesn't consume letta_agent_id from the DB. Two real fixes needed:

### Option A: boot env vars (operational)

Restart vibesync with:
  VIBESYNC_LETTA_CODE_SHIM_URL=http://localhost:8291
  VIBESYNC_LETTA_CODE_PARENT_AGENT_ID=agent-a9db7a7a-0ca7-4a3a-b124-11e8ab7fd7e1

This makes every project use the same shim+parent. Simplest path. May not work for multi-project dispatch if different projects want different parents.

### Option B: patch the resolver (code fix)

Modify buildProviderResolver in src/orchestration/boot.ts:216-281 to read letta_agent_id from the projects row (via store.getProjectProviderRouting which returns ProjectProviderRouting — extend that to include letta_agent_id) and use it as the parentAgentId for per-project resolution. Then the DB row I set above would be enough.

This is the architecturally correct fix and would let lcp use PM-vibesync as its dispatcher parent while other projects use their own.

## Recommendation

Option A as a quick unblock to verify the end-to-end dispatch loop works. Option B as the durable fix to file as its own follow-up.

## Workaround status

dispatch via vibesync rig CLI: still failing (this bead's original symptom)
the bead it's gating (lcp-h7z) is documented self-contained for any agent picking it up directly without going through the dispatcher

title: [epic] Desktop binary embeds Letta Code + admin-shim — single-binary self-contained install
description:
## Mandate (Emmanuel, 2026-05-27 ~22:53 EDT)

Made explicit during the Projects tree discussion:

> 'we really do need to make the kotlin app host the letta code server and the shim internally we already have the primitive'

The desktop story per multiplatform_roadmap.md Phase 3 (Windows-first, single binary, no separate services) requires the Compose Desktop app to internally launch and supervise both:

1. **Letta Code** — the agent runtime (TypeScript, Node-hosted; can run as a child process via system Node, embedded Node via JNI, or potentially via nodejs-mobile-on-desktop)
2. **admin-shim** — the transport layer (TypeScript, Node-hosted, same options)

All UI in the Compose Desktop app talks to the LOCAL shim over loopback WS — same protocol Letta Mobile uses against a remote shim. The host-FS / git / beads / cli access goes through the local shim, never directly from Compose.

This is the desktop equivalent of the mobile architecture: shim mediates everything, app is a thin host. Difference: on desktop the shim has authority to touch the local filesystem (because it IS the local user's machine); on mobile the shim runs on a server and the user explicitly approves what host-FS roots it can see.

## Why this lives in lcp

The shim source is here. The Letta Code source is here. The supervisor / launcher code that bundles both into a single distributable binary is most naturally also here — the mobile app consumes the published artifacts, doesn't need to know about the bundling story.

## Scope

### What this provides

1. **Embedded runtime launcher** — Kotlin/JVM code that knows how to:
   - Locate or extract a bundled Node runtime
   - Spawn Letta Code as a child process with the right env
   - Spawn admin-shim as a child process with the right env (pointing at the local Letta Code)
   - Monitor both, restart on crash, surface health to the UI
   - Clean shutdown on app exit

2. **Single-binary distribution** — jpackage / jlink wrapper that produces:
   - Windows: `.msi` or `.exe` installer with bundled JVM + Node + Letta Code + shim
   - macOS: `.dmg` with bundled JRE + Node + Letta Code + shim (later)
   - Linux: `.AppImage` or `.deb` with same (later)

3. **Process supervision** — basic restart-on-crash, max-restart-rate limiting, log capture, surfaced via a Desktop-only 'System' tab in Admin

4. **Loopback discovery** — Compose Desktop app finds the local shim at a known port (or ephemeral port + handshake file in user data dir), establishes WS, treats it as the canonical backend

5. **Data directory layout** — `%LOCALAPPDATA%/Letta` (Windows) / `~/Library/Application Support/Letta` (macOS) / `~/.local/share/letta` (Linux) for:
   - Letta Code state (memfs, conversations, runs)
   - Shim state (cursors, capabilities, audit log)
   - Provider credentials (in OS keychain, not flat file — see letta-mobile-0t8vf)

### What this does NOT provide

- Mobile equivalents (mobile uses different primitive — nodejs-mobile per lcp-59c)
- Auto-update mechanism (separate epic)
- Code signing for installers (separate operational concern)
- Telemetry beacon (separate; see letta-mobile-13mkq for the perf telemetry story)
- Migration from existing remote-shim install on the same machine (defer; v1 assumes fresh install)

## Tickets

### Runtime embedding strategy
1. **lcp-desktop.1** — Decision bead: Node runtime delivery mechanism — bundled system-style Node vs nodejs-mobile-on-JVM vs Bun. Spike each, pick one. (P2, gating)
2. **lcp-desktop.2** — Reference implementation: standalone Kotlin/JVM example launching Letta Code + shim from a test harness. Proves the supervision model end-to-end before integrating into Compose. (P2, blocked on lcp-desktop.1)

### Supervisor
3. **lcp-desktop.3** — `RuntimeSupervisor` Kotlin class: spawn / monitor / restart / shutdown for both child processes (P2)
4. **lcp-desktop.4** — Health probe — periodic check that both processes respond; report status via StateFlow consumable from Compose (P2)
5. **lcp-desktop.5** — Crash log capture — process stdout/stderr to rotating files in user data dir; viewable from Admin → System (P2)

### Compose Desktop integration
6. **lcp-desktop.6** — Compose Desktop app skeleton that boots, launches supervisor, waits for shim ready, opens main UI (P2)
7. **lcp-desktop.7** — Admin → System tab showing process status, log tail, restart buttons (P3)

### Distribution
8. **lcp-desktop.8** — jpackage / jlink build script for Windows .exe with bundled JRE + Node + Letta Code + shim (P2)
9. **lcp-desktop.9** — Same for macOS .dmg (P3, after Windows ships)
10. **lcp-desktop.10** — Same for Linux .AppImage / .deb (P3)
11. **lcp-desktop.11** — Code signing setup (Windows Authenticode + Apple Developer ID + Linux GPG) — separate but coordinated work (P3)

### Data layout
12. **lcp-desktop.12** — Per-OS data directory paths defined and respected by both Letta Code and shim (P2)
13. **lcp-desktop.13** — First-launch initialization — create data directory, generate keys, seed default config (P2)
14. **lcp-desktop.14** — Uninstaller behavior — preserve user data by default, opt-in to full removal (P3)

### Cross-cutting
15. **lcp-desktop.15** — Documentation for the embedding + distribution flow (P2)
16. **lcp-desktop.16** — End-to-end smoke test in CI: build the bundle, install it in a clean Windows VM, verify it boots and serves a chat (P2)

## Acceptance

- A user downloads a single .exe (Windows v1), double-clicks, app opens within 10s with Letta Code + shim already running
- Closing the app cleanly shuts down both child processes within 5s
- Crashing either child process triggers automatic restart with telemetry log
- User can configure providers (per letta-mobile-0t8vf) and start chatting without ever opening a terminal or editing a config file
- App survives reboot and resumes with all conversations / memory / providers intact
- No port conflicts when multiple instances of the app are launched (loopback discovery handles port allocation)

## Non-goals

- Mobile embedding (different primitive; see lcp-59c)
- Cross-platform on day one — Windows first, others follow
- Live-reload during dev (separate dev-mode concern)
- GUI for editing shim or Letta Code config (use the existing config-file path for v1; provider provisioning is the only required UI per letta-mobile-0t8vf)

## Sequencing relative to other work

This epic is a **prerequisite for shipping the desktop binary to non-engineers**, but NOT a prerequisite for Compose Desktop development. Order:

1. Land the data layer for letta-mobile-deol1 (Projects tree) — works against any shim
2. Land letta-mobile-0t8vf (provider provisioning UI) — works against any shim
3. **In parallel**: this epic — the desktop binary that hosts a local shim
4. Combine: Compose Desktop builds against the embedded shim instead of pointing at a remote one
5. Multiplatform-roadmap Phase 3 (Windows-first single binary) completes when this epic + Compose Desktop port of mobile UI both land

## Related

- lcp-59c (decision) — embed Letta Code on mobile; this epic is the desktop sibling
- multiplatform_roadmap.md Phase 3 — Windows-first desktop; this epic is what makes it 'single binary nobody wants to deal with install this then that'
- letta-mobile-deol1 — Projects tree + Admin agent control surface; consumes the local shim once this ships
- letta-mobile-0t8vf — Provider provisioning UI; required for non-engineer onboarding
- letta_cloud_unification.md — workspace capability model; local install is just another workspace from the client's perspective
- lcp-2hf (closed) + letta-mobile-vlttr — WS keepalive + cursor protocol; the local-loopback case still uses the same contract for consistency
- product_north_star.md — free agent / paid rig split; this epic ships the free agent's runtime container

## Severity rationale

P2 epic — large scope but not blocking current work. The mobile-first path keeps shipping in parallel. This epic gates the moment the desktop story becomes 'an app you can ship to anyone' rather than 'an app you can run if you know how to install Node and edit config files.' Should be in flight no later than when letta-mobile-0t8vf is mid-flight; they ship together for the v1 desktop onboarding story to make sense.

title: Remote action dispatch: tap, scroll, text input from CLI
description:
Third slice. CLI can drive the app — tap a component by ID, scroll a list, type into a field. Closes the loop from observation to interaction.

## Wire shape (proposed)

```json
{
  "type": "ui_introspect",
  "op": "action",
  "request_id": "...",
  "action": {
    "kind": "tap" | "long_press" | "scroll" | "text_input" | "key",
    "target_id": "send-btn",
    "params": { "text": "hello", "dx": 0, "dy": -200 }
  }
}
```

Response includes the post-action snapshot so CLI doesn't need to follow up.

## Design

- Target by stable component ID (from snapshot/subscribe), NOT by screen coordinates — robust against layout shifts
- Use Compose's testTag + SemanticsActions where possible (onClick, scrollBy, setText)
- Fall back to coordinate-based dispatch only when the component has no semantic action
- Permission gate: actions require an explicit `--allow-drive` flag on the CLI side; shim refuses unconfirmed action frames from unknown CLI connections
- Audit: every action logged with request_id, device_id, CLI session id

## Risk

This is the dangerous one. Lets a remote CLI tap arbitrary buttons on a running phone. Auth/scope MUST be tight before this lands. Specifically:

- Bearer token must be the same scoped token the CLI used for snapshot/subscribe
- Probably gate behind a developer-mode flag on the device (not on by default in user builds)
- Confirm with Emmanuel before exposing in any non-dev build

## Acceptance

- `letta ui tap <id>`, `letta ui type <id> '<text>'`, `letta ui scroll <id> --dy -200` all work
- Actions are reflected in the next snapshot
- Dev-mode gate on the device prevents drive in non-dev builds
- Audit log retained on shim for debugging

title: Live tree subscription: stream deltas on recomposition
description:
Second slice. CLI subscribes; app streams ASCII tree deltas on each meaningful recomposition.

## Wire shape (proposed)

Subscribe:
```json
{ "type": "ui_introspect", "op": "subscribe", "subscription_id": "...", "throttle_ms": 100 }
```

Delta frames (server-initiated after subscribe):
```json
{
  "type": "ui_introspect_delta",
  "subscription_id": "...",
  "seq": 17,
  "screen_id": "ChatScreen",
  "changed": [{ "id": "send-btn", "state": ["disabled", "loading"] }],
  "full_tree": null
}
```

Unsubscribe:
```json
{ "type": "ui_introspect", "op": "unsubscribe", "subscription_id": "..." }
```

## Design

- Diff against last-sent snapshot; send full tree on screen change, deltas otherwise
- Throttle on the device side (default 100ms) to avoid flooding on heavy recomp
- Single subscription per CLI connection initially — fan-out is a later optimization
- Coalesce rapid changes within the throttle window

## Acceptance

- `letta ui watch [--device <id>]` streams live ASCII to terminal, repainting in place
- Subscription survives screen transitions (sends new full tree on screen_id change)
- Disconnect cleans up server-side subscription state
- Throttling prevents runaway frame rates during animations

title: Read-only ASCII snapshot: app→shim→CLI
description:
First slice. CLI requests current screen, app returns ASCII projection of the active Compose tree, shim relays.

## Wire shape (proposed)

CLI → shim → device:
```json
{ "type": "ui_introspect", "op": "snapshot", "request_id": "..." }
```

Device → shim → CLI:
```json
{
  "type": "ui_introspect_response",
  "request_id": "...",
  "screen_id": "ChatScreen",
  "tree": "ascii string",
  "components": [{ "id": "send-btn", "bounds": [120, 400, 200, 440], "state": ["enabled"] }]
}
```

## ASCII format requirements

- Window frame with screen title
- Component boundaries labeled (Card, Column, List, Button, Text, etc.)
- State annotations inline ([disabled], [loading], [selected])
- Live dimensions (list item counts, tab counts)
- Stable IDs so the renderer/agent can reference 'the send button in ChatScreen' deterministically

## Implementation notes

- Generated from the live Compose tree via SemanticsNode walk (not source analysis — would lose runtime state)
- Probably under SemanticsOwner.rootSemanticsNode or LocalView.current.semanticsOwner
- Read-only: NO side effects on the app

## Acceptance

- CLI command: `letta ui snapshot [--device <id>]` returns ASCII to stdout
- shim relays the request to the targeted device's WS connection
- App returns within 500ms on a quiet screen
- ASCII fits within a normal terminal width (80-120 cols) at the top level; deeper trees indent

title: ASCII UI introspection: remote-drive mobile app from CLI over shim WS
description:
Live ASCII projection of the Android Compose UI, surfaced through the admin-shim WS, driven from the new lcp CLI.

## Motivation

Meridian (and any agent reasoning about the mobile UI) currently has to infer screen state from source code. That's brittle and stale within a day. A live ASCII projection of the current Compose tree would let agents and humans reason deliberately about what the user actually sees before emitting A2UI surfaces or making layout changes.

## Architecture

- **Driver service** lives in admin-shim (already terminates mobile WS, has auth, sees all devices)
- **CLI binary** lives in letta-code-parallel (new CLI being built; right home for ad-hoc dev tooling)
- **Device hook** lives in letta-mobile android-compose, surfaced over the existing /shim/v1/mobile WS contract
- **Wire format** extends the WS protocol with ui_introspect envelope (subtypes: snapshot, action, subscribe)

Shim is the multiplexer — CLI dials shim, shim relays to the chosen device.

## Scope (split into sub-tickets)

1. Read-only ASCII snapshot (request/response, no streaming)
2. Subscription / live delta stream on recomposition
3. Remote action dispatch (tap, scroll, text input) for interactive driving

## Not in scope (yet)

- Multi-device fan-out beyond simple device picker
- Desktop host support (will reuse same protocol when Desktop shell lands)
